items.title: [RFC] Direct Mooncake Store event ingestion for shared KV-aware routing
items.body:
# RFC: Event-driven shared KV placement from Mooncake Store

Parent: #294 · Related: #414, #528, #426, #489, #554

## Summary

Add an opt-in **direct Mooncake Store event source** to the Router's placement view. The Router subscribes to the Store Master's object lifecycle stream, converts supported connector-specific object keys into verified shared-cache placement, and combines that evidence with existing worker-local placement and load when selecting a target. The Router does not store or move KV tensors; the engine's connector performs the actual lookup and transfer.

This is a design proposal, not an implemented capability. It is an alternative or complement to the Conductor-backed provider in #414 / #528: both answer placement queries, but this design consumes Store events inside each Router. Reuse the placement/provider contract and existing scoring where appropriate; do not double-credit one physical copy when multiple sources describe it. The default deployment and routing behavior remain unchanged.

The first delivery targets a **version-pinned, validated vLLM MooncakeStoreConnector layout and full-attention model**. Do not credit unsupported key layouts, ambiguous connector events, or hybrid cache groups. The current Store stream supports shadow observations but does not, by itself, satisfy #294's active-credit freshness requirements. Active routing is gated on the trust and validation requirements below.

## Motivation

Consider two compatible workers attached to the same shared pool. W0 has the first 32 tokens on its GPU; the Store has a complete, connector-readable copy through token 64. A 65-token request can potentially reuse W0's GPU prefix and fetch the remaining Store-backed portion. W1 may also read the shared copy if it has the same verified pool and connector capability. The pool owns the shared copy; neither the publishing worker nor `medium=CPU` proves that W0 alone owns it.

The Router already indexes worker events and has a cache-owner concept, but the current `CacheOwner` also carries a source/rank and its `target()` resolves to a worker. That representation alone is not proof that other targets can fetch from a shared pool. Store object events also differ from engine block events: the master publishes raw object keys, not token IDs or a reproducible block-hash chain. We need an explicit pool owner, a verified access relation, a connector-specific key codec, and loss-aware source state.

## Architecture

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  E["vLLM workers"] -->|"engine KV events"| EI["existing local placement"]
  E -->|"connector put/get"| S["Mooncake Store"]
  S -->|"Master: stored / removed / cleared"| SUB["Store event subscriber"]
  SUB --> DEC["wire decoder + key/layout adapter"]
  DEC --> P["pool-scoped object presence + trust"]
  CAP["verified target ↔ pool capability"] --> Q["placement query / merge"]
  EI --> Q
  P --> Q
  REQ["request tokens + cache identity"] --> Q
  Q --> SCORE["kv_aware: compatible reuse + load"]
  SCORE --> E
```

The Store adapter is an event source for the #294 placement model, not a second authority for worker health or cache transfers. Its physical-object presence is evidence for proving a logical cache record complete; it must not become an independent competing residency authority. First adapt the existing index, and align logical record ownership with #489's proposed unified authoritative record model as that work lands. The subscriber runs asynchronously. The request path reads a bounded in-memory snapshot; it must not wait for replay, reconciliation, a Store RPC, or an actual cache transfer. All configuration names and types below describe proposed contracts, not existing flags or stable APIs.

### Separate identity, ownership and access

Conceptually keep the following distinct:

```text
PoolId          = configured Store backend / isolation domain
CacheIdentity   = tenant + model/weights + adapter + salt + verified hash/layout profile
ObjectKey       = raw connector-produced Store key
SharedCopy      = (PoolId, CacheIdentity, ObjectKey, medium)
ExecutionTarget = (instance_id, dp_rank, incarnation)
AccessContract  = target → pool + connector/version + compatible identity and layout
```

The Store's `group_id` groups objects and is **not** automatically a vLLM hybrid KV `group_idx`. A pool is not a worker. A worker restart or worker clear removes only that worker's local state and access binding; it must not clear the shared pool. A Store removal or clear retracts only the matching pool/tenant/medium scope, not independent GPU/host copies. Events from an engine connector and the Store may describe the same underlying copy; define a single authoritative source per copy, or deduplicate it, before assigning credit. If source/ownership cannot be distinguished, withhold the affected local/shared credit or remain in shadow mode; never infer local versus shared solely from `CPU` or `STORAGE`.

An access binding is a verified operator/worker capability, not an assumption that every registered target can read every pool. At minimum it identifies pool, tenant, model/weights, adapter/salt rules, compatible connector and layout, TP/PP/PCP/DCP arrangement and relevant block/chunk geometry. It is invalidated on worker replacement, config/connector change or pool binding change. Health, worker role and capacity are filtered separately. A missing or mismatched binding gives that target no shared-pool credit.

### Event protocol and object mapping

For the documented Store publisher, accept the ZMQ multipart frames `[topic, sequence, msgpack payload]`, where sequence is unsigned big-endian and the payload carries a timestamp, an array of events, and rank metadata. Iterate the full batch; validate frame sequence and stream-level `event_id` ordering according to the publisher contract. The envelope's `dp_rank` alone does not identify the shared owner or an eligible execution target. Store events contain `event_type` (`stored`, `removed`, `cleared`), `backend_id`, `tenant_id`, and for object events an `object_key`, `medium`, and possibly `group_id`. `cpu` and `disk` identify Store media; `disk` can represent several non-memory backends, not necessarily a worker's local disk. The Store does not decode its keys: its `seq_hashes` / legacy `block_hashes` are empty and `token_ids`, `parent_hash` and `base_block_idx` are nil. Legacy `type` tags do not change those semantics. See the [Mooncake subscriber guide](https://kvcache-ai.github.io/Mooncake/design/conductor/subscriber-guide.html).

Require object-key publication. Validate framing, sequence, event and field sizes, backend/tenant scope, known media and supported key grammar. Unknown versions, keys, or missing/contradictory metadata provide no placement credit. An undecodable or ambiguous removal/clear must revoke the affected source scope; if the scope cannot be proven, invalidate every scope on that publisher. Silently discarding a possible retraction can leave a stale positive. Limit batches, key length, object count and memory; on capacity overflow invalidate the affected source's credit rather than silently retaining a misleading partial view. Do not expose raw prompt tokens, raw object keys, tenant identifiers or salts as metric labels or in normal logs.

Use a versioned `StoreKeyCodec` for a **verified producer and layout**, with golden vectors generated by the real connector, not heuristic parsing of an arbitrary key. For a request, reproduce the connector's chained chunk keys from the exact prepared tokens and identity; account for connector retrieval granularity, chunk boundaries, group, namespace and all required TP/PP/PCP/DCP objects. If multimodal inputs, prompt embeddings, per-block extra keys or any other engine hash input cannot be reproduced exactly, v1 gives that request no shared credit. One object event is not necessarily one complete reusable KV chunk. A logical chunk is available at a given medium only when every object required by the target's access contract is known available; removing any required object revokes that proof. If the connector uses a different grammar, hash seed, granularity or object set, it is unsupported until independently verified. In particular, do not reuse Dynamo's SGLang HiCache key codec for vLLM by assumption.

Model presence as an idempotent set of `(pool, tenant, object_key, medium)`, not event-count-based replica reference counting: duplicate `stored`/`removed` events must not fabricate or underflow copies. A `removed` retracts only its medium; `cleared` retracts the Store-defined `backend_id + tenant_id` scope. An upsert's remove followed by store must be applied in stream order. Store object groups may optimize checks only when their completeness semantics are verified; otherwise verify every required key.

### Query and scoring contract

Extend the existing read-only placement/provider boundary only as needed to carry the prepared token IDs, cache identity, eligible target and access capability. `MatchQuery`'s router-local block hashes and today's `CacheKey` alone are insufficient to reproduce Store connector keys or establish tenant/layout compatibility. Reuse existing local `KvBlockIndexer`; the pool observation can be implemented as an adapter to the unified placement model, not as an obligation to replace the radix tree.

For each eligible target, derive ordered, aligned logical chunks with the target's verified codec, consult the current pool snapshot, and combine only contiguous, restorable evidence with that target's local tier segments. Never sum overlapping local and shared copies. Bound the candidate prefix by the request and engine's recomputation/alignment rules, including the last-token/logits constraint where applicable. Bound prompt tokens/chunks, eligible targets and pools, per-chunk object fanout, CPU work and query time; reuse derivations among targets with identical verified layouts. An exceeded budget withholds shared credit and preserves independent local scoring. Apply each batch atomically with its source progress and use a source-generation fence or equivalent so a query cannot combine an invalidated generation with a newer multi-object snapshot. A failed lookup, unsupported profile, stale pool, incomplete objects or unverified access yields **no shared credit**, not a fabricated hit or a routing error. Actual engine/connector lookup remains authoritative at execution time; an event-derived hit is a routing estimate, not a read lease or guaranteed hit.

The current scorer supports a device prefix plus a non-device continuation; it should not be assumed to implement arbitrary multi-tier stitching. For v1, preserve existing scoring semantics and admit shared continuation only when representable without double credit. If multiple successive or overlapping host/shared/disk segments are needed, specify and test a separate deterministic per-interval merge and tier-cost rule before enabling it. Tier discounts are configurable estimates, not measured transfer latency. Preserve healthy-worker filtering, load, admission and existing fallback even if the shared source fails.

### Example

```text
Request: 65 tokens; hypothetical block boundary: 16 tokens
W0/rank0 GPU:         [0................32)
Pool memory:          [0................................64)
Verified W0 → pool:    yes
Verified W1 → pool:    no

W0 candidate evidence: GPU [0,32) + shared continuation [32,64)
W1 candidate evidence: no shared credit (no verified access contract)
```

This is an illustrative placement calculation, not a measured hit. If any object needed for the shared continuation is removed, that portion loses credit. A concurrent eviction or transfer failure can still make the engine miss after a routing decision.

## Freshness and failure semantics

The documented Store Master stream has no startup snapshot and no replay. A new subscriber cannot know about objects stored before it joined. A gap, disconnect, publisher reset/sequence rollback, bounded queue overflow, source replacement, unknown generation or corrupt batch can hide removals. Sequence is scoped to the publisher stream: invalidate all scopes carried by that stream unless the protocol proves a narrower affected scope, while preserving independent worker sources and other publishers. Do not claim `EXACT` or automatically restore full trust merely because a socket reconnects, a timeout elapses, or a new `stored` event arrives.

Use explicit source states such as `UNINITIALIZED`, `PARTIAL`, `READY`, and `STALE`. `PARTIAL` means observations are incomplete and may be stale during transport uncertainty; an unobserved object is unknown, not a trusted miss. Under #294, this source remains **shadow-only** until a valid freshness contract is established: partial observations must not change active cache credit. Silence alone is not evidence of disconnection or freshness when the producer has no heartbeat; TTL and connection health do not prove correctness or replace retractions. An approximate active-scoring mode, if desired, is a separate future proposal requiring an explicit change to #294 and its acceptance criteria.

An `EXACT`-eligible full view requires an authoritative baseline with a publisher epoch and event watermark plus buffered, ordered handoff, or another explicitly verified equivalent. A plain key scan without a matching watermark is not a consistent snapshot. Per-key/batch probes, if added later, are point-in-time checks rather than leases; define their cost, timeout, error semantics and supported tier separately. A `cleared` event is a barrier only for its documented backend+tenant scope and only if subsequent continuity is established. If the producer cannot supply these guarantees, keep this source partial/shadow or use a provider with the needed recovery contract.

## Hybrid models and multimedium boundaries

V1 does not grant shared-pool credit to a hybrid model merely because one attention group's Store objects exist. Correct credit requires each required group to have authoritative lifecycle evidence and its own restoration rules, plus a common same-target boundary as in #489 / #512–#517 and #554 where applicable. Checkpoint positions, sliding windows, compression, partial pages, group dependencies, and tier/connector capabilities all need an engine-validated contract. A missing group is `unknown`, not a dense-only hit. V1 excludes these cases until tests prove them.

## Configuration and operability

Initially disable the feature by default. A deployment would explicitly configure Store endpoint, pool/backend and tenant, supported producer/codec version and layout, target-to-pool access mapping, memory limits, shadow mode, and (only when active-credit gates are met) applicable tier weights. Reject incompatible or incomplete configuration. Respect existing security/authorization controls; a pool event or a matching hash alone never grants a worker access to a tenant's cached data.

Mooncake needs event publishing enabled in its build and runtime; `kv_events_emit_object_key=false` suppresses per-object events. Monitor source state, last accepted sequence/age, gaps/restarts, dropped/invalid events, codec failures, observed object count, capacity invalidations, eligible/ineligible targets, shared-credit tokens and lookup latency. Use low-cardinality labels only. Store's `/kv_events/status` is useful for diagnostics but does not by itself establish a consistent snapshot or delivery completeness.

## Delivery and validation

1. **Contract and shadow ingestion:** versioned event decoder, bounded per-pool presence and state machine; expose metrics only. Pin and document exact vLLM/Mooncake versions and supported single-group layout.
2. **Identity and codec:** golden vectors from real connector keys for namespace, hash, chunk and all physical shards; negative fixtures for unsupported versions and incomplete objects. Verify pool/target bindings and avoid engine-connector/Store double attribution.
3. **Query and scoring:** integrate the local read-only placement port and one representable non-device continuation, preserving existing behavior when disabled; distinguish unknown, trusted miss and a shadow-only observed hit. Do not activate shared credit before the recovery gate below.
4. **Acceptance:** run deterministic tests for duplicate/upsert/medium removal/clear, late join, gap, reset, disconnect, queue/cap overflow, isolation between pools and local owners, tenant/LoRA/salt mismatch, inaccessible worker, partial object set, alignment, overlapping tiers and hybrid fail-closed. Compare Router predictions against actual engine-confirmed reuse under a real vLLM + Mooncake Store deployment, including warm Store before subscription, evictions and transport failure. Report false-positive and missed credits, TTFT, compute/transfer cost, CPU, memory and p95/p99 Router latency; no performance claim is assumed here.
5. **Recovery and expansion:** add only with an authoritative snapshot/watermark or equivalent contract; separately design multi-tier stitching, hybrid groups and additional connector key layouts.

## Alternatives and open questions

- **Conductor provider (#414 / #528):** centralizes event consumption and supports multiple Routers and engine types. Direct subscription avoids a per-request remote provider call and a separate index service, but multiplies event connections and state per Router replica. Compare deployment cost, latency, availability, consistency and recovery on matched workloads.
- **Engine-published shared-store residency:** [vLLM #58520](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58520) explores publishing complete block residency via the engine stream. That may avoid object-key coupling; confirm removal, ownership, completeness and retrieval semantics before choosing it as the sole source. Coordinate with [vLLM #65548](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/65548) on source identity and locality.
- **On-demand Store probes:** simpler residency checks but put remote I/O and timeout pressure on the path unless prefetched; probes do not themselves reserve data. Keep off the request path in v1.
- **Open:** Which connector versions and hash roots can be discovered authoritatively? Can the Store expose a snapshot with epoch/watermark? How is pool access capability attested and revoked? What is the supported source-authority rule during migration? What bounded-staleness policy is acceptable for opt-in hints?

labels.name: cursor
labels.description: Task for a Cursor background agent

items.body:
Plan: docs/cursor/Z-zenas-plan.md — read the whole plan (Non-negotiables apply to every phase) and AGENTS.md first.
One phase = one branch (cursor/<id>-<slug>) = one PR. Never push to main. Stop after the PR; Claude reviews before merge.

- `agents/zenas/pool/`: one adapter per source → common document model `{id, jurisdiction, level federal|state|national|provincial|international, body, kind statute|regulation|case|court_rule|treaty|form|guidance, citation, title, date, effective_from, effective_to, status, url, licence, text, sections[]}`. Keep every version (laws change; answers must be "as at" a date).
- Chunk by structure (section, subsection, paragraph), never by blind length. Store in Postgres (text + metadata + full-text index) and Qdrant collection `law_<jurisdiction>` (shared knowledge, not per tenant). Embeddings computed locally (C7's embedding service; a legal-tuned open model may replace it later).
- US sources, first wave (check and record each licence before ingesting):
  - US Code and CFR via govinfo.gov / eCFR APIs; Federal Register for changes.
  - Trade/shipping: 19 CFR (customs), HTSUS (USITC), EAR 15 CFR 730–774, ITAR 22 CFR 120–130, OFAC 31 CFR 500s, COGSA (46 USC 30701 note), Carmack (49 USC 14706).
  - International: CISG and UNCITRAL texts (UN, public).
  - Case law: CourtListener (Free Law Project) API, starting with federal appellate + Delaware/New York commercial decisions; Caselaw Access Project bulk data for history.
  - Court rules: Federal Rules of Civil Procedure and Evidence; local rules of the districts the panel practises in.
  - State law: start with Delaware (DGCL), New York and Texas commercial statutes as enacted; UCC Articles 1, 2, 9 as enacted by those states.
- A nightly update job per source; a `pool_status` endpoint (source, documents, last update, licence).
- **Done when:** the federal titles above and the first state statutes are searchable by citation and by meaning, with version dates; a re-run adds new versions without duplicating.

items.title: Scale: review what Grounded needs, measuring first (after v0.5.0)
items.body:
**Requested by the owner (2026-10-14): after v0.5.0, review what Grounded needs to scale, the way open-model-gateway just did.**

## How OMG did it (read as a template: `docs/roadmap.md`, `docs/governance.md`, its v0.4.0 and v0.5.0 release commits)
1. **A stated target** (tens of thousands of users, workspaces and keys, horizontally scaled replicas) and a **design document** naming the bottlenecks.
2. **P0, measure before fixing:** latency histograms for the hot paths, a mock upstream, an open-loop load generator and a seeder, and a multi-replica stack with PgBouncer.
3. **Fixes in phases, each landed with its numbers** (there: lock-free reads, scoped admission instead of one global lock, per-replica caches with change notifications, leased background work, partitions and rollups for history).
4. **Cluster capacity runs** from a purpose-built load-test image, and **HA runs under failure** (pooler restart, failover under load), written up.
5. Issues for each step, one branch and PR per issue, a plan file.

## Proposed shape for Grounded
- **Needs from the owner first:** the scale target (users, teams, knowledge bases, documents and passages, concurrent chats, answers per minute, ingestion volume) and what is acceptable (latency, availability). Without it we would optimise blind.
- **P0 measurement.** Already there: 78 `grounded_*` metrics and traces in the cluster's Mimir and Tempo. To add: a seeder (N teams, knowledge bases, documents, passages), an open-loop load generator for search, chat and ingestion, the fake gateway as the upstream (it exists for `--demo`), and a multi-replica stack on the cluster.
- **Review by subsystem, to find the bottlenecks (not assumed):** the vector tables (one `emb_<profile>` table each, HNSW, F2 partitioning), retrieval and rerank, the River job queues (ingest, embedding sets, evaluations, crawls), the crawler, SystemOne capacity slots, the answer cache, Valkey rate limits, usage-ledger writes and rollups, sessions and auth, the audit log, evaluation runs, Postgres sizing, backups and restore time at size.
- **Then** issues per finding, fixes in phases each with before and after numbers, a capacity run and failover run on the cluster, and a scale section in the operations docs.

Not started. It follows v0.5.0 (the index preview and the rest of the release) and needs the targets above.

items.title: [Feature] Ingest externally-measured usage into virtual-key spend tracking (async batch traffic bypassing the proxy)

labels.name: Cost & Budgeting
labels.description: Wrong or missing spend/cost, pricing and cost-map rows, budgets and spend limits

items.body:
**Context**
We rely on LiteLLM virtual keys for auth, budgets, and spend attribution across our platform. Some inference traffic goes through the LiteLLM proxy as usual, but we also run an asynchronous batch path (OpenAI Batch API style, built on `llm-d-batch-gateway`): users upload JSONL files with thousands of requests, and a batch processor dispatches each line directly to model gateway / inference-pool endpoints.

This direct path bypasses the LiteLLM proxy **on purpose**: sustained batch throughput would make the proxy a bottleneck, and batch calls don't need proxy-time features (retry/fallback routing, per-request guardrail decisions).

**The gap**
- Usage data exists: batch output rows carry per-request `usage` (prompt/completion tokens), and key/tenant identity is propagated from job submission through the batch pipeline.
- Spend for this traffic never lands in LiteLLM's spend tables, because spend is only written by the proxy logging pipeline for requests that pass through it.
- We checked current master (`spend_management_endpoints.py`): spend endpoints are read/report-only (`/spend/calculate`, `/global/spend/reset|refresh`) — there is no supported way for an external system to record usage against a virtual key/team.

**Questions / proposal**
1. Is there a recommended pattern today for attributing usage of non-proxied traffic to virtual keys (short of writing `LiteLLM_SpendLogs` rows directly, which we'd rather not depend on)?
2. If not, would you accept a contribution adding an ingestion entry point (endpoint or documented internal API) that accepts externally-measured usage — key, model, tokens, timestamp, metadata — and feeds it through the same spend-update pipeline (key/team/user spend logs, budget accounting)? Happy to implement and upstream it in whatever shape maintainers prefer.

The broader goal: keep budgets/spend coherent in LiteLLM as the single metering system, even in deployments where part of the traffic legitimately bypasses the proxy.

items.title: [Bug]: Embedding ingestion needs rate pacing; 429 retries replay the whole document
items.body:
### Affected Component

Model Service

### Bug Description

When importing a document with many chunks through an OpenAI-compatible embedding provider, WeKnora can exceed the provider account RPM/TPM limit even when model concurrency is configured conservatively.

This is not only a provider quota issue: the current ingestion path limits in-flight concurrency, but does not pace request rate. After a partial batch failure, the outer retry calls `BatchEmbedWithPool` again with the entire document, so already successful sub-batches are sent again. This creates a retry amplification loop and turns a recoverable 429 into a document-level failure.

Relevant code paths in v0.7.0:
- `internal/models/embedding/batch.go`: splits the document into sub-batches and submits all of them to the worker pool.
- `internal/application/service/retriever/keywords_vector_hybrid_indexer.go`: `batchEmbedWithBackoff` retries the complete `contentList`.
- `internal/models/embedding/openai.go`: HTTP responses such as 429 are returned without honoring `Retry-After`.

### Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a generic OpenAI-compatible embedding model backed by a provider/account with an RPM or TPM limit.
2. Set conservative concurrency values, for example:
   - `BATCH_EMBED_SIZE=10`
   - `WEKNORA_MODEL_MAX_CONCURRENCY=2`
   - `CONCURRENCY_POOL_SIZE=5`
3. Create a knowledge base and upload a Markdown document that produces about 700 chunks. Question generation can be enabled, which adds more embedding traffic, but the initial document embedding is sufficient to reproduce.
4. Observe the app logs and document status.

With 712 chunks and batch size 10, the document still creates about 72 provider requests. A concurrency cap of 2 limits simultaneous requests, but fast responses can still send those requests within a short time and exceed RPM/TPM.

### Expected Behavior

Large documents should be processed slowly but eventually succeed when the provider returns a transient 429.

Suggested behavior:
- Apply configurable request-rate/token-rate pacing in addition to concurrency limiting.
- Honor the provider's `Retry-After` header when present.
- Retry only failed sub-batches, preserving successful results.
- Use jittered backoff and avoid retrying the complete document from the beginning.
- Expose a production configuration for the rate limit without requiring source modifications.

### Actual Behavior

The provider returns `429 AccountRateLimitExceeded`. The document fails after several rapid whole-document attempts instead of slowing down.

In one reproducible run on August 5, 2026 at 09:32 CST:
- Document size: 712 chunks
- Configured model concurrency: 2
- Batch size: 10
- Five outer document-level attempts occurred in roughly 12 seconds
- Multiple 429 responses occurred during each round
- The final document status was parse/embedding failure

Historical comparison on the same deployment: documents up to 183 chunks had succeeded. Failures became strongly correlated with larger chunk counts (minimum observed failed document: 117 chunks; median: 383; maximum: 1023). This indicates sustained request volume rather than malformed Markdown content.

### WeKnora Version

App Version: v0.7.0, UI Version: v0.7.0, official Docker images, revision e8dcbb07d09db88894601b564ebabe21dda6830d

### Deployment Method

Docker Compose

### Operating System

Windows 10 Enterprise 22H2 (build 19045), Docker Compose

### Relevant Logs

```shell
BatchEmbedWithPool attempt 1/5 failed: ... 429 ... AccountRateLimitExceeded
BatchEmbedWithPool attempt 2/5 failed: ... 429 ... AccountRateLimitExceeded
BatchEmbedWithPool attempt 3/5 failed: ... 429 ... AccountRateLimitExceeded
BatchEmbedWithPool attempt 4/5 failed: ... 429 ... AccountRateLimitExceeded
BatchEmbedWithPool attempt 5/5 failed: ... 429 ... AccountRateLimitExceeded


Provider credentials, endpoint details, and document names have been intentionally omitted.
```

### Confirmation

- [x] I have searched existing issues and confirmed this is a new one

items.title: Built-in PII redactor + learnable detect_pii switch for the storage redaction hook
items.body:
## Context

`Storage(redact=...)` is the right boundary for HIPAA/PII/export-controlled workloads — it runs a pre-write transform on every `ClassificationRecord` before it touches disk or the sync queue. But every adopter must hand-write the redactor.

This matters most for **shared / cross-tenant learned switches**: when many customers' inputs pool into one model (e.g. document categorization, where the taxonomy is universal and a shared model gives new customers zero cold-start), a missing or weak redactor becomes a data-governance leak — one tenant's PII can end up in the features that serve another tenant.

Real adopter context: we run a cross-tenant `classify_library_category` switch (ag-document categorization). We currently mitigate by limiting features to non-sensitive document-name signals, but we'd rather delegate to a first-class Postrule redactor at the storage boundary.

## Ask

1. **Batteries-included redactor.** Ship `redactors.regex_pii()` (emails, phones, SSNs, lat/long coordinates, dictionary names) usable directly as `Storage(redact=...)`.
2. **PII detection as a first-class `detect_pii` learned switch.** Seed with regex / an LLM judge, accumulate verdicts, graduate an ML head via `LearnedSwitch` — so `redact` can delegate to a model that *improves* with use. This dogfoods Postrule on its own ingestion path (Postrule scrubbing the data that trains Postrule).
3. **Docs for shared cross-tenant switches.** Document redact-before-persist as a hard requirement for any switch keyed by author (no account dimension), with a feature-allowlist helper.

## Why it's a fit

Postrule already has `LearnedSwitch`, the universal classifier, and judge committees — everything needed to make PII detection itself a switch. The redaction hook is the perfect place to consume it.

items.title: [Audit][Roadmap] Ragbot platform architecture audit and prioritized execution plan
items.body:
## Executive summary

Audit baseline: `main` at the September 2026 architecture after durable worker reliability, staged knowledge generations, parser/chunker ports, Golden Dataset and parser/PDF benchmark work.

Ragbot is already beyond a prototype RAG application. Its strongest current properties are:

- PostgreSQL-backed durable ingestion queue with lease/heartbeat/retry/DLQ/reconciliation
- staged source knowledge generations with PostgreSQL activation authority and durable Qdrant cleanup
- dense Qdrant + PostgreSQL CJK-aware lexical hybrid retrieval + RRF + reranking
- Parser/Chunker ports and promotion benchmarks
- multi-tenant ACL/RBAC enforcement
- SaaS/local/object-source ingestion coverage
- Prometheus/OpenTelemetry plus quality benchmark infrastructure
- OpenAI-shaped compatibility API and a preliminary Node client

The next architecture risk is **integration growth without stable platform contracts**. Current factories and ingestion dispatch still branch on implementation/source names; model routing is not wired as the production composition boundary; embeddings are synchronous; vector index schema has no first-class lifecycle; persistence has a legacy inheritance stack/fat repository; and the SDK/identity/object-storage surfaces are not yet at the same maturity as the ingestion core.

The recommendation is therefore **not** to add dozens of providers/connectors/vector databases immediately. First establish stable extension and index contracts, then expand implementations behind them.

---

## Priority 0 — platform correctness and evolvability

### #50 Platform registry / typed runtime profiles
Make connector/model/embedding/vector/upload implementations resolvable behind one stable registry and shared config/capability schemas.

### #51 LLM provider/router plane
Wire capability-aware model routing into production; remove global environment mutation; add OpenAI/Anthropic/Gemini/Azure/Bedrock/Ollama adapters behind one contract.

### #52 Embedding plane
Replace synchronous embedding transport with bounded async batching/retry/rate-limit handling and a complete embedding contract identity.

### #53 Vector index lifecycle
Introduce versioned indexes, shadow validation, Qdrant alias activation and rollback for embedding/vector-schema upgrades.

### P0 exit criteria

- adding a provider/connector no longer requires editing core dispatch switches
- model and embedding clients use pooled bounded transports with explicit capabilities
- every indexed chunk can be associated with an immutable embedding/index contract
- incompatible embedding changes build a new index and support atomic cutover/rollback
- current production paths remain regression-compatible

Do not start broad provider/connector expansion before these boundaries are stable.

---

## Priority 1 — production platform surface

### #54 Connector SDK
Standardize snapshot/incremental/checkpoint/deletion/ACL/rate-limit semantics and then validate with SharePoint/OneDrive, Azure/GCS, Slack/Teams or other new connectors.

### #55 Storage architecture
Split the monolithic `Repo`, retire the `postgres_repo -> pg_repo -> managed_pg_repo` inheritance stack and clarify transaction/capability boundaries.

### #56 PostgreSQL performance gates
Keyset pagination, SQL-side filtering, COPY/staging batch paths, queue claim/reconciliation hot-path cleanup, pool/timeouts and query-plan benchmarks.

### #57 Retrieval engine
Move hybrid retrieval to a reusable async/composable pipeline. Keep current hybrid RRF as control, then benchmark Qdrant dense+sparse, alternate fusion, MMR and multi-vector plans.

### #58 Public API / SDK / MCP
Freeze versioned knowledge/search contracts, add maintained Python+Node SDKs, typed retry/error/pagination/stream semantics and a scoped MCP/tool surface.

### #59 Upload object storage
Keep `UploadStore`, add S3/MinIO first and then Azure Blob/GCS, including direct upload and lifecycle/GC semantics.

### #60 Enterprise identity/security
Add OIDC/JWT, service accounts, hashed/rotatable API keys and unified SecretResolver backends while preserving Ragbot RBAC/ACL as authorization truth.

### #61 Durable quality/observability
Tie production requests and evaluation runs to parser/chunker/embedding/index/retrieval/reranker/model contract IDs; use benchmark evidence as promotion gates.

### P1 exit criteria

- platform can horizontally scale API/workers without shared upload PVC
- source catalog/job APIs remain bounded at large cardinality
- retrieval has deadline/cancellation and measurable stage-level latency
- Python and Node consumers have supported, versioned SDKs
- operators can identify exactly which data/model/index contracts produced a response
- identity/secrets no longer depend on one static plaintext API-key mapping pattern

---

## Priority 2 — controlled capability expansion

### #62 Multimodal RAG
Preserve tables/images/layout and visual citations in the normalized document/index contracts, benchmarked against the text-only baseline.

### #63 Release governance
Remove roadmap drift, lock/constraint CI/runtime dependencies, add SBOM/security/compatibility checks and mechanically validate capability/version documentation.

P2 can be partially parallelized, but multimodal indexing should wait for #52/#53 and object artifacts should build on #59.

---

## Dependency graph / recommended order

1. **Foundation:** #50
2. In parallel after the foundation shape is agreed: **#51, #52, #55**
3. Build **#53** on the embedding/index contract from #52
4. Run database operational work **#56** alongside storage consolidation, but do not delay obvious pagination/hot-path regressions
5. Use the registry in **#54 and #59** rather than adding new branches
6. Refactor retrieval in **#57** after the embedding/index interfaces are stable; preserve the current RRF path as the benchmark control
7. Productize **#58** over stable public contracts rather than exposing internal service objects
8. Implement **#61** across all preceding work so promotion decisions become evidence-based
9. Harden enterprise identity with **#60** before positioning Ragbot as a multi-tenant shared service
10. Add **#62** multimodal representations only after index/artifact lifecycle is explicit
11. **#63** begins immediately and stays cross-cutting

---

## Architectural principles to freeze

1. PostgreSQL is the authoritative control-plane/system-of-record store; Qdrant is a derived vector index.
2. Source publication and vector-index publication are different lifecycles; both require atomic activation/rollback semantics.
3. Product semantics/config schemas live in stable handwritten contracts; vendor adapters sit behind them.
4. Connectors emit normalized source changes; parsers emit normalized document blocks; chunkers emit chunks; embedding/index stages do not reach back into vendor connectors.
5. Tenant/ACL filtering happens before evidence is returned, not as a post-generation cleanup.
6. New retrieval/vector techniques are promoted by Golden Dataset + latency/cost evidence, not by feature novelty.
7. Public API/SDK contracts are smaller and more stable than internal service classes.
8. Production network clients use pooled transports, bounded concurrency, explicit deadlines, retries and structured errors.
9. Secrets and identity are references/claims, not arbitrary plaintext configuration fields.
10. Runtime capabilities and release documentation should be machine-verifiable.

---

## Industry baseline used for the audit

- LangChain: common provider/document-loader/vector-store interfaces and separately packaged integrations
- Haystack: composable pipeline components + distinct Document Store abstractions
- Unstructured: source/destination connector architecture, optional connector packages and configurable ingestion stages
- Qdrant: dense+sparse/named vectors, multi-stage Query API and atomic collection aliases for vector-version cutover
- Weaviate / Azure AI Search: explicit hybrid fusion + reranking stages and multi-tenant/filter-aware retrieval
- Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases: decoupled Retrieve vs RetrieveAndGenerate, metadata filtering, reranking, structured/multimodal knowledge paths and retrieval traces
- Vercel AI SDK: provider registries/capability normalization
- OpenAI / Anthropic SDKs: typed streaming/errors, configurable timeout/retry and provider transport concerns kept out of application logic

This audit intentionally treats these products as architectural references, not dependencies to copy wholesale.

---

## Overall target state

Ragbot should converge from a feature-rich RAG service into a **versioned Knowledge Retrieval Platform** with five explicit planes:

1. **Connector/Ingestion plane** — durable source sync, parsing/chunking, generation publication
2. **Index plane** — embedding contracts, vector/sparse indexes, version/cutover/rollback
3. **Retrieval plane** — filters, candidate retrieval, fusion, rerank, evidence/citations
4. **Model/Agent plane** — provider registry, capability routing, bounded tool/model execution
5. **Control/Developer plane** — PostgreSQL metadata/jobs/evals, identity/RBAC, observability, SDK/MCP/admin

The existing code already contains many of these concepts; the next milestone is to make the boundaries explicit enough that new integrations can grow without destabilizing the core.

items.body:

# XIV AI GLOBAL OFFLINE SUPER BRAIN — MASTER CURSOR EXECUTION PROMPT — 62L-DC

## Mission
Continue GLOBAL OPERATIONS BRAIN as the XIV Superbrain root by building the SUPERBRAIN SERVICE FABRIC, AGENT DEPARTMENT API MESH, DISTRIBUTED MEMORY LAKE STREAMING, MODEL BROKER & EVALUATION GRID, ADAPTIVE ACCELERATOR FEDERATION, AUTONOMOUS AI PRODUCT STUDIO NETWORK, and MULTI-UNIVERSE STATE COMPILER & DISASTER RECOVERY FABRIC.

This phase should evolve the distributed runtime mesh into a service-oriented operating fabric that can expose bounded department capabilities through explicit APIs, stream approved memory/knowledge/experiment products into a distributed lake, broker local/cloud model work under policy, evaluate model quality continuously, federate verified heterogeneous compute, operate multiple isolated AI product studios in sandbox, and compile signed/revocable Universe state packages with recovery plans for authorized nodes and storage tiers.

Interpretation rules:
- 'Superbrain Service Fabric' = application-layer service registry, routing, policy, health, state and evidence contracts; not consciousness/sentience.
- 'Department API Mesh' = explicit typed APIs for bounded department capabilities with authz, tenancy, classification, quotas, rate limits, timeouts and evidence; API availability never grants authority.
- 'Distributed Memory Lake Streaming' = lawful signed movement of approved derived memory/knowledge/experiment objects among explicitly enrolled local/edge/cloud storage and indexes; no raw private global pooling.
- 'Model Broker' = local-first policy router among configured/evidenced model providers with data-class firewalls, fallbacks and budgets; unknown providers stay UNAVAILABLE.
- 'Evaluation Grid' = reproducible task-specific evals, evidence traceability, calibration, safety, latency, cost/resource proxies and regression tracking; agreement is not proof.
- 'Adaptive Accelerator Federation' = compatibility and candidate scheduling across VERIFIED CPU/AMD/NVIDIA/NPU/simulator/QPU targets; no arbitrary hardware discovery/control or spending.
- 'AI Product Studio Network' = bounded product/architect/coder/tester/security/evidence workcells creating sandbox tools/plugins/services/apps with reuse-first and human promotion gates.
- 'State Compiler' = compiles approved checkpoints, indexes, skills, models, policy-safe metadata and derived knowledge into signed/versioned destination-scoped state packages; no unrestricted database copies.
- 'Disaster Recovery Fabric' = recovery simulation, integrity checking, checkpoint selection, compatibility planning, revocation and rollback for authorized infrastructure only; recovery candidate != production failover authorization.

Target cycle:
AUTHORIZED OBJECTIVE -> TENANT/UNIVERSE/CLASSIFICATION/POLICY CHECK -> SERVICE/API PLAN -> SOURCE/DATA/TOOL RIGHTS CHECK -> LOCAL-FIRST MODEL/COMPUTE PLAN -> BOUNDED SERVICE/STUDIO EXECUTION -> SIGNED MEMORY/STATE/ARTIFACT -> STRUCTURED EVIDENCE/DISSENT -> TEST/SECURITY/EVAL/BENCHMARK/REPLICATION -> HUMAN/POLICY REVIEW -> VERIFIED_CANDIDATE -> SIGNED PACKAGE/ROUTE/RECOVERY CANDIDATE -> EXPLICIT AUTHORIZATION -> CHECKPOINT/SYNC CANDIDATE -> FOUNDER BRIEF.

## Mandatory Preflight
Read reports through 62L-DB and inspect the actual worktree/runtime. Reuse Distributed Runtime Mesh, Department Microservices, Memory Streaming Fabric, Multi-Provider Model Gateway, Accelerator Scheduler, Software R&D Company Network, Universe State Replication/Recovery, Superbrain Runtime Kernel, Local Brain, Agent Population, Provider Fabric, Accelerator Fabric, Quantum Research, Knowledge Graph/Lakehouse, Data Refinery, Plugin Runtime, Digital Genome, Workforce/Census Ledger, Homeostasis, Guardian/RLS and Offline Policy.

Before broad edits produce:
1. exact logical/materialized/registered/active/RUNNING_VERIFIED agent/workcell/service/API/node census from heartbeat/runtime evidence,
2. explicit enrolled-node and service/API topology with OS/architecture/power/connectivity/runtime/checkpoint truth states,
3. department API inventory with owner, authz scope, tenant/Universe/classification and consequence level,
4. distributed memory-lake/storage/index topology with provenance/freshness/retention/revocation states,
5. model broker/provider matrix with CONFIGURED/AUTHORIZED/EVIDENCED/AVAILABLE and task-eval states,
6. CPU/AMD/NVIDIA/NPU/quantum capability/benchmark matrix with DETECTED/SUPPORTED/VERIFIED separation,

## Governance
L4_AUTONOMY_ENABLED=false. No production deploy/merge/migrations, self-granted permissions, Guardian/RLS weakening, uncontrolled recursive agent/model/tool/product/service/genome replication, arbitrary internet/LAN/server/database/device discovery or scanning, interception, credential harvesting, offensive cyber, malware, stealth persistence, exfiltration, unauthorized scraping/data mining, leaked/stolen/restricted data ingestion, raw-private cross-tenant pooling, covert tracking, autonomous financial/legal commitments, autonomous external publishing, autonomous purchasing/cloud spend, unsafe physical/satellite/vehicle control, hidden chain-of-thought storage, consciousness/sentience claims, unsupported quantum advantage, or literal impossible-scale claims.

Unknown/unconfigured provider/model/runtime/hardware/node/dataset/license/service/API/tool/plugin/QPU/Universe destination = UNAVAILABLE / WAITING_DATA / WAITING_NODE / UNKNOWN / DENIED as appropriate. Most restrictive policy wins.

## 30 User Stories
DC1 Superbrain Service Fabric Contract — service identity, owner, node, tenant/Universe, classification, capability, authz, health, budgets, evidence, retry, timeout and authority boundaries.
DC2 Service Registry v3 — explicit service/API capabilities with versions, schemas, owners, dependencies, availability and verification state.
DC3 Service Route Compiler — candidate routes only among compatible authorized VERIFIED services/nodes, with no trust downgrade on failure.
DC4 Service Mesh Heartbeat/Census — exact RUNNING_VERIFIED service/API/agent/workcell/node counts with timestamps and evidence.
DC5 Service Circuit Breaker & Quarantine — bounded failure thresholds, backoff, degraded state, quarantine and human-visible recovery requirements.
DC6 Service Contract Compatibility Gate — schema/version/permission/dependency compatibility before routing or handoff.
DC7 Agent Department API Mesh Contract — typed request/response, caller, object, purpose, tenant/Universe, classification, consequence, quota, timeout and evidence requirements.
DC8 Department API Gateway — bounded gateways for business, finance, supply chain, operations, software, AI, data, research, security, history/culture and executive domains.
DC9 API Authz & Data-Class Firewall — deny-by-default caller/object/purpose/classification checks; API discovery never grants rights.
DC10 API Idempotency/Rate-Limit/Budget Controller — bounded retry keys, quotas, model/tool-call budgets and no unsafe amplification.
DC11 Cross-Department API Workflow Compiler — typed DAGs with evidence gates, dependency states and no permission inheritance.
DC12 API Reliability/Truth Scorecard — correctness, evidence completeness, availability, latency, stale state, failures and regression.
DC13 Distributed Memory Lake Streaming Contract — object/event ID, source/destination tenant+Universe+node, classification, provenance, hash, format, retention, expiry and revocation.
DC14 Memory Lake Object Manifest v2 — immutable content hash, rights, classification, lineage, representation, storage tier, encryption/key ref and lifecycle.
DC15 Memory Lake Stream Router — explicit enrolled destinations only, local/sealed firewall, cross-Universe deny-by-default.
DC16 Memory Lake Compaction/Index Pack Builder — compressed signed lexical/vector/graph/structured/temporal/offline packs preserving required provenance and contradictions.
DC17 Memory Freshness/Contradiction Monitor — stale/unknown/conflicting state surfaces explicitly and never auto-resolves unsupported claims.
DC18 Memory Lake Recovery/Replay Harness — corrupted object, stale replica, revoked package, partition, duplicate and restart scenarios.
DC19 Model Broker Contract — provider/model/version/locality/data classes/context/tools, authz, budgets, rate/resource proxies, eval state and availability.
DC20 Local-First Model Broker v7 — select verified local models first where suitable; use configured cloud providers only when policy/classification permits.
DC21 Provider Data Boundary Firewall v4 — sealed/local-only/private classes denied from disallowed providers with explicit reason codes and no silent fallback.
DC22 Model Evaluation Grid Contract — task suite, dataset/source rights, metrics, baselines, seeds/configs, hardware/runtime, evidence and reproducibility.
DC23 Continuous Model Reliability/Regression Matrix v5 — task quality, citation/evidence traceability, calibration, safety, latency, resource/cost proxies and regressions.
DC24 Adaptive Accelerator Federation Contract — enrolled compute node, architecture, runtime/driver/toolchain, trust, locality, quota, memory, precision, health and benchmark evidence.
DC25 Federated Workload Placement Candidate Engine — correctness/security/privacy first, then verified performance, locality, capacity, checkpointability and resource proxies.
DC26 AMD/NVIDIA/NPU/Quantum Compatibility & Benchmark Matrix v7 — reproducible evidence, classical baselines, simulator-vs-QPU truth and fallback states.
DC27 Autonomous AI Product Studio Network Contract — isolated studio, owner, user story, repo/workspace, roles, scopes, data classes, tools/models, budgets, tests, security, evidence and stop conditions.
DC28 Studio Product Engineering Pipeline — gap/user story -> architecture -> sandbox implementation -> tests -> security/SBOM/secret scan -> eval/benchmark -> human review -> VERIFIED_CANDIDATE or RETIRED.
DC29 Multi-Universe State Compiler & Disaster Recovery Fabric — signed/versioned/revocable state manifests, derived deltas, compatibility gates, explicit destination/purpose/classification/time, recovery simulation, rollback and no raw-private pooling.
DC30 Founder Superbrain Service Fabric Brief — exact live census, service/API health, memory-lake status, model broker/eval states, accelerator states, studio outputs, Universe state/recovery health, blockers and next safe stories.

## Required Verification
- RUNNING_VERIFIED requires current heartbeat/runtime evidence.
- Service/API registration or discovery never grants execution/data authority.
- Department APIs enforce caller/tenant/Universe/object/purpose/classification and consequence boundaries.
- Offline work checkpoints/stops when no authorized powered node is available.
- Memory streaming uses explicit enrolled endpoints only; no arbitrary scanning/interception.
- Sealed/local-only data cannot silently transit provider/service/memory/Universe routes.
- Unknown-rights/leaked/stolen/restricted data cannot enter models, evals, memory, products, tools or replication.
- Memory compaction cannot erase provenance, contradiction or audit requirements.
- Multi-model agreement is not evidence; hidden chain-of-thought is never persisted.
- DETECTED != SUPPORTED != VERIFIED != RUNNING_VERIFIED.
- Quantum simulator qubits are never represented as physical QPU qubits; classical baseline mandatory.
- Accelerator federation cannot purchase capacity, grant hardware authority or create billing commitments.
- Product Studio agents cannot create external accounts/credentials, publish, contract, purchase, move money, deploy production or weaken Guardian/RLS.
- Universe state packages are explicit, signed/versioned/revocable and scoped per destination/purpose/object/classification/time.
- Raw private cross-tenant pooling remains DENIED.
- Disaster-recovery test PASS does not authorize production failover.
- Founder Brief reports UNKNOWN/UNAVAILABLE/NOT_TESTED truthfully.

Evidence vocabulary: PASS / FAIL / PARTIAL / DEGRADED / UNAVAILABLE / WAITING_DATA / WAITING_NODE / OFFLINE_STOPPED / UNKNOWN / STALE / REGRESSED / NOT_TESTED / DENIED. DOCUMENTED != IMPLEMENTED. IMPLEMENTED != VERIFIED. VERIFIED != PRODUCTION AUTHORIZATION.

items.body:
## Purpose
Track Santo's ordered implementation roadmap and release gates without overbuilding product/UI before the core architecture is proven.

GitHub code, issues, PRs, commits, and Actions are the source of truth.

## Completed architecture foundation

- [x] #1 — P0 Bootstrap Santoreno monorepo and CI
- [x] #2 — P1 Provision Cloudflare foundation and bindings
- [x] #3 — P2 Minimal B2B auth, tenancy, and tenant isolation
- [x] #4 — P3 Customer server credentials and domain controls
- [x] #5 — P4 `/v1/session/exchange` for external users
- [x] #6 — P5 Atomic `TenantMeterDO` quota engine
- [x] #7 — Minimal grounded AI vertical slice
- [x] #33 — Phase 6 Global AI Search catalog and filtered retrieval
- [x] #36 — Phase 7 Full AI Core, validated buffered SSE and bounded failure lifecycle
- [x] #43 — Phase 8 Authenticated trusted sources, source details and R2 media
- [x] #52 — Phase 9 SQLite ConversationDO, grounded follow-ups, verified bounded context and replay

### P6 vertical slice / #7 completion evidence

Final PR #25 documentation head `59679a56eb273e2f343e2d6ee7d94babf9409b1e` passed both required gates on the exact same SHA:

- `Verify` `37305283632` (#250) — success
- `P6 Staging Acceptance` `37305276676` (#26) — success

PR #25 was squash-merged to `main` as `8d1a422c514869844fefc9c5c29c1ffdf2bc923e`.

Exact post-merge `Verify` `37306176415` (#251) passed `repository-policy` and `code-quality` including lint, typecheck, tests, build, and smoke.

### Phase 6 global retrieval / #33 completion evidence

Final PR #35 clean head `a5746b8b87ad23c6aeada29740e7c0ae7955e5bb` passed both required exact-head gates:

- `Verify` `37327203385` (#283) — success
- `P33 Global Search Staging Acceptance` `37327194943` (#15) — success

Live acceptance proved the authenticated `/v1/ai/query` path with two run-isolated Santo-wide libraries, MRCP-only filtering, USMLE-only filtering, All Libraries default behavior, real Workers AI generation, server-validated citations, library-scoped idempotency, invalid-filter fail-closed behavior, deterministic quota release, and full fixture cleanup.

PR #35 was squash-merged to `main` as `81d15a61140cee28d1a9a7909cb27e1a70b7ba14`.

Exact post-merge `Verify` `37330375869` (#284) passed repository policy, formatting/lint, typecheck, tests, build, and smoke.

### Phase 7 / #36 completion evidence

- PR #38 model policy and PR #39 deterministic prompt builder: merged and post-merge verified.
- PR #42 final head `6c1ba89448725507dcade62b95963753e127de10`: **Verify 37931171789** and **P7 Validated Streaming Staging Acceptance 37931165458** both passed on the exact same SHA.
- Live staging proved WorkOS tenant/session, two isolated global AI Search libraries, Workers AI, validated citations, buffered SSE, quota idempotency, invalid filter fail-closed, and full cleanup.
- PR #42 merged as `29805bc85ac864e66b7cdc7cd787ac52c1749613`; exact post-merge **Verify 37932098841** passed.
- Handoff PR #44 merged as `566d5ab97b2750137896647d2277c0576ffbfa8d`; exact post-merge **Verify 37932600616** passed.
- Strict buffer-until-validated transport is intentionally distinct from provider-token streaming; Cloudflare Workers AI JSON Mode does not currently provide native JSON-schema streaming. See `docs/AI_STREAMING_CONTRACT.md`.

### Phase 8 / #43 completion evidence

- PR #49 source/image contracts: exact-head `Verify 38414736636`, merged `05b75ba9384ece2250983994e92190a69cfadd9b`; post-merge `Verify 38415599816` passed.
- PR #50 authenticated source resolver and R2 media: final head `3769cdc9d79e4deb671bb512e9d9c02f4b05f7dd` passed **Verify 38419869177** and **P8 Trusted Sources Staging Acceptance 38419858440** on the exact same SHA.
- P8 live staging proved WorkOS-backed tenants/sessions, verified AI Search citations, real R2 image manifests/delivery, source/user/tenant isolation, failed/forged assets, and fixture cleanup.
- PR #50 merged `93ac404f3de1c59949eb856e41d5a8cb433afb8a`; exact post-merge **Verify 38420860631** passed.
- Source schemas/API lifecycle are documented in `docs/TRUSTED_SOURCE_CONTRACT.md`. Production R2 lifecycle cleanup remains a deployment-operations prerequisite.

## Current active implementation issue

**#58 — Phase 10: embeddable Lit Santo Widget.** Phase 9/#52 completed and post-merge verified.

Phase 9 builds on the proven #7/#33/#36/#43 identity, atomic quota, global retrieval and trusted source/asset authority. No premature full widget or portal.

### Phase 9 complete / Phase 10 active

- Phase 9 PR #54 (ordered state), PR #56 (grounded follow-ups) and PR #57 (bounded summary + stale lease fencing) are merged. PR #57 final head `84e785a7067fc0257f843655f84e2eb89956b279` passed exact-head **Verify 38445457126** and real **P9 Summary & Lease Staging 38445450546**; merged `17e032e3935cad4f6ec290ee770e3baaf09f6540`, post-merge **Verify 38446592614** passed.
- Final handoff PR #59 merged `a5313b67beb7a8a53389e48232740193d92ea0af`, postmerge **Verify 38447039474** passed. Issue #52 closed as completed; duplicate #51 closed as duplicate.
- **Active #58 Phase 10 Santo Widget** — first secure Lit/Shadow DOM, mobile shell, strict API-backed session, conversation retry and grounded media/citation delivery. Phase 11 framework compatibility and Phase 12 full tenant portal remain deferred.

## Mandatory architecture gates

### Identity gate — PASSED
- Tenant identity comes from authenticated context.
- Customer server credentials rotate/revoke.
- External-user sessions are short-lived and tenant-scoped.
- Cross-tenant access fails closed.

### Quota gate — PASSED
- 100 simultaneous reserve attempts with one remaining unit produce exactly `1 allowed / 99 denied`.
- Reserve/finalize/release are atomic and idempotent.
- Tenant allowance overrides oversized user quota.
- Suspension/expiry rules fail closed.

### Grounding/retrieval gate — PASSED in #7 and #33
- Auth occurs before quota/search/model work.
- Quota reserve occurs before expensive work.
- AI Search evidence is retrieved through the global catalog boundary.
- `All Libraries` remains the default; validated `library_id` is retrieval filtering, never tenant authorization.
- Answer generation is bounded by retrieved evidence.
- Citation IDs are server-validated against retrieved source IDs.
- Unknown library filters fail closed without silent broadening.
- No-evidence/search-failure/invented-citation paths do not produce a fake sourced answer.
- Successful requests charge exactly once.
- Identical retries cannot double-charge, including across library scope.

The Master Plan §123 first technical milestone is proven end-to-end and the Phase 6 global retrieval expansion is post-merge verified.

## Portal sequencing rule

The original hard block on broad portal expansion is lifted because session exchange, atomic quota, and the grounded AI path are proven. However, continue in roadmap order and do **not** jump directly to a full tenant portal. Build the remaining core AI/content/conversation/widget primitives first unless a narrowly scoped administration surface is required to test them.

## Active/deferred backlog

- [x] #33 — Phase 6: Global AI Search catalog, optional library filtering, retrieval metadata — **COMPLETED + POST-MERGE VERIFIED**
- [x] #36 — Phase 7: Model adapter, bounded RAG prompt, strict JSON/SSE contracts, validated citations, cancellation/timeouts — **COMPLETED + POST-MERGE VERIFIED**
- [x] #43 — Phase 8: Trusted source metadata, citation resolution and R2 images — **COMPLETED + POST-MERGE VERIFIED**
- [ ] #52 — Phase 9: `ConversationDO` multi-turn state, ordering, summaries, stream coordination and idempotent messages — **ACTIVE**
- [ ] Phase 10 — Full Lit `<santo-ai>` widget
- [ ] Phase 11 — Framework compatibility matrix: React, Next.js, Vue, Laravel-rendered, WordPress-like, plain HTML
- [ ] Phase 12 — Full Tenant Portal: Overview, Users, Plans, Usage, Branding, Integration, Team, Billing, Settings
- [ ] Phase 13 — Branding/white-label controls
- [ ] Phase 14 — Customer Management API for quota/plan/expiry/suspend/resume/usage
- [ ] Phase 15 — Queues & Webhooks with signing, retries, delivery logs, idempotency
- [ ] Phase 16 — Analytics Engine events and portal reporting
- [ ] Phase 17 — Security hardening: WAF, rate limits, CORS, CSP, Turnstile, IDOR/role/audit/abuse tests
- [ ] Phase 18 — Load tests for session exchange, quota, config, conversation creation, search, mock model, then real model
- [ ] Phase 19 — Pilot with Royal Bank + MedPark, no tenant-specific forks
- [ ] Phase 20 — Production launch gate

Open detailed implementation issues only as the preceding dependency is completed or when a safe parallel dependency is explicit.

## Permanent constraints

- No separate DB per customer initially.
- No separate R2 per customer initially.
- No separate AI Search per customer initially.
- No Supabase dependency in Santo core.
- No direct customer production-database access.
- No customer-specific Santo forks/hacks.
- Tenant identity must come from authenticated context.
- External users remain scoped by `tenant_id + external_user_id`.
- Quota remains server-side, atomic, and idempotent.
- Portal/widget never access D1/DO/R2/AI Search directly.
- Global libraries are shared; library selection is a retrieval filter, not tenant authorization.
- AI output is structured, not arbitrary HTML.
- Citations are server-validated against retrieved source IDs.
- Customer owns its users/billing; Santo owns AI infrastructure.

## Verification protocol

For every meaningful implementation change:

1. Implement the smallest clean change tied to the active issue.
2. Add/update tests.
3. Require GitHub Actions `Verify` on the exact implementation head.
4. Run any issue-specific staging/live acceptance gate on that exact head.
5. Fix failures before proceeding.
6. Update the active issue checklist and add exact evidence.
7. Update `PROJECT_STATUS.md` when project state changes.
8. Update this roadmap when completion/sequencing changes.
9. Add an ADR only for a material architecture decision.
10. Require exact post-merge `Verify` before closing an implementation issue.

items.title: [P0] Audit en handhaaf 100% portaalinvoer, externe-data-doorwerking en tenant-readback
items.body:
# Doel
**Werkelijke 100% formulier- en externe-brondekking** in het bestaande klantportaal aantoonbaar maken. Geen parallelle Brain, Heartbeat of scheduler. Gaat verder dan de nu ingediende lossless causal-impact reparatie in PR #4214.

## Traceerbare verplichtingen

1. Inventariseer alle routes/pages uit `portal-v2/page-registry.js`, `portal-v2/page-shell.js`, `portal-next`, legacy en dynamische/integratieformulieren. Verzamel in een automatisch gevalideerde matrix: pagina, veld-ID, eigenaar, tenantcontext, write-endpoint, readback, sourceRevision, Brain-ACK en afhankelijke modellen. Markeer read-only en admin-only apart.
2. Sluit iedere customer write aan op één bestaande canonieke state/BusinessInput writeflow of bewijs een andere authoritative servermutatie met precieze Brain lineage. Verbied parallelle browserstores en orphan inputs.
3. Externe provider-/regulerings-/marktdata: op nieuwe observation via bestaande Source Universe + Company Graph per tenant impact herbeoordelen; alleen daadwerkelijk gewijzigde dependency subgraph, met provenance en freshness. Externe refresh mag customer input niet overschrijven; tenant-impact is nooit globale signaaldata.
4. Voor finance, AI/cloud, governance, proces, marketing, mensen, risico, juridische kaders en CSRD geldt: bij relevante change de juiste modellen herberekenen of expliciet REVIEW_REQUIRED als gegevens/regeldragende bron ontbreken. Geen gefingeerde €-impact/emissies/compliance.
5. Complete durability: transactioneel idempotente outbox/split-batch van >750 KB, restarts/offline, foutretries zonder dubbele Brain-records, monotone versiecontrole en per-batch consumer-ACK.
6. Klant ziet in dezelfde portalweergave: wijziging, bron, tijd, vorige/nieuwe waarde waar geautoriseerd, betrokken pagina's/modellen, actueel/stale/review/pending/applied, reden, voorgestelde actie en readback; alleen eigen tenantinformatie. De bestaande impactmap uit PR #4214 is de eerste UI-draaglaag.
7. CI-contract: auto-gegenereerde route/form-dekking op iedere PR; browser E2E met twee geïsoleerde tenants, 200 velden, 1000 signalen, gelijktijdige writes, fake provider failure, conflict, revocation, GDPR/minimisatie, backfill en bijbehorende evidence.
8. Afsluiten alleen na exact-main Required+CodeQL, Supabase runtime/projection readback, Netlify deployment & authenticated browser readback, en bewezen terugkoppeling naar ONE BRAIN/Heartbeat/Powerhouse. Admin-control-center toont per keten onafhankelijk bewijs, geen kunstmatige green.

## Huidige realiteit
Het bestaande impact engine-contract registreert alle **geregistreerde page IDs**, niet het daadwerkelijke gebruik van iedere DOM-input. PR #4214 sluit enkele bewezen causal-loss/race-gaten en voegt klantzichtbaarheid toe. Dit issue mag niet automatisch sluiten op basis van PR #4214 alleen. Laat eerdere gekoppelde verplichtingen bestaan tot eindbewijs.

## Borgingsconsolidatie — 20 oktober 2026

Fingerprint: `borging-consolidatie-20261020-v1`. Op expliciet verzoek zijn negen bestaande Notion-pagina's bijgewerkt en teruggelezen; drie betrokken database-records hebben daarnaast actuele samenvattende properties gekregen. Geen nieuwe parallelle registers.

- [Master Build, Borging & Go-Live Register](https://app.notion.com/p/3c3da36aac8a81dda3fec4fc12bba5df): geconsolideerde statusmatrix en bronbewijs.
- [Canonical System Map](https://app.notion.com/p/3dcda36aac8a8152be3dedbb32b06239): samenhang en bewijsgrenzen.
- [Error Register & Release Gates](https://app.notion.com/p/3c6da36aac8a81cc9731ea9355881230): bewezen herstel versus open resultaten.
- [Menselijk Handboek](https://app.notion.com/p/3dcda36aac8a81acaad1c88751e9e814): uitleg borging en ondernemerbetekenis.
- [Direct Knowledge Base](https://app.notion.com/p/3c7da36aac8a817a8beff480e45a2aef): learning, herstel en preventie.
- [Dashboard Hub](https://app.notion.com/p/3e4da36aac8a81fbb340daccce80dec8): bestaande vindplaatsen gekoppeld aan actuele waarheid.
- [Engineering Registry](https://app.notion.com/p/3cada36aac8a81199e6cfa9217bf5218): historische Make-snapshots onderscheiden van actuele evidence.
- [Bestaande auditregistratie](https://app.notion.com/p/3ffda36aac8a81ac927fe06346420cb9): ochtendbevindingen behouden, latere bewijzen aangevuld.
- [Portal V2 Current State](https://app.notion.com/p/3dcda36aac8a81deb0f9e516a088939a): inhoud en statusvelden bijgewerkt; fixing/blocked blijft functionele acceptatiestatus.

Documentaire readback: alle negen pagina's bevatten exact eenmaal deze fingerprint; centrale matrix bevat de vier exacte bronlinks en e-mailproductie-event. De drie bijgewerkte recordproperties zijn na schrijven teruggelezen. Dit sluit deze documentaire synchronisatie, niet de volledige systeemacceptatie.

Open borgingsdekking onder dit bestaande issue: volledige vergelijking **capability/route/veld → owner/autoriteit → code/config → logging → test → exacte productie-identiteit → getroffen portaalpagina → resultaat**. Volledigheid is niet aangetoond door deze documentatie-update. Twee echte geautoriseerde klantketens, Brain/Heartbeat ACK, negatieve tenantisolatie, #4558 representatieve 51-veldpariteit, daadwerkelijke connector/model/forecast-output en afzonderlijke providerresultaten blijven nodig.

Bronnen: [laatste portaalacceptatie](https://github.com/arthurprinsen-ai/Bedrijfsgeheugen/issues/4215#issuecomment-6296290722), [laatste historische telling 11 bewezen/225 open](https://github.com/arthurprinsen-ai/Bedrijfsgeheugen/issues/4215#issuecomment-6295423181), [#4567 e-mailproductiebewijs](https://github.com/arthurprinsen-ai/Bedrijfsgeheugen/issues/4478#issuecomment-6296265910), [release/index/HTTP-bewijs](https://github.com/arthurprinsen-ai/Bedrijfsgeheugen/issues/4215#issuecomment-6295387867).

Geen productiecode, scheduler, autorisatie of portaalweergave veranderd; runtime-consumptie van de nieuwe Notion-tekst en automatische volledige inventarisdekking worden niet als bewezen geregistreerd. Oorspronkelijke acceptatiecriteria en historie hierboven blijven intact; issue blijft open.
