items.title: [FABRIC CONVERGENCE] Grok orchestration + VPS/website migration to canonical Agent Fabric
items.body:
Workstream: WS:EXECUTIVE-CAPACITY-FABRIC
Authority: current Chairman direction, 2026-09-24
Program owner: Sol / CEO
Protected source pin at creation: 41617f5087d14fcbc782bf419cf1a1cd16b1918f
Skillpack: mastermind.sol_skillpack.v1 1.0.1 / bootstrap-major 1

## Outcome

Converge two consumers onto the **existing** Mastermind Executive/Capacity/Worker Fabric without creating another router, queue, lifecycle, retry plane, provider selector, result store, or host-control authority:

1. **Grok Operations Bot becomes a thin orchestrator/principal** that decomposes and adjudicates while bounded execution is delegated through the canonical Fabric.
2. **Mastermind VPS / website reasoning stops directly executing through the legacy Codex -> Claude OAuth waterfall** and instead submits role-correct bounded work to the same Fabric, with Capacity selecting the least-scarce capable eligible worker/provider/host.

The accepted end state is one control plane:

```text
caller (Grok principal | website service principal | future clients)
  -> authenticated role-specific Executive ingress
  -> canonical Runtime Job / Attempt / effect truth
  -> existing COO/planning + Model Router + Capacity
  -> exact selected Worker / host / realm
  -> local or remote Worker Broker / provider-neutral adapter
  -> canonical result + review/repair evidence
  -> exact parent/service result consumption
```

Studio is an execution host, not the public orchestration authority. The existing remote Worker Gateway remains post-placement transport bound to an already-selected Job/Attempt/Worker identity; callers do not directly choose Studio, provider credentials, accounts, hosts, or worker ids.

## Current source facts

- Existing remote substrate: `control_plane/remote_worker_transport.py`, `control_plane/remote_worker_broker_client.py`, `ops/executive_os/remote_worker_gateway.py`, `control_plane/executive_capacity_join.py`.
- Existing Grok Wake substrate: `integrations/executive_wake/grok_bot_http.py` and `grok_bot_routine.py`; accepted/start is distinct from target consumption/result.
- Existing Fabric visibility: `control_plane/fabric_job_view.py`.
- Existing website legacy direct balancer: `brain/provider_waterfall.py` -> `brain/client.py`, currently used by Strategist/Committee/Macro Risk/CIO and other seats.
- Existing Astra external-Fabric freeze already establishes the key client law: model-facing callers author bounded intent; trusted code authors authority and physical placement; no public `fabric.delegate` / provider-spawn API.
- #804 is the incumbent non-CEO service-principal mutation-sink carrier.
- #957/#960/#961 are the incumbent broad COO-principal mandate/request lineage.
- #624 is the Grok autonomy architecture lineage; its older consultation-only assumptions must be reconciled with current protected Grok Wake/Company Consultation source rather than duplicated.
- #386 remains the active dispatch-consumption / watcher-wake convergence P0; do not claim end-to-end autonomy before its relevant real-path gates close.
- #633 remains the attended Astra -> Fabric client carrier and has an unrelated Auth0 DCR `EFFECT_UNKNOWN`; do not retry, replace, or reuse that exact enrollment effect.

## Architecture rulings

### A. Grok

Grok is a **principal/orchestrator**, not a worker pool and not a second scheduler.

Grok should:
- recover intent and decompose work;
- keep architecture / hard judgment / cross-return synthesis;
- issue role-correct Fabric child/root requests through an authenticated Executive profile;
- read bounded canonical job/result views;
- receive exact RuntimeBinding/Wake nudges for returns;
- request repair / continuation / stop through the incumbent lifecycle owner.

Grok should **not**:
- use its VPs to log into Studio and drive workers directly;
- choose provider/model/account/host credentials;
- maintain its own durable queue, worker registry, retry ledger or result store;
- replay worker transcripts into its main context;
- retry or fail over a modifying operation after START / effect uncertainty.

Provider-native Grok VPs/helpers may exist only as shrink-only, same-Attempt helpers under an admitted capability ceiling. Any independently recoverable responsibility, separate review, distinct custody, or durable fan-out becomes an Executive child Job.

Company Consultation remains useful for bounded principal-to-principal questions. It is not the execution Fabric.

### B. Remote Fabric

Do **not** expose the raw Worker Broker as a generic public subagent API.

The remote-callable Fabric boundary is the authenticated Executive ingress + read/status surface. After canonical placement, the existing remote broker transport reaches the selected host. This preserves one lifecycle and makes Studio/Mac minis/VPS workers interchangeable physical capacity behind Capacity.

### C. Website / VPS

Replace the legacy execution role of `brain/provider_waterfall.py` with a Fabric-backed compatibility adapter while initially preserving the `brain.client.call_model(...)` consumer contract.

Website processes are **service principals**, not CEO/Fable impersonators. They must enter through the role-correct non-CEO sink (#804 lineage or its accepted successor), with tightly derived task kind / authorities and stable operation identity.

Migration policy:
- feature-gated `fabric` backend first;
- no caller-supplied provider/model/account/host;
- pre-effect unavailability degrades according to the seat's existing deterministic fallback policy;
- once a Fabric attempt STARTS or becomes EFFECT_UNKNOWN, never replay through the old waterfall;
- preserve seat/book/usage attribution in canonical telemetry;
- old waterfall becomes diagnostic-only after accepted parity canaries, then is retired as an execution router.

First website canary should be a low-authority additive narration/research seat (e.g. CIO narration) before strategist/risk/committee paths.

## Dependency / wave plan

### G0 — ingress convergence
Reconcile the role-correct non-CEO/COO ingress owner (#804 + #957/#960/#961) into one accepted mutation sink with distinct role policies. No new listener or Job creator.

### G1 — Grok Fabric client
Add a Grok principal profile/client over the accepted Executive ingress:
- stable operation/request identity;
- bounded objective/acceptance packet;
- canonical status/fabric view;
- exact effect reconciliation;
- no placement fields;
- exact RuntimeBinding/Wake return.

### G2 — Grok token-relief canary
Run one substantive bounded project:
Grok decomposes -> Fabric child executes -> independent review/repair if required -> bounded result returns -> Grok adjudicates.
Measure Grok context/token usage, delegated share, return bytes, latency, duplicate/effect-unknown incidents, and Chairman interventions. No transcript replay.

### V0 — website Fabric compatibility adapter
Introduce a Fabric backend behind `brain.client.call_model` without changing downstream seat semantics. Map role/seat to reviewed service-principal task profiles and preserve deterministic degradation.

### V1 — one website canary
Move one additive/read-only seat to Fabric and prove output shape, attribution, timeout/result handling, restart/idempotency, and no direct OAuth-provider choice.

### V2 — staged website migration
Move remaining eligible seats in risk order. Interactive streaming/chat paths are assessed separately where their latency/streaming contract differs from batch/background reasoning.

### V3 — retire legacy balancer
After parity, failure-injection and production-path proof, remove the old Codex/Claude OAuth waterfall from normal website execution. Provider/account cooling remains a Capacity/provider-readiness responsibility, not a website router.

### R0 — remote-host proof
Prove one canonical Job placed by Capacity onto a remote eligible host, executed through the existing mTLS gateway/broker, result returned to Runtime, no duplicate effect under response loss, and exact cleanup/readback.

### R1 — resilience / scale
Fault matrix: pre-submit refusal, lost response after modifying write, host offline, provider exhausted, stale Capacity, worker crash, parent restart, duplicate submit, review rejection/repair, return-path failure. Prove no blind failover and no second control plane.

## Acceptance

Program is complete only when:
- Grok routinely delegates bounded work without direct Studio/provider orchestration;
- one remote host round trip is production-proven through canonical placement;
- website batch reasoning uses Fabric rather than the legacy direct OAuth waterfall;
- Capacity owns provider/account/host selection;
- result/review/repair returns are canonical and bounded;
- START/EFFECT_UNKNOWN never trigger blind replay;
- failures degrade truthfully;
- one real Grok token-relief comparison demonstrates a material reduction in principal-context/worker-token burn without reducing accepted output quality;
- one website staged migration passes real production-path canaries;
- Chairman performs zero routine account selection, tab shuttling, or worker-message relay.

## Immediate next action

Do not arm another dispatcher. First reconcile G0 against current #804/#957/#960/#961 and #386 source/ownership, then implement the first **client-side, role-correct** vertical on a path-disjoint carrier. The website and Grok clients can advance independently once the accepted ingress contract is stable; remote host execution remains behind current Capacity/Worker Broker ownership.

items.title: Billing: design mechanism ADRs and implement device metering, relay billing, and optional spending caps
items.body:
## Current progress

The design work and first metering/reporting slices are in `main`. The remaining implementation must stay opt-in: no account receives a paid schedule or spending cap by default, and deployments without billing configuration keep current behavior.

- ADR-0049 records the billing boundary. ADR-0050 (#276), ADR-0051 (#305), ADR-0052 (#306), and ADR-0053 (#307, updated in PR #316) are accepted: they define usage metering/reporting, versioned rates and alerts, optional organization-wide managed-relay caps, and the Paddle merchant-of-record pilot. The approved policies are implemented behind explicit assignments/opt-ins; shadow-driven tuning and launch configuration/retention gates remain open below.
- Merged device work (#283, #285, #286, #288, #297) supplies lifecycle accounting, authorized device reports, audited operator controls, relay attribution, recoverable aggregation, and opt-in successful-write collection.
- #298 and #299 are merged: signed relay usage batches, immutable spool replay, authenticated bounded ingestion, authorization checks, and transactional deduplicated relay totals/coverage.
- #301 is merged after all CI checks passed. The relay uploads retained signed batches only when configured; delivery is outside the packet forwarding path.
- #303 is merged after 27 successful checks and 3 skips. Customer relay reports are account-scoped, audited, and include coverage/freshness limitations; missing usage is not estimated.
- #308 is merged after 27 successful CI jobs and 3 skips. It adds exact calculator-only graduated device and pooled relay estimates, plus the approved pilot schedule constructor. It does not assign a schedule to an account, emit invoices, or enforce caps. Focused management tests and billing vet passed on its rebased head.
- #312 is merged after 55 successful CI jobs and 6 skips. It adds immutable persisted rate snapshots, explicit account-period assignments, overlap protection, snapshot digest validation, and an estimate path that only uses an assigned schedule. It does not finalize invoices or enable recurring charges.
- #313 merged at `473de7897e688d519ca6a9e7a12a2855fd3809e0` on 2026-10-12 after 27 successful CI jobs and 3 skips. It adds an explicitly invoked, audited command to assign the approved pilot schedule for an exact account period, plus assignment and shadow-usage operator guides. It does not finalize invoices, collect payment, send alerts, or enforce caps.
- #314 merged at `da443e91ab74b6404340c75e2ac0978838686953` on 2026-10-12. It adds immutable invoice-input finalization for complete reports in explicitly assigned UTC calendar months, with exact proration and per-line truncation down to minor units. It also updates `quinn-proto` to fixed `0.11.18`; its updated-head CI passed, including dependency policy.
- #315 merged to `main` as `2654703` on 2026-10-13. It adds authenticated relay credit grants, account-wide reservation, the default-off local forwarding gate, safe cap activation through short uncapped leases, the audited owner/admin cap API, persisted in-app alerts, and a Billing console. Commit `480f377` adds signed, idempotent grant surrender: clean shutdown closes the forwarding gate and returns unused credits within a 15-second budget, enabling current-period decreases after all grants are accounted for. Local focused Rust/Go/frontend checks and generated API drift checks passed; updated-head GitHub CI and deliverable-build jobs passed. Crash recovery/fencing remain open; support terms are approved below.
- #331 merged at `e98d661` on 2026-10-13, delivering the approved durable Paddle retry schedule and payment-state handling.
- #334 merged at `e247fb2` on 2026-10-13: invoice-gated 13-month lifecycle-event pruning, verified account checkpoints, and report reconstruction, with a fail-closed guard for report windows before the earliest pruned checkpoint.

## Agreed product and architecture decisions

- Support managed hosting and self-hosted deployments with optional paid support. Licensing stays unchanged. Plan enforcement defaults off; an unconfigured deployment keeps existing behavior.
- Managed hosting uses graduated device pricing: each tier is charged at its own rate. Approved pilot rates are $2.50/device/month for devices 1–10, $1.50 for devices 11–50, and $0.75 above 50.
- Enrolled, non-revoked devices are billable while online or offline. Bill only the eligible enrolled time; online activity does not determine billability.
- Managed relay use is pooled by organization and billed separately. Count customer traffic forwarded by managed relays in both directions; internal relay-to-relay hops and direct peer-to-peer traffic are excluded.
- The accepted relay meter boundary (ADR-0050) is opaque `RecvPacket` payload bytes counted only after a complete successful destination-client transport write. It excludes framing/transport overhead, retransmissions, failed or partial writes, queue drops, direct traffic, internal mesh hops, and unconfigured self-hosted/TURN transports. A successful write is transport acceptance, not proven endpoint receipt.
- Approved pilot relay rate: 10 decimal GB included per organization-month, then $0.20 per additional decimal GB.
- Usage alerts are intended to be on by default. Customers may opt into a managed-relay spending cap and must acknowledge that reaching it can interrupt relayed connections. The cap applies to relay spend, not device charges.
- The control plane owns plans, usage totals, and global spending policy; relays enforce local traffic limits. Any global cap must coordinate reservations/allowances across relays rather than relying only on ADR-0038's local capacity cap.
- Payment updates subscription/payment state asynchronously and must never be a live networking dependency.

## Approved billing policies

- Use UTC calendar months. Prorate devices by exact eligible enrolled time; enrollment, revocation, and re-enrollment change eligible time. Keep incomplete usage open and unbilled rather than estimating it.
- Truncate invoice line amounts down to cents at finalization; do not round up. Finalize each line once after its period's usage is complete.
- Send relay-usage alerts at 75%, 90%, and 100% of allowance/cap, once per threshold per period, to billing admins. Include a warning when usage coverage is incomplete.
- Relay spending caps use the UTC calendar-month period and remain off unless an organization explicitly sets a USD relay-overage limit and acknowledges possible interruption. Use central byte-credit reservations shared across relays; reserve before forwarding and count ambiguous writes as consumed. At exhaustion, stop only capped managed-relay forwarding. Target no charge overshoot from admitted writes; show usage-report delay separately from reserved credits. Apply increases only after credits are durably granted and decreases next period unless every outstanding relay grant is surrendered or safely fenced. Tune grant size/expiry and the healthy accounting-delay limit from the 30–90 day shadow window.
- For the pilot, use a 14-day payment grace period; retry asynchronously on days 1, 3, 7, and 12; send in-app notices to billing admins; then keep service active after day 14 and mark the invoice past due for customer/operator resolution. Payment failure never suspends networking. Keep finalized invoices and audit/payment state for 7 years; keep normalized webhook events for 13 months; discard raw webhook bodies after signature verification. Checkout prices are pre-tax USD; Paddle calculates applicable tax and displays it as a separate line. The Karst-managed one-time retry mechanism is approved and is being implemented in PR #331.

## Decisions still needed before dependent behavior ships

1. The merchant-of-record model and Paddle Billing pilot provider are selected and recorded in ADR-0053 / PR #316. Paddle publishes a 5% + $0.50 fee per Checkout transaction ([pricing](https://www.paddle.com/pricing)). Live collection remains gated on Paddle business/domain approval, supported launch markets, and SaaS tax-category configuration. Checkout is pre-tax USD and Paddle displays applicable tax separately. The adapter must reconcile ambiguous transaction creates using the stable Karst invoice reference before retrying, because Paddle does not accept client-supplied idempotency keys for arbitrary creates.
2. Paid self-hosted support terms are approved: $1,200/year for six remote hours, weekday first response within two business days, $200/hour for additional pre-approved work, and no on-call or resolution SLA. Support is a service offer under ADR-0007 and does not change software licensing.
3. Additional billable units are excluded for the pilot. Keep the approved meters to graduated enrolled-device time and managed-relay traffic; revisit only with shadow-data evidence.
4. Resolved: retain one-time finalized invoices and use a Karst-managed durable scheduler for the approved retries on days 1, 3, 7, and 12, keyed by invoice and attempt. Use a saved payment method only when Paddle confirms Checkout consent; otherwise provide a fresh Checkout link and stop later automatic attempts. Reconcile ambiguous creates before another attempt and keep service active after day 14. Implementation is in [PR #331](https://github.com/karst-net/karst/pull/331). 


## Cost and usage evidence

The approved schedule is a pilot model, not an empirical margin forecast. Illustrative totals are $25 for 10 devices/10 GB, $103 for 50 devices/100 GB, and $433 for 250 devices/1,000 GB. These scenarios are sensitivity cases only; no representative customer usage distribution is available. Collect 30–90 days of shadow data and compare cloud-egress bytes separately from customer-billable bytes before broad rate publication.

For each account and UTC period, compare metered customer payload bytes with provider egress bytes and cost by provider, region, and route class; record free-tier/shared allowance usage separately, along with report coverage, freshness, and mapping gaps. Do not treat payload bytes as a one-to-one proxy for billed egress. For cap calibration, capture grant size/expiry, granted and consumed bytes per relay generation, renewal and surrender outcomes, accounting lag, relay count, cap-blocked forwarding time, and credits stranded by unclean restarts. Review peak/percentile consumption and worst-case outstanding reservations against remaining cap headroom; target zero overshoot, then tune grant size and healthy accounting-delay limits to reduce unnecessary interruption. Retain aggregate operational metrics only, not traffic content.

Public North America/Europe egress examples checked 2026-10-12: AWS about $0.09/GB after the account-wide 100 GB allowance; Azure about $0.087/GB for the next 10 TB on Premium routing (or $0.08/GB transit after its allowance); Google Cloud $0.12/GiB through 1 TiB, then $0.11/GiB. Actual cost varies by region, route, service, and shared-account allowances: [AWS](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/pricing/on-demand/), [Azure](https://azure.microsoft.com/en-us/pricing/details/bandwidth/), [Google Cloud](https://cloud.google.com/vpc/network-pricing).

At the approved relay rates, 100 decimal GB incurs $18 of overage and 1,000 decimal GB incurs $198. If each billable decimal GB also creates one provider-billed outbound decimal GB, public North America/Europe internet egress is roughly $0–$11 at 100 GB and $72–$112 at 1,000 GB when monthly free allowances are available; if those allowances are already consumed, roughly $8–$11 and $80–$112, respectively. The estimates use AWS’s shared 100 GB/month allowance and $0.09/GB afterward; Azure’s first 100 GB/month free then $0.087/GB Premium or $0.08/GB transit; and Google Cloud’s first 1 GiB free then $0.12/GiB through 1 TiB. GB-to-GiB conversion is included for Google. Actual routes, account-level usage, compute, inter-zone traffic, IP/NAT, control plane, support, payments, and tax can materially change costs. These are list-price sensitivity cases, not margin forecasts.

For domestic-card examples, Stripe Payments plus Billing is about $1.20 on a $25 invoice and $4.01 on $103. Paddle is about $1.75/$5.65; Stripe Managed Payments plus Billing about $2.08/$7.61. Fees exclude FX, international/payment-method differences, taxes, and negotiated pricing. Provider references: [Stripe Billing](https://stripe.com/billing/pricing), [Stripe Managed Payments](https://stripe.com/pricing), [Paddle](https://www.paddle.com/pricing). The seller/tax model and Paddle provider are now selected; this comparison is historical cost context, not a pending provider recommendation.

## Remaining delivery

On an unclean restart or unconfirmed relay report, old credits remain reserved through period end and a fresh relay generation cannot reuse them. This safely bounds spend but can strand capacity.

ADR-0051/0052 are now accepted on `main`, the shadow-usage worksheet is available, and the device-usage and package guidance reflect the remaining retention/checkpoint gate.

Adrian selected Karst-owned internal account(s) for the window; exact account ID(s) are still needed before enabling collection, which remains off until then.

Paddle collection defaults off; when enabled, it defaults to sandbox, and live API calls require a separate explicit approval gate. CI passed with 55 successful checks and 6 workflow skips.

It remains a service contract under the existing software license, with no managed-only software features.

Support price sensitivity: $1,200 for six hours and $200/hour extra implies $200 revenue per delivered hour when all included time is used. These are scenarios, not Karst's actual costs. items.title: Investigate GitHub Copilot usage-metrics REST API for cost-centre spend + model-choice analysis
items.body:
## Context

GitHub Enterprise Cloud exposes [REST API endpoints for Copilot usage metrics](https://docs.github.com/en/enterprise-cloud@latest/rest/copilot/copilot-usage-metrics?apiVersion=2026-03-10). Cost Compass currently only *simulates* AI-credit and budget behavior (`src/engine.js`, `scenarios/`). To follow up on real cost-centre usage we need to ingest this real data and answer two questions per cost centre/user:

1. **How much** are they spending (AI credits / paid overage)?
2. **How** are they spending it — e.g. are expensive models (higher premium-request multipliers) being used for trivial tasks like code review, versus lighter models for equivalent work?

## Ask

- Investigate the data points exposed by the enterprise/organization/user/repo/user-teams report families and the preview `usage-records` endpoint, and identify which fields support cost-centre attribution and model-choice/task-type analysis (feature, IDE, language, and model breakdown arrays such as `totals_by_model_feature`, `totals_by_language_model`, `totals_by_feature`, `ai_credits_used`, `ai_adoption_phase`, etc.).
- Determine whether the needed data is only available at daily granularity (`*-1-day`, historical up to 1 year) or also as rolling 28-day snapshots (`*-28-day/latest`, latest window only, no historical range parameter), and what that implies for how we must durably store extracted data ourselves (idempotent per-day upserts using the `day_partition`/`etl_id` housekeeping fields, since GitHub's signed download URLs expire and the 28-day endpoint has no history).
- Note the key limitation that `ai_credits_used` is a per-user/day total **not broken down by model or feature**, so per-model spend must be *estimated* by combining per-model interaction/LOC breakdowns with GitHub's published premium-request model multipliers, not read directly.
- Research how the resulting cost-centre/user spend and model-usage data could be linked into Azure cost-controlling functionality (Azure Cost Management, tagging/allocation, and the Microsoft FinOps toolkit/FOCUS data format), given Copilot spend billed through an Azure subscription is not natively broken down per user/model on the Azure invoice.
- Produce a written investigation/design summary (data points, granularity + storage implications, and the Azure cost-management linking approach) to ground a future ingestion implementation.

## Out of scope for this issue

Building the actual ingestion pipeline, storage backend, or Azure Cost Management connector — this issue is investigation/design only. A follow-up implementation issue should be filed once the approach is agreed.

items.title: Research and phase-plan a financial analysis workspace: one-month challenge, licensed data and bank acceptance
items.body:
## Objective and current authorization

Research and specify an independent financial-analysis and client-materials workspace for corporate finance/M&A, capital markets, PE and VC. Independently implement useful capabilities comparable to Finster, Model ML and peers; buy licensed content where suitable. Legal-document review/drafting is outside scope.

**Updated authorization — 22 October 2026:** the owner explicitly requested a local external MVP for Monday 26 October: public-data financial scenarios, digital presentations adapted from public Rabobank references, inspection exports and page-by-page review/voice. This narrow MVP is authorized. Bank production, confidential processing, institutional-data purchases, provider outreach and tenant integration remain outside the current build scope. The original full-product plan below is preserved as a separate conditional baseline.

## Research finding

The hypothesis is substantially supported for a bounded workflow: structured financial content can be purchased through provider MCP/API/feed offerings and used with our own models, orchestration and UI. Buying content removes much collection/normalization work. Financial semantics, deterministic methods, source support, editable outputs, information barriers and bank acceptance remain substantial.

Public FactSet catalog inspection found company screening, fundamentals, estimates, debt/bond and private-market tools, while its M&A tool description specifies publicly traded targets. S&P/Kensho, LSEG, Daloopa and PitchBook are alternatives/complements, not interchangeable subscriptions. Actual contracted schemas, data quality, rights, prices and SLAs remain unverified.

[Market/peer research](https://github.com/NeoDemos/investment-banking-reimagined/blob/main/docs/MARKET_RESEARCH.md) · [Field and supplier acceptance specification](https://github.com/NeoDemos/investment-banking-reimagined/blob/main/docs/DATA_REQUIREMENTS.md) · [Bank control/evidence gates](https://github.com/NeoDemos/investment-banking-reimagined/blob/main/docs/BANK_ACCEPTANCE.md).

## One-month challenge

One sector, one subject plus 5–10 listed peers, one provider, historical/LTM comps, bounded scenario DCF, source-linked corporate briefing, fixed editable PPTX/XLSX exports, review states and frozen snapshots. Use public/synthetic or expressly permitted data; no bank-production claim.

One full-time owner with an Opus 5.5 lead and bounded Sonnet/Haiku-class workers on **one Max 20× subscription**. Month-one owner effort low/base/high: **101/128/192 hours**. Base capacity is 160 hours over 20 working days, including 32 hours reserved for rework/interruptions/usage waits. Additional specialist review is roughly 12–16 finance hours and 8–12 security/platform hours, plus provider/procurement capacity. If the owner must absorb those roles, cut scope or extend time.

Illustrative kickoff **26 October 2026**, stretch demonstration **20 November 2026**; neither is an authorized start or commitment. A 6–8-week fallback is appropriate if access/semantics/review consume contingency. Defer DCF first while retaining complete, sourced comps and reviewed outputs.

## Subscription and costs

Max 20× is listed at $200/month with shared five-hour and weekly limits; subagents share those limits. There is no verified token allowance permitting a guaranteed subscription-month forecast. Current Anthropic documentation also lists a separately claimed, eligibility-dependent $200 monthly API credit; it does not extend interactive Claude Code usage. Owner eligibility is unverified. The bank-product reference route requires approved API/cloud processing and a separate runtime budget. For this owner-authorized personal external demo only, current Anthropic documentation permits the installed `claude -p` interface through plan limits; this is not bank approval, ZDR, unlimited capacity or shared credential access.

A narrow demonstration is estimated at 1–2 subscription months; expanded analyst pilot around 2–3+ months; favorable bank-assessment candidate 3–6 months, conservatively 6–12+ pending actual bank requirements; broad competitor-style scope 12–24+ months. These are scope-based elapsed estimates. Data rights, hosting, runtime, finance/security reviewers, independent tests, contracts, operations and maintenance are additional and mostly unquoted.

[Full delivery/capacity/cost assumptions](https://github.com/NeoDemos/investment-banking-reimagined/blob/main/docs/DELIVERY_PLAN.md). Earlier token envelopes in TOKEN_ESTIMATE.md are uncalibrated processed-token illustrations, not throughput or delivery predictions.

## GitHub execution plan

[Project: task plan, execution board and delivery roadmap](https://github.com/users/NeoDemos/projects/3) · [Dated task register](https://github.com/NeoDemos/investment-banking-reimagined/blob/main/docs/planning/TASK_REGISTER.md).

37 planned child tasks, five milestones, native blocking dependencies, per-task start/target dates, low/base/high owner effort, proposed executor, specialist capacity, external wait and acceptance criteria. The original 37-task acceptance scope remains uncompleted; the accelerated Monday MVP is tracked separately and must not be mistaken for bank or full valuation acceptance. Dates beyond month one are conditional planning windows and must be rebaselined for gates, bank holidays and leave.

items.body:
<!-- CANONICAL_USER_GATE_DOCUMENT_FIRST_20261003 -->
## Canonical user-gate document-first execution rule — 2026-10-03

When the owner asks to run the project's CLI/Feature/Scenario test, Surface Reconciliation, FULL_USER_E2E, or an equivalent named user gate, the request means **execute the repository's canonical contract exactly as written**, not improvise a substitute test.

Mandatory order:

1. Resolve the target repository and active worktree.
2. Resolve the exact canonical contract path for the requested gate.
3. **Read the entire current contract before starting the gate.** Do not begin by inventing a checklist, running a convenient wrapper, replaying a script, searching unrelated repos, or substituting a generic test suite.
4. Understand and preserve the contract's semantics: persona roles, black-box/public-surface boundary, scenario inventory, prohibited actions, evidence/ledger rules, finding-accumulation rule, cleanup, restart/invalidation rules, and PASS/FAIL/BLOCKED criteria.
5. Then execute every applicable contract requirement directly. For user-role lanes, **ChatGPT itself acts as the user/operator/admin and follows the public surface**. Wrappers, shell/Python scripts, CI, unit/integration suites, browser automation, parsers, and scanners are supporting evidence/orchestration only; they cannot impersonate the user lane or turn their PASS into a user-gate PASS.
6. If a scripted/harness shortcut conflicts with the canonical contract, the contract wins and the shortcut must not be used as a substitute.
7. If the gate produces bugs/findings, finish the complete safe discovery pass, freeze the finding set, batch-fix, then restart the complete gate from the beginning on the new exact candidate. Repeat until clean with no fixed pass limit.
8. Apply the same document-first rule independently to FULL_USER_E2E after Surface/CLI reconciliation converges.

A run is invalid for roadmap/release closure if ChatGPT did not first execute from the current canonical contract or if primary user evidence was replaced by a wrapper/scripted replay.

---

<!-- RELEASE_QUALITY_CLOSED_LOOP_20261003 -->
## Release-quality closed loop — 2026-10-03

This roadmap uses **defect-convergence, not a fixed number of test passes**, as the terminal release rule.

1. Finish the roadmap/function scope far enough to enter release closure.
2. Run the complete **Surface Reconciliation** gate. For CLI products this is the exhaustive **CLI ↔ Feature ↔ Scenario** audit; for browser/other products use the equivalent complete public-surface/capability scenario audit. **ChatGPT directly acts as the applicable real User/Operator/Admin persona.**
3. Finish the complete discovery pass before remediation, retain all findings, then batch-fix every actionable in-scope product/UX/contract defect. A severity downgrade alone is not closure.
4. If the product/public surface/contract changed, start the complete Surface Reconciliation gate again from the beginning on the new exact candidate. **Repeat with no fixed pass limit until the complete run finds zero new or unresolved actionable defects and has zero mandatory FAIL/PARTIAL/BLOCKED results.**
5. Only then run the complete **Full User E2E** gate with real user journeys, state changes, read-back/effective runtime truth, failures/recovery, and cleanup. Finish the whole run, batch-fix every actionable defect, then rerun the complete gate from the beginning. **Repeat with no fixed pass limit until clean.**
6. If Full User E2E remediation changes the public surface or its contract, return to Surface Reconciliation and reconverge before closure.
7. Only when the latest complete Surface Reconciliation and Full User E2E are both clean on the **same exact HEAD** may the roadmap declare `PRODUCT_QUALITY_CLOSURE=PASS`.
8. Then and only then: **candidate freeze → release-specific upgrade/migration/platform/performance qualification → final exact-HEAD CI/regression → artifact/hash/SBOM/provenance/manifest/attestation → owner acceptance/release authorization → immutable release/publication → post-release smoke**.

Final CI, SBOM/provenance, candidate freeze, tag/publication, or other downstream release work must not displace either defect-convergence loop while it can still change the candidate. Scripts/CI/harnesses are supporting evidence and never substitute for ChatGPT's direct user-role execution.

## 2026-10-03 — Verified Continuous Engineering Memory roadmap (canonical)

This section supersedes older post-v0.1.0 memory/context candidates where they conflict.

### Product goal

Atlas should reduce repeated owner explanation and repeated context reconstruction across ChatGPT/Codex/other approved AI clients without becoming a generic chat archive or duplicating Engineering System authority.

Canonical engineering truth remains GitHub/OpenSpec/code/tests/ADR/CI and Engineering System. Atlas memory is provider-neutral derived context and may never outrank current canonical state.

### Confirmed capability roadmap

1. **Automatic Task Context Bootstrap**
   - an approved AI client can ask Atlas for one bounded current task context by repository/workstream;
   - return only current high-signal state plus references for deeper retrieval;
   - no requirement for the owner to say “look in Atlas.”

2. **Continuous Canonical/Event Ingestion**
   - GitHub, Engineering System, CI/test/release/runtime evidence is reconciled automatically where an approved source/event path exists;
   - user “save this” instructions are not required for canonical machine evidence.

3. **Scoped Automatic Memory Candidate Extraction**
   - extract only bounded non-authoritative durable candidates from approved interaction/run summaries;
   - initial candidate classes: OWNER_PREFERENCE, VALIDATED_FINDING, LESSON_LEARNED, RUN_SUMMARY, FUTURE_IDEA, REFERENCE_FACT;
   - never promote extracted conversation content directly to canonical engineering truth.

4. **Provenance/Citation-bound Memory**
   - memories backed by repository/ADR/spec/evidence retain source identity/revision/digest where available;
   - raw secret-bearing/source bodies are not copied into durable memory merely to support citation.

5. **Recall-time Current-state Revalidation**
   - citation-backed memory is revalidated against current canonical state before being presented as CURRENT;
   - stale, contradicted, unavailable or superseded memory is explicit and cannot silently override current state.

6. **Dedup + Consolidation + Supersession + TTL**
   - equivalent memories converge instead of growing unbounded;
   - newer facts may supersede older facts while history remains attributable;
   - TTL/decay is type-specific rather than one global lifetime.

7. **Progressive / JIT Context Retrieval**
   - first response is a small bounded context summary/index;
   - deeper evidence/memory is fetched only when the task needs it;
   - do not inject the whole memory store into every model prompt.

8. **User Review / Correct / Forget / Pin**
   - the owner can inspect and correct derived/personal memory, forget it, or pin intentionally durable items;
   - these controls do not mutate canonical GitHub/Engineering System truth indirectly.

9. **Memory & Context Effectiveness Evals**
   - measure important-memory recall, stale/irrelevant injection, duplicate rate, repeated-owner-explanation count, injected context size/cost and downstream first-pass task success;
   - promote retrieval heuristics only from measured evidence.

### Explicit non-goals

- no full raw ChatGPT transcript archive as the primary memory plane;
- no automatic learning of engineering procedures/rules that duplicates Engineering System/AGENTS/runbooks/skills;
- no external Mem0/Zep/Letta SaaS runtime dependency;
- no mandatory new graph database or vector database while existing Atlas retrieval is sufficient;
- no AI-extracted memory automatically promoted to architecture/security/release authority;
- no whole-memory prompt injection;
- no provider-specific memory silo as source of truth.

### Implementation order

**M1 — Context Bootstrap + Revalidation + JIT retrieval**
- first implementation priority;
- reuse existing registry/retrieval/lifecycle/Engineering System evidence surfaces;
- add a bounded provider-neutral task-context contract and read-only CLI/MCP/UI parity where useful.

**M2 — Continuous ingestion + candidate memory store**
- event/source reconciliation plus bounded candidate model, authority/scope separation and secret-safe persistence.

**M3 — Consolidation / temporal validity / TTL**
- dedup, supersession, expiry and recall-time validity state.

**M4 — User memory controls**
- inspect/correct/forget/pin for non-canonical memory.

**M5 — Memory effectiveness evals**
- use real DataRelay workloads before adaptive retrieval/ranking expansion.

### Relationship to existing roadmap

- Engineering System remains methodology/execution/release/security authority.
- #59 Personal Knowledge remains a non-authoritative source class and is reused rather than replaced.
- #261 Engineering System evidence federation is an input surface.
- #55/#56 remain measurement-gated and may later consume memory/context effectiveness evidence.
- #76 stays DEFERRED; context compression/provider-specific quota optimization is not part of M1.
- #254 Weave Router remains future/optional and does not block this roadmap.
- #268 production rollout remains a separate protected production-effect track and does not block non-production implementation of M1.

ChatGPT may remain an independent supervisory/audit surface, but routine orchestration must not depend on a human repeatedly writing prompts or manually sending `계속`.

### Capability sequence

Implement this in the following order. Do not skip directly to a large agent fleet.

1. **Executable Work Packet**
   - treat the canonical Work Packet as a machine-executable specification, not only a handoff note;
   - include bounded acceptance criteria, allowed effects, required deterministic tests/evidence, retry policy, budget/policy limits, and HUMAN_REQUIRED conditions;
   - GitHub remains canonical; transient model conversations remain non-canonical.

2. **Autonomous Planner**
   - derive a bounded execution plan/graph from the Work Packet plus Engineering System policy;
   - prefer deterministic templates and typed transitions over unrestricted free-form planning;
   - verify repository, branch, exact HEAD, clean/expected worktree, and canonical packet before dispatch.

3. **Worker Runtime**
   - treat Cursor and future providers as workers, not conversational authorities;
   - reuse bounded project-local worker/session state where safe instead of creating a new conversation for every packet;
   - preserve host/worktree isolation and never allow one project's worker to mutate another project's worktree.

4. **Trust Plane**
   - separate machine-verifiable completion from model judgment;
   - deterministic gates include exact HEAD, worktree state, tests, CI, provenance, policy, required artifacts, and stale/duplicate suppression;
   - semantic audit runs only after deterministic preconditions are satisfied;
   - a worker claiming PASS is never sufficient by itself.

5. **Automatic REWORK loop**
   - deterministic or audit failures become one bounded consolidated finding set;
   - safely redispatch the same workstream without human prompt rewriting;
   - retry only within explicit bounded policy;
   - repeated failure, ambiguity, security-sensitive decisions, credentials, destructive effects, or owner approvals escalate to `HUMAN_REQUIRED`.

6. **Dependency Graph**
   - replace simple linear queue chaining with explicit dependency/readiness relationships;
   - serialize conflicting worktree/resource mutations;
   - allow independent work to run concurrently only when dependencies, isolation, and budget permit.

7. **Multi-agent concurrency**
   - increase worker count only after a single Work Packet can reliably complete the full closed loop;
   - concurrency is a throughput optimization, not the foundation of correctness;
   - enforce global/project concurrency, budget, rate, and blast-radius limits.

### First mandatory milestone

Before scaling concurrency, Atlas must prove one real Work Packet can progress without further human prompting through:

```text
READY
  ↓
RUNNING
  ↓
VERIFYING
  ├─ PASS → COMPLETED / next ready packet
  ├─ REWORK → bounded redispatch → RUNNING
  └─ HUMAN_REQUIRED → owner
```

Exit criterion:

> One bounded Work Packet can go from READY to COMPLETED, including at least one possible REWORK cycle, using canonical GitHub state, deterministic gates, bounded independent audit, and safe worker redispatch without Rick or ChatGPT manually rewriting the next prompt.

### Relationship to current Atlas work

- **Issue #47** is the immediate bridge toward this architecture: host-local worker execution, durable project descriptors, exact-HEAD audit checkpoints, bounded audit providers, automatic REWORK redispatch, and GitHub-backed state.
- **Queued Work Packet chaining** remains the near-term linear predecessor to a true dependency graph.
- **Engineering System** remains the canonical methodology/policy source. Atlas consumes and executes those contracts; it must not fork a separate methodology.
- Existing functional-core and production-dogfood work remains valid. This control-plane direction should reduce manual orchestration across those phases rather than create a disconnected side project.

### Non-goals / safety constraints

- Do not make model conversation history canonical.
- Do not treat model self-reported PASS as completion evidence.
- Do not auto-cross owner approval, credential, destructive, release, deploy, or other HUMAN_REQUIRED gates.
- Do not create a general-purpose workflow engine unrelated to engineering control.
- Do not increase agent count before deterministic trust/idempotency/recovery behavior is proven.
- Do not duplicate Engineering System primitives when an adopted canonical primitive already exists.

### User-facing target

Routine operation should converge toward:

```text

Atlas:
resolve packet → validate state → plan → execute → verify
→ rework automatically if bounded and safe
→ audit → update GitHub → continue to next ready packet

Owner notification:
✅ COMPLETED
⚠️ HUMAN_REQUIRED
❌ BLOCKED
```

The key optimization is therefore not "better prompts". It is moving repeatable intent, context, policy, verification, retry, dependency, and evidence into durable system contracts so prompts become a thin control surface rather than the workflow itself.


## Model-Aware Instruction Governance — 2026-09-25

Atlas should operationalize the Engineering System Model-Aware Prompt / Instruction Hygiene contract. Atlas does **not** define prompting methodology; it discovers managed instruction surfaces, invokes the canonical audit/eval contracts, preserves evidence, and coordinates safe adoption.

### Target lifecycle

```text
model / harness / instruction change
        ↓
Atlas resolves affected repositories + instruction surfaces
        ↓
Engineering System prompt-surface inventory
        ↓
read-only instruction audit
        ↓
bounded proposed diff
        ↓
behavior eval / deterministic policy checks
        ↓
   ┌───────────────┬────────────────┐
   │               │                │
NO_CHANGE      CANDIDATE_PASS   HUMAN_REQUIRED
   │               │                │
checkpoint      canary / PR       owner decision
                   ↓
             measured comparison
                   ↓
             managed adoption
```

### Atlas capability sequence

#### AIG-0 — Consume, do not fork, the Engineering System contract

Atlas must consume the canonical Engineering System definitions for:
- prompt/instruction surface inventory;
- finding classifications;
- behavior-eval requirements;
- provider/model profile identity;
- rollout/canary evidence.

No Atlas-specific duplicate methodology or competing prompt policy.

#### AIG-1 — Repository instruction inventory

For registered projects, Atlas should be able to identify behavior-bearing surfaces such as:
- `AGENTS.md`;
- managed Cursor/provider rules;
- skills/hooks;
- Work Packet templates;
- tool/MCP descriptions;
- repository-owned prompt/request templates;
- approved model/reasoning/tool profiles.

Store provenance and hashes/revisions, not secret-bearing raw prompt history when unnecessary.

#### AIG-2 — Trigger and scope resolution

Instruction audit should be eligible when one of these bounded triggers occurs:
- approved model/provider/harness version changes;
- Engineering System managed instruction baseline changes;
- a behavior-bearing instruction surface changes;
- repeated eval/telemetry evidence suggests instruction-induced waste or regression;
- owner explicitly requests an audit.

A trigger must resolve to a bounded repository/workstream/model profile. Do not launch organization-wide scans by default.

#### AIG-3 — Read-only audit worker

Use a dedicated bounded audit provider/worker to:
- classify load-bearing vs candidate cruft;
- identify duplicate/contradictory/model-obsolete instructions;
- return normalized findings and proposed diffs;
- cite current model/provider guidance when the audit depends on it;
- never directly modify repository policy in the initial phase.

The audit worker is advisory evidence, not authority.

#### AIG-4 — Eval + Trust Plane integration

Before a proposed instruction change can advance:
- run the Engineering System behavior-eval set appropriate to the repository/task;
- run deterministic security/policy checks;
- compare exact outcome, retries, tokens/cost, latency, and human intervention;
- bind evidence to exact repository revision + instruction candidate + model/harness profile;
- require independent verification at the trust level dictated by risk.

Atlas must fail closed when the evidence is stale, missing, cross-model, or cross-revision.

#### AIG-5 — Canary and managed adoption

For a candidate that passes offline eval:
1. apply only through the normal branch/PR/Work Packet path;
2. canary on one selected repository/profile;
3. observe measured task outcomes;
4. compare with the previous baseline;
5. either promote through Engineering System managed rollout or REWORK/rollback.

No direct default-branch rewrite. No bulk repository mutation.

#### AIG-6 — Continuous hygiene as maintenance graph

After the single-packet autonomous control loop is proven, instruction hygiene can become a low-frequency maintenance node in the Atlas dependency graph:

```text
model/harness release or managed baseline change
        ↓
affected-surface discovery
        ↓
audit
        ↓
eval
        ↓
candidate PR / no-op / HUMAN_REQUIRED
```

This should be cheap when nothing changed and must not consume expensive model calls repeatedly for the same exact revision/profile.

### Relationship to the Autonomous Engineering Control Plane

Model-Aware Instruction Governance fits between **Trust Plane** and **managed maintenance**, not before the core closed loop.

Priority order remains:

1. finish the current #47 bridge;
2. prove one real Work Packet can close `READY → RUNNING → VERIFYING → REWORK/PASS → COMPLETED` without prompt rewriting;
3. add dependency/readiness graph behavior;
4. then activate model-aware instruction governance as a recurring maintenance capability;
5. only then consider broad multi-agent scale-out.

This prevents prompt optimization from becoming a side project that delays the core autonomous control plane.

### Human interaction target

Routine case:

```text
Atlas:
"Model/harness profile changed.
12 managed instruction surfaces checked.
8 KEEP_LOAD_BEARING
3 NO_CHANGE
1 candidate simplification passed eval and canary.
PR ready for normal governance."
```

Escalation case:

```text
⚠️ HUMAN_REQUIRED
Candidate removes a policy-bearing rule or produces mixed eval results.
No mutation performed.
```

### Exit criterion

Atlas can detect a model/harness or managed-instruction change, produce a bounded evidence-backed cleanup proposal, prove it through Engineering System eval/trust gates, and route it through normal PR/adoption governance **without treating prompt text or model self-report as authority**.

## Provider Capacity Broker / Quota-aware Scheduling — 2026-09-25

Atlas should eventually orchestrate not only **which worker performs a task**, but also **which approved provider/model/runtime capacity should execute it**. The reference idea is quota/reset-aware routing such as openllms, but Atlas must implement a stricter **policy-aware Capacity Broker** rather than a subscription-limit maximizer.

### Target architecture

```text
Work Packet / execution node
        ↓
Engineering System eligibility policy
        ↓
Atlas Provider Capacity Broker
        ↓
approved candidate routes
   ├─ Cursor/native runtime
   ├─ Claude native/approved SDK/API
   ├─ OpenAI API / approved native runtime
   ├─ Codex/reviewer provider
   └─ future local/enterprise providers
        ↓
route scoring
(capability + policy + trust + cost + quota/reset + latency)
        ↓
selected worker/provider
        ↓
normalized evidence
        ↓
Trust Plane
```

### Broker responsibilities

For each eligible provider/model/runtime route, Atlas may track:
- provider + model/profile;
- usage mode;
- policy eligibility;
- health / cooldown / throttling;
- remaining quota or credit where observable;
- reset horizon where observable;
- estimated marginal cost;
- latency / queue depth;
- task capability compatibility;
- current Work Packet budget;
- host/session/worktree availability;
- recent failure state;
- whether model/provider transition would invalidate cached context or require re-validation.

### Routing strategies

Atlas should support policy-bounded strategies such as:

- **CAPABILITY_FIRST**
- **COST_FIRST**
- **RESET_SOON**
- **BALANCED**
- **FAILOVER**
- **STEWARDSHIP**

`STEWARDSHIP` should become the preferred long-term policy: choose the best approved route using capability, current cost, expiring capacity/reset horizon, latency, trust requirements, and project budget.

### Policy gate before scoring

Candidate generation must occur in this order:

```text
all configured routes
    ↓
provider-policy eligibility
    ↓
task capability compatibility
    ↓
trust / verification compatibility
    ↓
budget / blast-radius / WIP admission
    ↓
capacity scoring
```

A route with attractive quota but `UNKNOWN` or `DENIED` policy status is not eligible.

### Failover semantics

Failover must be explicit and attributable.

Example:

```text
Cursor / model A
   ↓ rate/quota failure
compatible route check
   ↓
Claude / model B
   ↓
new provider identity recorded
   ↓
fresh deterministic evidence
   ↓
independent audit as required
```

Rules:
- no silent provider/model switching;
- no reuse of stale semantic audit across materially different provider/model paths;
- no provider switch that bypasses tool, permission, or worktree constraints;
- repeated failover exhaustion becomes `BLOCK` or `HUMAN_REQUIRED`.

### Evidence contract

Every execution node should be able to retain bounded metadata such as:

```text
IMPLEMENTER_PROVIDER=
IMPLEMENTER_MODEL=
IMPLEMENTER_PROFILE=
USAGE_MODE=
ROUTING_STRATEGY=
ROUTE_REASON=
CAPACITY_SNAPSHOT_REF=
WORK_PACKET_BUDGET=
SUBJECT_HEAD=
```

Independent audit records its own provider/model identity separately.

Canonical GitHub state should contain only bounded attribution/evidence references, not raw OAuth/session tokens or provider secrets.

### Reference implementation intake

Treat projects such as `openllms` as reference implementations for:
- reset-aware scheduling;
- quota discovery;
- cooldown/health handling;
- failover;
- weighted route scoring;
- unified provider abstraction.

Do not adopt any consumer-subscription credential/session mechanism merely because a reference implementation supports it. Only approved provider-native/API/enterprise usage modes are eligible for Atlas production routing.

### Relationship to existing Atlas roadmap

This capability depends on earlier foundations:

1. **#47 bridge**
2. **single Work Packet autonomous closure**
3. **dependency/readiness graph**
4. **provider capability adapters**
5. **Provider Capacity Broker**
6. **Model-Aware Instruction/Harness maintenance**
7. **measured multi-agent concurrency**

The broker may later improve concurrency scheduling, but it must not be used to justify broad multi-agent scale-out before the Trust Plane and dependency graph are reliable.

### Initial implementation slice

When activated, start small:

1. synthetic provider descriptors only;
2. deterministic policy eligibility evaluator;
3. deterministic route scoring tests;
4. one approved real route plus one approved fallback route;
5. record selection evidence and failover behavior;
6. no consumer-subscription pooling in the first production slice.

### Example operator outcome

```text

Eligible routes:
- GPT-5.6 Sol API: ALLOWED, high capability, paid
- Codex fallback: ALLOWED, lower marginal cost, available
```

or:


### Exit criterion

<!-- beta-tracking -->
# The tortoise path — **four stages, in this order** (owner, 2026-11-09)

**Owner ruling, verbatim:** *"1. get to private beta (so all the issues needed for that, also ensuring they're labelled p0 or p1 so the auto dispatch prioritises them) 2. any issues and work needed for the venture studio design partner (they record meetings and feed it to an extractor that needs to work for meeting transcripts…) 3. complete any remaining issues that will improve longmem eval directly … so that means also making sure they're marked in the tracking issue as the next wave(s) following private-beta ones 4. run benchmarks for longmemeeval and also for reasoning (the gbrain ones we already setup)"*

**And the ordering constraint that governs stage 4:** *"the issues we filed that affect longmem eval need to be finished before the benchmark, as otherwise we're benchmarking over something that we know is broken and know how it's broken and just needs a fix from us."*

**So: wave 3 gates wave 4.** The benchmark is a *measurement of a known-good state*, not a way to discover the state.

---

## ⛔ STAGE 1 — PRIVATE BETA: the set, stated so it can be counted

The beta is the P0/P1 set. **Re-measured 2026-11-13 by label: P0 6 · P1 23 = 29 open** (this line previously read *P0 10 · P1 17 = 27*; the P0 half was 4 CLOSED issues and the P1 half was short). Each is either *beta work*, *a decision waiting on the owner*, or *mis-filed into the wrong wave* — the table says which.

### P0 — 6 open
| issue | what it actually is | wave |

| `#7879` | **epic** the Postgres record — 23/36 children closed | 1 (children) |

| `#10977` | tracking: making the hosted graph usable — "the three things nobody owns" | 1 |
| `#11609` | **the live surface is 72 tools / 150 methods against an approved 27 / 40** | 1 |
| `#12047` | **P0 NEW — entity resolution does not exist and the queue reports a false clean.** `list_dedup_candidates(candidate_type='entity')` returns `[]` from a hard-coded stub, so "are there duplicate entities?" answers **none** when the truth is **cannot answer**; `#783` was closed COMPLETED on an acceptance criterion naming `entity_resolver.py`, a file that has never existed in git. Measured damage: one person under five Subject names, one role under three, documents filed as roles, `holdsRole` has zero edges in both hosted graphs, and `default`'s 872 Subjects are 870× kind `other` (453 of them `issue:<repo>#<n>`). **Blocks the graph re-file** — that work multiplies entities on every item | 1 |
| `#12477` | **P0 NEW — the hosted API times out on every request while its health check reports 2/2 passing.** Measured 2026-11-13: `GET /v1/health` / 1-row `GET /v1/points` / `POST /v1/objects` all time out (30-45 s), MCP returns `-32009 wait budget exceeded`, an in-process write hung past 300 s — while the control plane answers instantly and `flyctl` reports `2/2 checks passing` on a `shared-cpu-2x:4096MB` box that restarted at 17:53Z, with vector/FTS queries blowing a 500 ms budget at 1.5-3.9 s. **Blocks the private-beta dogfood** — the clean-graph migration cannot start until a write completes | 1 |

> **📌 Board edit 2026-11-11** — added `#11089` (P1, the `#5090` capstone) and `#4333` (P2, deliberately out of the beta set) to this table, and refreshed the `#5090` row. **The counts in this section are a MEASUREMENT STAMP, not a live figure** — they were measured by another lane on 2026-11-11 and several rows have since closed; re-measure before quoting them.

### P1 — 23 open, split by what they are *for*
| issue | subject | wave |
|---|---|---|
| `#5333` | design(extractor): the destructive half of G5 — may any pass remove/archive an existing fact? **DECIDED, needs the capstone** | 1 |
| `#10360` | extractor: no mechanical enforcement of the verbatim state-value guarantee | 1 |
| `#11002` | extractor: the eight steps actually — bounded re-narrate, S4 gap-filling misplaced. ⚠️ **Its blocker is now cleared:** the ADD-capable stage landed (`#11534` → `#11554`), which is exactly the successor S4's removal requires. The owner question was **withdrawn** 2026-11-07 — the repo's own ordering obligation decides it (build the successor, prove the merge property, then delete `run_s4`) | 1 |
| ✅ **`#11237` — LANDED 2026-11-10 (`#11548`)** | extractor: the relations channel's **write path**. It also **closed the wiring gap** I reported on 2026-11-07: `tortoise/relation_write.py` now calls `plan_hierarchy_edges` (`:53`, `:589`, `:631`) and writes the pack-declared structural hierarchy edges, so a capture **can** produce them. `#11001`'s "no production call site" finding is **false on today's main** and was corrected there and here | 1 |

| `#11534` | extractor: the ADD-capable stage must reach PARTIAL gaps | 1 |

Bar proposed: **unbound-and-unexplained declared relations = 0**, denominator 42 (36 relations + 6 hierarchy paths), with the `written` column *reported beside* — not the bar, because `A1` already measures the written graph | 1 | ✅ **implemented in PR #11688** (head `41550c65a9`, MERGEABLE): `E6` is required for the **record** (`REQUIRED_CRITERIA`), recognised by the scorer (`RECOGNISED_CRITERIA`), and **not** part of the close — `V9`/`--require-green` stays `E1..E5`, per the `A1`–`A5` precedent (*"a registration may not turn a row into a gate before anyone has measured it"*). ⚠️ **The head's checks are mostly `cancelled`** (a push landed while CI was running, which cancels the queue position) — it needs a **fresh run** before the rail will accept it |
| `#11695` | **nothing can emit an `E6` verdict**, so no **scored run can produce a complete record** (`E6` is required by `REQUIRED_CRITERIA`). ⚠️ **Not** a closing blocker: the close is five rows. The fix is a producer reading the existing `docs/evidence/11083/pack-relation-census.json` — it must **not** re-open the closing set | 1 |
| `#11000` | packs: **`subclassOf` never widens — the expansion loop drops the parent** | 1 (**a pack that cannot widen connects nothing**) |
| `#4051` | quota: the commit lane's only org-limit gate was the session cap | 1 (revenue guard) |
| `#10175` | ops(capture): the hosted capture cap is HELD deliberately — never override | 1 (standing rule, not work) |
| `#8486` | **Run LongMemEval-S** (never executed; no comparable number exists) | **4 — this IS the benchmark** |
| `#2513` | multi-session retrieval evidence surface — the dominant QA loss (53 % of misses) | **3** |
| `#8488` | context-enriched embeddings **+ BM25 lexical** — the two signals we lack | **3** |

| **`#4333`** | **storage-architecture owner** — node volume + true per-node cost. **`P2-moderate`, so it is deliberately OUTSIDE the beta set** (the set is P0/P1) and is listed here only so nobody re-files it as a `#5090` child: it is the *owner* of the storage question, not a child of the vector layer | **3 (not beta)** |
| `#11395` | tracking(5090): the S3 vector-removal / surface-approval call has no successor issue | **3** |
| `#10656` | **credential provenance (REOPENED 2026-11-11** — it had been closed COMPLETED by a PR that never touched it; all three claims re-measured true at `origin/main` `372f926cd9`: `:1506` writes `<cwd>/.tortoise`, `:2133` ranks it above the global store, `:1662-3` is a non-atomic `write_text`+`chmod`) — plaintext key in a working tree, at a precedence that shadows the user-global store. **Both halves are lane decisions, not owner ones** (contradiction test 2026-11-11: no recorded decision requires the cwd location — it arrived with `61f32e1ce4` and `#1708` moved `signup`/`recover` to the global store without ever ruling on `init`). (a) atomic write + FIFO guard **dispatched**; (c) write to the user-global store with `<cwd>/.tortoise` kept read-compatible **decided and queued behind (a)** — same function, so one lane at a time | 1 |
| `#11912` | **`doctor` cannot see half the product** — 8 local checks, **zero** credential or hosted ones, so a revoked key reads `8 pass, 0 fail` (measured on this box). #10655 built `config show` (the offline reporter); this is the first-run surface that should REACH it. **Dispatched** | 1 |
| `#12060` | **P1 NEW — per-kind guards: redirect mis-filed writes with an AX contract, not a refusal.** Every core kind gets a deterministic, token-free guard: accept / **redirect** / refuse — a guard may never refuse a case whose right home is known. Shipped with a fixed AX message shape (what changed, why, the exact override, how to undo) plus a `kind_redirect` field so agents branch on data not English, an `intent="as_declared"` override that records that it fired, and redirect counters. **Cross-pack resolved:** targets are core / own namespace / `depends_on` only; `pack validate` refuses a bad reference (fail at install, not at write); at write time a missing target makes the guard **abstain** — never reject, because a write must not depend on which packs are installed. Packs declare guards **optionally**; `_template` carries a worked example. **Prevents the re-file from re-creating the 453 issue-as-Subject + 870 `other` nodes** | 1 |

### ✅ DEFINITION — UNCHANGED, AND NOT MINE TO MOVE (owner, 2026-11-09)
> **"the cut line depends on what's needed not a fixed number — focus on advancing towards the private-beta while I handle what 'done' is and my definition hasn't changed."**

**So: beta ships when the open `P0-blocker` + `P1-severe` issues are merged and closed.
