items.title: Hypothesis 1: experience cards as evidence, not rules
items.body:
## What this is

A product hypothesis we can implement as a small, isolated script pack and then measure.

It does **not** touch Architecture v2, Google Memory Bank, the DSPy compiler, OpenSpec components, or the M1–M3 lab pipeline. Those keep running. This is a standalone slice: chat in → card out → later agent sees a recommendation.

Spec (arriving in a follow-up PR): `standalone/h1-experience-cards/`.

---

## The business picture

A shop runs several customer-facing agents. Customers are mostly anonymous. What one agent learns dies when the chat closes. The next agent, on another channel, solves the same jam from scratch.

Hypothesis 1: after each closed chat we extract a short **experience card** and, if it earns the right, show it to the next agent as **evidence** (“this has worked when the request looked like this”), never as a **rule** (“always do this”).

### Walkthrough

Customer to Agent A: *ordered size 42, got 41, want an exchange, tag already cut off.*

Policy blocks exchanges without a tag. Agent A finds a workaround: photo of the defect + order id → warehouse accepts it as a defect, not a change-of-mind. Chat ends.

We do **not** keep the transcript as memory. We keep a card:

- **problem_shape** — exchange, wrong size, tag missing
- **constraint** — no-tag exchange is closed by policy
- **unlock** — reclassify as defect when photo + order id exist
- **what_worked** — the steps that actually ran
- **receipt** — source chat, agent/tenant, time, allowed scope (this shop / this vertical)

No customer identity on the card.

Next day a different customer asks Agent B the same shape of question. Agent B does not get an order. It gets a packet:

> Similar cases in this shop: exchange without a tag is blocked. One workaround that worked: reclassify as defect with photo + order id. This is not policy. Check the current warehouse rule first.

Money movement, account changes, and PII actions never ride on the card alone.

---

## Why this is worth trying

1. The second agent does not re-discover the same dead end.
2. The knowledge survives a model swap, a prompt rewrite, and an agent leaving.
3. Anonymous traffic stops being a knowledge leak: we remember what was learned, not who asked.

This is not a universal brain. It is a shift-handover note inside one line of support.

---

## What we already know vs what this pack must measure

Already measured on ABCD (see #6 / BON-41), used here as a constraint, not as a dependency:

- Matching on customer wording, inside one vertical, can hit the frozen false-friend bar without embeddings.
- A five-field card compresses a chat ~4× with the current schema, not 10×.
- A clean win/loss label is missing on most real chats, so promotion cannot wait on “outcome”.

Still unproven — this pack exists so we can get numbers:

- Does the card keep enough of the chat to be useful?
- Does showing the packet change what the next agent does?
- Does a naïve “seen twice → publish” rule promote junk?

---

## Scope of Hypothesis 1

In:

- extract a card from a finished dialogue (LLM prompt, frozen schema)
- store it `private` by default
- match later dialogues with a cheap lexical key, same scope only
- promote to `shared` after K independent confirmations (default K=2)
- serve as evidence, with a frozen serve prompt
- expire on “wrong / stale” feedback or a hard age cap

Out:

- cross-vertical sharing
- source-reputation scores
- using the card as an instruction
- any existing repo service (Memory Bank, compiler, ranker, graph)

---

## Implementation contract

The spec lists the scripts. Code comes next, in the same isolated folder. Then we (or the lab) drop a pile of dialogues on it and report:

- cards extracted / rejected
- private vs shared split
- match precision on a held-out slice
- how often a served packet would have named the unlock that actually happened

That last number is the usefulness figure this hypothesis owes us.

## Definition of done for this issue

- [ ] Spec merged under `standalone/h1-experience-cards/`
- [ ] Scripts implemented against that spec (follow-up PR)
- [ ] A first fixture set of dialogues run through the pack
- [ ] A short numbers note: extract yield, promote yield, packet usefulness

labels.name: needs-decision

items.body:
# WhatsApp Feature Parity & Alignment Campaign — meta-issue

**Campaign: bring Hermes's WhatsApp surface into full bloom and alignment with the official WhatsApp Business Platform Cloud API and the bridge backends Hermes actually runs (whatsapp-web.js / Baileys / Business API).**

Every WhatsApp issue, subissue, and PR in this tracker is interlocked here. One campaign, one canonical view, one reconciliation.

## Why this campaign

- **456 open issues** touch the WhatsApp surface (search union: `whatsapp in:title,body`; 77 carry `platform/whatsapp` — measured 2026-08-05).
- **388 open PRs** mention WhatsApp in title/body (search API total_count, 2026-08-05).
- The adapter (`plugins/platforms/whatsapp/adapter.py`, **1,918 lines** @ 0577116f83) is a **multi-backend bridge**: WhatsApp Business API (Meta verification), whatsapp-web.js, Baileys. At 96% of the 2,000-line ceiling with accumulated responsibilities (backend dispatch, pairing/QR lifecycle, messaging, media, groups, secret + Windows-subprocess hygiene) it is a **god-file in waiting**. Under-ceiling rule (Axl, 2026-08-05): *"Just because it's under 2000 lines does not mean that you are not decomposing WhatsApp. Simplify so that it never has a chance of being longer than 2000 lines."* Lane S6 decomposes it NOW so the core adapter lands far under the ceiling with structural headroom. Headroom is the Ramp's job; the ceiling is not a target.
- The surface is "conflicted at best": partial parameter coverage, silent drops, and a bridge lifecycle (QR pairing, reconnects, multi-device semantics, Node subprocess spawn hygiene) that is itself a failure surface — plus whole Cloud API feature families (message templates, interactive messages, flows, payments, catalogs, quality rating) unexpressed or half-expressed.
- Operator/community-reported pain already on record: reaction-status mirror missing (#23899), group mention gating incomplete (#7269), Node-bridge dependency contested (#7274 Neonize pure-Python path).

## Method (three-wave blind analysis + validation)

1. **Wave 1** — 5 blind analysis workers, one per domain shard (S1 core messaging, S2 Cloud API business surface, S3 groups, S4 bridge/backend lifecycle, S5 rich features), each in an isolated worktree at a pinned main. Output: gap catalog (GAP_UNSUPPORTED / GAP_PARTIAL / GAP_CONFLICTED / GAP_DOCS / GAP_BUG_TRACKED) with docs-anchor + repo-file evidence, plus per-domain adapter cluster maps. The S6 decomposition lane produces the graph-before-slice cluster map from the same wave.
2. **Wave 2** — 5 blind cross-check workers, same inputs, forbidden from reading wave-1 output. Agreement between two independent witnesses is the public-confidence bar.
3. **Wave 3** — validation: every agreed gap re-verified at current main + live tracker; issue drafts with evidence and interlock links; existing coverage → interlock, never duplicate.

## Lanes

| Lane | Domain | Status |
|---|---|---|
| S1 | Core messaging: text, media (image/document/audio/video/sticker), reactions, edits, deletes, typing, location/contact sharing | wave analysis |
| S2 | Business Cloud API surface: message templates, 24h customer-service window, webhooks, phone-number provisioning, quality rating, rate limits | wave analysis |
| S3 | Groups: metadata, mentions, admin ops, invite links, descriptions, per-sender gating (#48394 class), group controls (#7992 class) | wave analysis |
| S4 | **Bridge/backend lifecycle**: whatsapp-web.js / Baileys spawn, QR pairing, reconnect/backoff, multi-device semantics, Node subprocess hygiene (windows_detach_popen_kwargs), Neonize pure-Python path (#7274) | wave analysis |
| S5 | Rich features: interactive messages (buttons/lists), flows, payments, catalogs, ephemeral, status/broadcast | wave analysis |
| S6 | **Decomposition & headroom**: graph-before-slice extraction of adapter.py clusters (backend dispatch, bridge lifecycle, messaging, media, groups, secret + Windows hygiene) — one PR per cluster, seam identity + regression tests, suite green. Core adapter lands far under 2,000 lines: it never has a chance of crossing the ceiling | cluster maps in waves; plan issue follows agreement |

## Deliverables

- One issue per confirmed gap (this meta links them all; each issue carries `Campaign: WhatsApp` and interlock links).
- Interlock of all pre-existing WhatsApp issues/PRs into lanes (no orphan artifacts).
- `whatsapp-dev` skill shipped with Hermes (Cloud API + bridge operations, multi-backend diagnostics) — created during this campaign.
- S6 decomposition plan issue + one PR per extraction cluster (adapter.py core shrinks with headroom; seam tests + regression suite per Shard).
- Public reconciliation document per cluster/gap: members, evidence, both waves' bases, confidence, verdict.

## Standards (hard)

- **Evidence everywhere**: every issue cites the docs anchor + repo `file:line` verified at main.
- **Exact numbers**: counts measured, never "about".
- **No duplicate issues**: existing coverage → interlock with the exact number.
- **One PR per bug class** when fixes ship; suite green; attribution to the author who earned it.
- Security/data-loss findings get P1 (this surface is security-sensitive: pairing credentials, phone-number PII); everything else P2/P3.
- **No hype**: every capability claim carries a witness receipt before it may appear in public copy.

## Ledger

| Issue | Lane | Gap | PR | State |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| #80094 | S4 | `is_reconnect` cold-respawn bug | #80608 | integration-ready |

items.title: The successful-stop acknowledgement lacks #179 §1.3's trigger source, configured ceiling and customer-scope COGS (R9d)

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent

items.body:
> *This was generated by AI.*

# The successful-stop acknowledgement lacks #179 §1.3's trigger source, configured ceiling and customer-scope COGS (R9d)

## Current authority (2026-10-08) — supersedes the scope wording below where they differ

Ruled by the owner and consultant across [`6066575387`](https://github.com/ashcochrane/ubb/issues/569#issuecomment-6066575387) (preparation), [`6069593729`](https://github.com/ashcochrane/ubb/issues/569#issuecomment-6069593729) (rulings applied) and the final confirmation of 2026-10-08. **Blocked by #609** (built first). The build brief is `R9-569-IMPLEMENT-PROMPT.md`.

**Persistence and replay**
- **The snapshot.** An insert-only stop-acknowledgement snapshot is written for every recorded result, `stop` true or false, atomically with the recording that owns the idempotency key. It holds the facts actually returned.
- **The replay reads only the snapshot.** It never reconstructs anything from current counters, Task state, Pool state, configuration, Posting or the live-stop record.
- **The confirmed consequences:**
  - an original `stop: false` replays as `stop: false`, even if the customer or Task became stopped afterwards;
  - an original stop replays with its original trigger, reason, scope, bound and measured values;
  - #609's precedence is replayed exactly as originally selected.

**The fields** (on the single route, every batch item, which becomes typed, and `UBBStopRequested`)

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `trigger_source` | The mechanism that applied the stop. `charge_projection` is approved as the mechanism when a delivered fixed-price unit's Charge projection drives the stop: one mechanism value, never a reason, and no per-branch values. `usage_drawdown` is withdrawn. |
| `stop_bound_micros` | The configured monetary bound relevant to this stop. |
| `stop_measured_micros` | The actual monetary quantity assessed against that bound. |

- **What the figures mean is fixed by `stop_reason`:**
  - a Task or Subtask ceiling → COGS;
  - the customer Pool → customer charges;
  - the wallet floor → the wallet balance.
- **No "amount kind" field in v1.**
- **Not applicable means null.** For a non-monetary stop, both figures are null, never zero.
- **`task_not_active`** has `trigger_source`, bound and measured all null, and it stays outside the stop-reason registry.

**Out of this ticket's path:** the webhooks' zero is **#610**, which blocks #190. No further satellite issue is raised unless something prevents the stop acknowledgement itself from being correct.

---


**Register line R9d** ([`5767413717`](https://github.com/ashcochrane/ubb/issues/194#issuecomment-5767413717) on #194). Raised 2026-09-25 by #184's window 2, on the owner's ruling (item 1 of the batch recorded on #184). Evidence was verified against `origin/main` = **`16f4f757`** and banked in #184's bank (c) row c8 ([`5794604521`](https://github.com/ashcochrane/ubb/issues/184#issuecomment-5794604521)), bank (d) row d6 ([`5794604900`](https://github.com/ashcochrane/ubb/issues/184#issuecomment-5794604900)) and bank (g) row g4 ([`5794606036`](https://github.com/ashcochrane/ubb/issues/184#issuecomment-5794606036)).

## The governing decision

**#179 §1.3** (`docs/plans/2026-08-04-generated-runtime-contract-decision.md:140-153`) says that the stop signal carries the successful acknowledgement, so that *"a handler can log what happened without a follow-up read"*. Its seven fields include the **trigger source**, **current COGS** and the **configured ceiling**. §8 calls `trigger_source` a *"**new** field on the signal payload"*. No later document narrowed this:
- slice 5's spec (#187 `5413281395` §24) builds the signal without re-listing its fields;
- slice 6's spec (#188 `5593386744`) only froze the stop field names and added utilisation.

**The meaning of `trigger_source`, ruled 2026-09-25 (batch item 2):** it keeps its established registry meaning, *the mechanism that applied or enforced the stop* (`domain-vocabulary/concepts/tasks.yaml:88`: `usage_ingest`, `enforcement_patrol`, `parent_cascade`, `pool_crossing`, `stale_reaper`). The cause stays in `stop_reason` (concept `reason_code`). One word, one meaning.

## What `main` does instead (implementation drift)

`RecordUsageResponse` (`openapi/v1.json:5977`), and so `UBBStopRequested.result` (`ubb-sdk/ubb/exceptions.py:137-159`), carries `event_id`, `stop`, `stop_reason` and `stop_scope`. It is missing three things:
- **No trigger source.** The recording path knows it at its kill call (`usage_service.py:462`), but publishes it only on the four terminal webhooks and `CeilingEpisodeRow`.
- **No configured ceiling amount.** There is only `ceiling_remaining_micros` (clamped at zero once reached) and `ceiling_used_percentage`. The pinned figure is readable only from `StartTaskResponse` / `TaskDetailOut`.
- **No current COGS for a customer-scope stop.** `task_total_provider_cost_micros` is unit-scoped only, and it is **null on an idempotent replay** (`usage_service.py:220-225`).

`stop_context` is an untyped array, and batch items are untyped (`UsageBatchResponse.results`, `additionalProperties: true`).

## Scope

- **In:** on every recording acknowledgement that carries a stop (the single route and each batch item), and read through on `UBBStopRequested`:
  - (1) `trigger_source`, in the registry's existing meaning;
  - (2) the configured limit the stop was measured against, for each stop reason that has one: the unit's ceiling for a unit-scope stop, the pool's limit for a customer-scope stop;
  - (3) the spend measured against that limit, **including** for a customer-scope stop and on an idempotent replay.

  Where a stop reason has no monetary limit (for example `silence_window`, `absolute_deadline`, `parent_killed`), the field states that no limit applies. **It never reads as zero.** Field names ship final (ADR-0007 §3) and go through ADR-0006. The batch item schema is typed, because the new fields must appear there too.
- **Out:**
  - how the Code Builder renders them. That is #184's, and generated code must not derive or substitute these values (#184's consolidated spec §9).
  - `stop_behavior` (an SDK ticket in #184).

## Edges

- **#190 is `blocked_by` this issue**: it is a public recording contract, and it must be final before the baseline.
- **#184:** only the tickets that consume the new data wait for it: the Shell stop-metadata ticket, the Verify-stage acknowledgement rendering, and the flip, which runs Seam C's ceiling-crossing scenario. **Window 3 sets these ticket edges.** Early #184 tickets are not blocked.

## Done when

On `main`, a stop on the single and batch routes carries the trigger source, the configured limit (or an explicit statement that none applies) and the spend measured against it, for task, subtask and customer scope, including on replay. `UBBStopRequested` exposes them. Tests go through the public route and the SDK. The spec is regenerated.

items.title: Spec: future-state DocuFlow backend architecture and nine-phase migration

labels.name: ready-for-agent
labels.description: Fully specified, ready for an AFK agent

items.body:
## Problem Statement

TECHMA operates DocuFlow today as a single-company installation: one Express process serving one React SPA and one REST API, one PostgreSQL database with no tenant boundary, background work running as in-process intervals, hosting coupled to Replit sidecar credentials, and an admin-impersonation API key in the authentication path. The product vision — an all-in-one operations platform sold to service businesses and individuals — cannot be hosted on this backend: there is no Workspace boundary, no Membership or role model, no Subscription or billing machinery, no public API or webhooks, no audit or GDPR posture, and no safe way to run replicas or recover from failure. Meanwhile the existing installation carries real operational history — projects, documents, files, time entries, activity evidence, enrolled desktop devices — that must survive any change with its identity and behavior intact.

## Solution

Evolve the production backend in place into the decided target architecture: a modular monolith in one repository with separate HTTP and durable-worker runtimes, ten domain modules behind strict interfaces, shared-schema Workspace tenancy with row-level security in depth, Clerk-backed authentication with DocuFlow-owned authorization, Stripe-backed billing behind an adapter with DocuFlow-owned entitlements, three contract surfaces (web BFF, versioned desktop sync protocol, additive public `/api/v1` with signed webhooks), an S3-shaped object-storage port, a Postgres-backed jobs port with transactional-outbox events, an Intelligence module serving retrieval and gated AI, platform audit/privacy/compliance ports, and Render + Neon + Cloudflare R2 hosting in Frankfurt with an independent immutable evidence account.

The path there is the nine-phase, in-place migration recorded in ADR-0017: stabilize and de-Replit, lift hosting, stand up durable jobs, establish the Workspace seam, migrate identity, carve out modules with the data splits, expose the new contract surfaces, take billing live, and retire legacy surfaces — every phase made of expand/contract deploys with verifiers, temporary flags, and rollback paths, preserving every legacy ID, contract, and running Timer.

## User Stories

1. As a prospective customer, I want to start a trial workspace without a card and receive the complete product, so that I can evaluate DocuFlow before paying.
2. As a workspace owner, I want my Workspace to be the sole boundary for data, members, policy, and subscription, so that my records never mix with another tenant's.
3. As an individual user, I want a one-member Workspace with the same product, so that I can add members later without migrating to a different product type.
4. As a workspace owner, I want ownership transfer required before my membership can lose access, so that a workspace always has an ultimate authority.
5. As a workspace administrator, I want to invite, add, edit, archive, restore, and remove members, so that access always matches current responsibility.
6. As a workspace administrator, I want roles built from named capabilities — Owner, Administrator, Member plus custom roles — so that permission is explicit rather than implied by flags.
7. As a user, I want memberships in several workspaces under one login with an Active Workspace switcher, so that I can work for multiple organizations without separate accounts.
8. As a user, I want to authenticate through a managed identity provider with MFA and session rotation, so that my credentials are protected by a specialist.
9. As a member, I want my Timer to be a single globally active tracker scoped to one workspace and one project, so that my recorded time is always unambiguous.
10. As a member, I want timer starts, pauses, resumes, and stops applied as idempotent commands at their claimed effective time, so that duplicates and retries never distort my hours.
11. As a desktop member, I want offline timer commands and activity evidence queued locally and synchronized later, so that connectivity problems never cost me recorded work.
12. As a member, I want late or clock-skewed submissions flagged for review rather than rejected, so that my time is never silently lost.
13. As a member, I want to inspect the Tracking Policy currently applied to me and all of my own Activity Evidence, so that monitoring is transparent to its subject.
14. As a workspace administrator, I want versioned Tracking Policy where stale-policy capture fails closed while the Timer stays open, so that policy is enforced without punishing the member.
15. As a timesheet approver, I want Timesheets to move through Open, Submitted, Approved, and Rejected with approval locking entries until an audited reopening, so that reported time is trustworthy.
16. As a member, I want one Daily Update per Workday grouped by project, so that my reporting matches my working schedule and time zone.
17. As a workspace administrator, I want Opportunities separated from Projects with Won and Lost as fixed terminal outcomes, so that sales conversion and delivery status have unambiguous meanings.
18. As a member, I want the Project Dossier connecting tasks, time, activity, updates, Documents, and Files, so that everything about one engagement lives in one place.
19. As a member, I want Project Assignments to grant project responsibility and visibility without workspace authority, so that being on a project never leaks admin power.
20. As a member, I want Workspace Documents with folder-inherited Document Access enforced identically in browsing, search, and AI citations, so that visibility rules cannot be bypassed by asking differently.
21. As a member, I want Files uploaded directly to object storage through signed slots with versions, previews, and derived artifacts, so that large uploads are fast and never overwrite history.
22. As a member, I want user uploads to pass a fail-closed scan before becoming available, so that malware never spreads through shared files.
23. As a member, I want deleted Documents and Files held in Trash with a restore window before an irreversible purge, so that mistakes are recoverable but deletion is real.
24. As a member, I want automatic transcription of audio and video Files in French and English producing immutable, citable Transcripts, so that recorded knowledge becomes searchable.
25. As a member, I want source-cited AI Answers over the knowledge corpus, kept in my per-workspace history under configurable retention, so that I can trust and revisit what the AI told me.
26. As a workspace owner, I want Workspace AI Policy controlling purposes, providers, regions, and retention with contractual no-training guarantees, so that my content never trains a model.
27. As a member, I want lexical search guaranteed even when AI is disabled or a provider is down, and semantic features failing explicitly rather than returning silently empty results, so that degradation is honest.
28. As a workspace owner, I want AI usage entitlement-gated and metered per purpose, so that spend is bounded and predictable.
29. As a member, I want notifications from all my workspaces in one cross-workspace inbox with origin visible, so that I never miss work from a workspace I'm not currently viewing.
30. As a member, I want per-workspace, per-category Delivery Preferences with mandatory security, billing, and membership notices always delivered, so that I control noise without missing what matters.
31. As a workspace owner, I want seat-based billing where only accepted active memberships consume purchased seats, so that invitations and archived members never cost money.
32. As a workspace owner, I want plan and seat changes inside DocuFlow with immediate prorated increases and period-end decreases floored at consumption, so that billing follows my team's reality.
33. As a workspace owner, I want an expired trial, cancellation, or failed dunning to end in a Read-only Workspace — viewing, export, and recovery preserved — so that my data is never held hostage.
34. As a workspace owner, I want entitlements derived from a versioned Plan Registry with version pinning, so that plan changes never silently alter what I bought.
35. As an external integrator, I want an additive public `/api/v1` authenticated by Service Account API keys with rate limits, idempotency keys, cursor pagination, and RFC 9457 errors, so that my integration stays stable for years.
36. As an external integrator, I want thin, HMAC-signed webhooks with retries, replay, and auto-disable, so that I learn about changes without polling and re-fetch state with my own credentials.
37. As a workspace administrator, I want Service Accounts as non-member principals with explicitly granted capabilities and no seat consumption, so that integrations act with least privilege.
38. As a desktop member, I want the sync protocol versioned with a drain window in which an outdated agent can still upload queued offline work, so that version hygiene never destroys recorded evidence.
39. As a workspace administrator, I want Device Enrollments revocable per workspace without touching the user's other enrollments, so that offboarding one engagement is surgical.
40. As a customer data controller, I want DocuFlow to operate as GDPR processor for workspace content with a published Subprocessor Registry and signed DPAs, so that my own compliance story holds.
41. As a user, I want account deletion with guided workspace transfer, a cancelable grace window, controller-side erasure, and pseudonymized memberships, so that I can leave without breaking the workspaces I contributed to.
42. As a workspace owner, I want a self-serve account-level export, so that leaving or auditing DocuFlow never requires support tickets.
43. As a workspace administrator, I want security-relevant actions recorded in an append-only audit trail with immutable exports, so that investigations have evidence.
44. As a workspace owner, I want platform staff to reach my content only through time-boxed, workspace-visible Support Access Grants or loudly audited break-glass, so that operator access is consented and visible.
45. As a platform staff member, I want a separate audited operator surface with dedicated principals and no standing content access, so that support work is safe by construction.
46. As a DocuFlow operator, I want RPO ≤ 5 minutes and RTO ≤ 4 hours with quarterly timed restore drills and Erasure Journal replay, so that recovery is proven rather than assumed.
47. As a DocuFlow operator, I want one OpenTelemetry pipeline into managed EU sinks with hard-failure-only paging and a public status page, so that incidents surface without alert fatigue.
48. As a DocuFlow operator, I want per-provider spend alerts at 80% of the €300–500/month ceiling, so that cost surprises cannot accumulate silently.
49. As a DocuFlow developer, I want expand/contract deploys with rollback by image redeploy and never a down-migration, so that every release is reversible.
50. As a DocuFlow developer, I want every deferred effect running as a durable idempotent job with declared retries, dead-letter capture, and audited replay, so that background work is observable and recoverable.
51. As a DocuFlow developer, I want domain events on a transactional outbox with at-least-once delivery and per-aggregate ordering, so that consequences never depend on a dual-write.
52. As a DocuFlow developer, I want strict module interfaces with service extraction only on measured evidence, so that the monolith stays modular without premature distribution.
53. As a DocuFlow developer, I want billing, email, storage, AI, and identity providers behind replaceable adapters, so that no vendor decision is irreversible.
54. As a TECHMA legacy user, I want every existing project, client, document, file, time entry, screenshot, device, and URL to keep its identity through migration, so that history and bookmarks survive.
55. As a TECHMA legacy user, I want my password login to keep working across the identity cutover without a forced reset, so that migration is invisible to me.
56. As a TECHMA legacy user, I want my enrolled desktop agent to keep syncing through every migration phase without re-login, so that evidence capture never stops.
57. As a workspace owner of the migrated workspace, I want a pinned legacy plan with no billing surprises, so that becoming tenant number one costs nothing.
58. As a DocuFlow developer, I want temporary DB-backed feature flags with named owners and removal gates, so that migration switches cannot become permanent architecture.
59. As a DocuFlow developer, I want every backfill to ship a verifier whose output lands in an in-repo evidence trail, so that "did we lose anything?" is answerable from the repository.

## Implementation Decisions

The authoritative record is ADR-0001 through ADR-0017 in the repository's ADR directory plus the two research artifacts linked from the wayfinder map ([map issue #1](https://github.com/Lamakira/docuflow/issues/1)). Summary of the decided architecture:

**Topology and modules** (ADR-0005, 0008, 0014)
- Modular monolith, one repository, one authoritative PostgreSQL database, two runtimes from one Docker image: HTTP and durable worker.
- Ten domain modules: Identity & Access, Workspace, Clients & Sales, Projects, Time, Activity, Knowledge, Billing, Notifications, Intelligence. Modules own implementation and persistence behind explicit interfaces.
- Immediate invariants use synchronous calls; deferred consequences use transactional-outbox events. Workspace provisioning is the single sanctioned synchronous cross-module command chain, with compensation.
- Policy lives with its enforcing module: Tracking Policy in Activity, Work Schedule in Time, Workspace AI Policy in Intelligence.
- Read models start as composed queries; materialization per module only on measured need. Service extraction only after interface and data ownership stabilize plus a measured need.

**Tenancy** (ADR-0004, 0006)
- One Workspace model for individuals and organizations. Shared-schema pooled tables; immutable `workspace_id` on every workspace-owned row, propagated through requests, workers, caches, queues, objects, search records, analytics, and audit records.
- Application scoping + composite relational constraints + PostgreSQL row-level security as defense in depth. Small global allowlist for identity and system control data. Privileged cross-workspace operations only through a separate audited interface. Single-home-region placement seam for later relocation.

**Identity and authorization** (ADR-0007)
- Clerk as managed identity provider behind an `IdentityProvider` seam: credentials, authentication flows, MFA, session rotation. DocuFlow owns Users, Workspaces, Memberships, Workspace Roles, Capabilities, Service Accounts, Devices, Device Enrollments, and every authorization decision, evaluated centrally against a PrincipalContext carrying explicit workspace scope.
- Reassessment triggers: EU identity-residency customer or enterprise-procurement requirement.

**Time and activity** (ADR-0009)
- Server-authoritative Timer state machine; at most one active Timer per User enforced by partial unique index. All surfaces submit idempotent Timer Commands (origin, per-origin sequence, claimed effective time, explicit workspace scope) applied in effective-time order, materializing Time Entries that split on pause and overlap; late arrivals trigger bounded re-materialization; append-only command log is provenance.
- Claimed device times pair with server receive times under monotonic-clock anchoring, clamped to the present, flagged not rejected. Activity Evidence enters via two-phase uploads and idempotent batch commits; derived processing rides outbox workers. Capture obeys immutable versioned Tracking Policy; stale cache fails capture closed with the Timer open.

**Billing** (ADR-0010)
- Stripe Billing behind a replaceable BillingProvider adapter; DocuFlow as merchant; Stripe Tax from launch. Subscription = Plan + purchased seat capacity; increases immediate with proration, decreases at period end floored at active Billable Seat consumption.
- DocuFlow-owned versioned Plan Registry; effective entitlements are a pure function of billing state, plan, and registry version; audited overrides; grandfathering by version pinning. DocuFlow-owned billing state machine (Trialing, Active, PastDue, ReadOnly, cancel-at-period-end); no-card trials with no Stripe objects; full access during dunning; ReadOnly enforced centrally by capability write-classification.
- Webhooks land in a signature-verified deduplicating inbox; workers re-fetch the authoritative object into a provider-neutral projection, recompute entitlements, bump the authorization version, emit outbox consequences; daily drift-alerting reconciliation. Checkout and payment methods on hosted Stripe surfaces; plan/seat changes only in DocuFlow.

**Contract surfaces** (ADR-0011)
- Three surfaces on one HTTP runtime, all calling the same module interfaces: private web BFF in lockstep with the web client; separately versioned desktop sync API; public `/api/v1` with URL major versions and additive-only evolution.
- Public auth: per-Service-Account static API keys → PrincipalContext; token-bucket rate limits per Service Account plus per-workspace aggregate from the Plan Registry; optional Idempotency-Key replay. Errors RFC 9457, cursor pagination only, opaque IDs, RFC 3339 UTC timestamps.
- Webhooks: workspace-owned endpoints, explicit public event allowlist from the outbox, HMAC-signed, at-least-once unordered, ~72h backoff, auto-disable, replay; thin payloads (event type + resource IDs).
- Desktop protocol: agent-initiated HTTPS; handshake carries clock anchor, Tracking Policy version, minimum protocol version, directives; 12-month/two-version support plus 6-month drain window for uploading queued offline work. Public majors live ≥ 12 months with Deprecation/Sunset signaling.

**Documents, files, storage** (ADR-0012)
- Native Document content in PostgreSQL; Files and derived artifacts in an S3-shaped object store behind one shared port. Immutable, ID-only, workspace-prefixed object keys; names and scope only in database metadata.
- Direct signed-PUT two-phase uploads with finalize verification; short-lived audit-logged signed GETs after backend authorization; proxy streaming for sensitive classes. App-owned versioning on both planes. Eager derived artifacts via outbox workers. Fail-closed scan state machine for user uploads; agent screenshots exempt.
- Two-phase deletion everywhere: 30-day Trash then idempotent purge cascade across rows, objects, derived artifacts, indexes; workspace deletion freezes 30 days then sweeps the prefix. Erasure primitives and purge-blocking hold flag in the port. Legacy objects keep existing keys; database row is key authority.

**Jobs, events, email, notifications** (ADR-0013)
- All deferred effects in the worker runtime through a DocuFlow-owned jobs port on a PostgreSQL queue in the authoritative database; enqueue commits transactionally with domain writes; HTTP runtime does no background work.
- Outbox event log (UUIDv7, versioned type, workspace + principal provenance, thin PII-minimized payload); dispatcher claims with `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED`, fans out one job per registered consumer: at-least-once, per-aggregate ordering, per-consumer retry isolation, bounded replay window. Job types declare attempts, backoff, timeout, concurrency class; dead-letter table with audited replay. Lease-elected scheduler tick; module-owned schedules expanding into idempotent occurrence-keyed jobs.
- Resend behind a narrow email port (SES named successor); DocuFlow-owned templates, delivery projections, suppression; thin emails. Notification fan-out materializes per-recipient rows with snapshot resolution and read-time membership gating; Delivery Preferences per user/workspace/category/channel; in-app always on; security, billing, membership mandatory.

**Intelligence** (ADR-0014)
- Intelligence module owns index artifacts, ingestion, retrieval, AI gateway and adapters, AI Purpose taxonomy, Workspace AI Policy, content-minimized AI audit. Retrieval covers the knowledge corpus only (Documents, File extracted text, Transcripts).
- First-wave engine: PostgreSQL FTS + pgvector, outbox-fed, full provenance on index rows; side-by-side index generations with per-workspace atomic cutover for model/chunker migrations; managed-service extraction only on measured thresholds.
- No ACL duplication in indexes: retrieval joins canonical Document Access and Project Assignment at query time; deletions ride the purge cascade plus nightly reconciliation; citations re-check access at read.
- Gateway exposes `generate`, `embed`, `transcribe`; authorizes capability and Document Access, evaluates policy and purpose, minimizes payloads, allowlists provider/region/retention, enforces budgets/rate limits/circuit breakers, audits every call. Providers: OpenAI direct (embeddings, generation); Azure Speech provisional STT (French + English), gated on a consented benchmark. Transcripts immutable, copy-out only; Loom scraping retired. AI on by default under a non-negotiable floor (no-training, payload minimization, no raw prompt logging) with per-purpose opt-out; entitlement-gated, metered in units; lexical search is the no-external-call floor; generation hard-stops at budget exhaustion; no automatic PII redaction in v1.

**Security, audit, privacy, compliance** (ADR-0015)
- Append-only audit port in PostgreSQL, one log with workspace and platform scopes, mutation grants revoked, closed segments exported to immutable object storage. Audited actions: authentication, membership/role lifecycle, policy changes, billing changes, sensitive exports/downloads, deletions/restores, credential and Service Account lifecycle, device enrollment, privileged access, AI gateway calls.
- GDPR: processor for workspace content, controller for account/billing/telemetry. Account deletion: guided transfer/delete of owned workspaces, cancelable grace window, controller-side erasure, in-place Membership pseudonymization, workspace notification. Six fixed Data Classes drive the control matrix; retention lives with owning modules as idempotent scheduled jobs; bounded backup window with ID-only Erasure Journal replayed after restores.
- Encryption: provider-managed at rest + TLS; KMS envelope encryption for Secret-class fields; credentials as one-time-shown hashes. Host-managed secret store, versioned signing keys; legacy ephemeral JWT secret and `MCP_API_KEY` retired. Platform Staff from a dedicated identity pool on a separate audited surface; Support Access Grants time-boxed and workspace-visible; audited break-glass. 72-hour breach runbook; Legal Hold as purge-blocking primitive; Subprocessor Registry gated on DPAs, regions, no-training; in-repo compliance control matrix; quarterly access reviews.

**Hosting, deployment, observability, recovery** (ADR-0016)
- Render (two-instance HTTP + worker, one image) + Neon PostgreSQL (plain SQL, no vendor-specific features) + Cloudflare R2 `eu` jurisdiction, all Frankfurt; standalone AWS account with Object-Locked S3 for nightly encrypted exports and audit segments. Cloudflare DNS/CDN/WAF/edge rate limits.
- OpenTelemetry through a collector into Better Stack (EU) + Sentry (Germany); telemetry carries IDs only. GitHub Actions trunk-based: auto-deploy staging (synthetic data), manual promotion, migrations as a gated pre-deploy step under expand/contract, rollback by image redeploy.
- Targets: 99.9% monthly internal HTTP SLO; worker lag SLO 95% under 60s; RPO ≤ 5 min (PITR), RTO ≤ 4 h; daily independent logical exports; quarterly timed restore drill with Erasure Journal replay recorded in-repo; annual restore-from-export drill. Hard-failure-only paging; 80% spend alerts against €300–500/month; sized ≤ 25 workspaces at launch with ~10× headroom.

**Migration** (ADR-0017)
- Nine dependency-ordered overlapping phases, each of small expand/contract deploys with verifier, temporary flag, rollback path: (1) stabilize — de-Replit, containerize, CI/CD + synthetic staging, one plain-SQL migration journal applied as gated pre-deploy, delete boot-time DDL/data mutation, characterization + contract tests on legacy web API and desktop v1 protocol, OTel baseline, persistent versioned desktop signing key; (2) hosting lift with GCS still serving; (3) worker runtime + jobs port + outbox; (4) Workspace seam — seed one Workspace and Memberships (main admin → Owner, admin → Administrator, user → Member, special flags → capabilities, archived users → Archived Memberships, global settings → Workspace policy rows), per-table lineage backfill nullable → resumable job → zero-orphan verifier → NOT NULL, core composite uniques, RLS table-by-table after verified scoping, Teams dropped after evidence snapshot; (5) Clerk migration — bcrypt import, dual-auth drain, OIDC-only invites, then Replit OIDC and `MCP_API_KEY` removed; enrolled devices untouched; (6) module carve-outs carrying the data splits — Opportunity/Project by stage rule with legacy IDs staying on Projects, Document/File split preserving object keys with access defaulting to everyone-in-workspace, embeddings dropped and rebuilt, GCS → R2 bulk-copy/dual-write/read-flip, legacy Time Entries kept with legacy provenance and no synthesized commands; (7) new contract surfaces; (8) billing go-live with the legacy workspace pinned; (9) retirement.
- Cross-cutting: DocuFlow-owned DB-backed feature flags (global/workspace/user) behind a cached port, each flag temporary with owner and removal gate; flags are not entitlements and not policy. Bounded announced maintenance windows allowed for hosting and identity cutovers while single-tenant; all else zero-downtime. Destructive drops gated on ≥ 14 days zero-reference telemetry plus two backup cycles. Desktop v1 endpoints removed after two weeks of zero v1 traffic from the force-updated internal fleet. Legacy web API retires only after v2 UI cutover; backend and UI never block each other. Per-phase evidence (verifier outputs, snapshots, cutover timestamps) recorded in an in-repo migration evidence directory.

## Testing Decisions

- A good test asserts external behavior at a contract, never implementation details. Renaming internals, moving code between modules, or swapping a provider adapter must not break tests.
- **Primary seam: HTTP contract surfaces against a real PostgreSQL.** Phase 1 captures characterization/contract tests on the legacy web API and desktop v1 protocol before anything moves; those suites run continuously against the compatibility adapters through every later phase. Each new surface — web BFF, desktop sync v2, public `/api/v1`, webhook delivery — gains contract tests as it lands. Real PostgreSQL in tests so tenancy scoping, RLS, composite constraints, and outbox writes are exercised, not mocked.
- **Test doubles only at the architecture's own ports:** storage port (S3-shaped in-memory or MinIO), jobs port (inline synchronous test driver), email port, BillingProvider (fake Stripe), IdentityProvider (fake Clerk token verifier), AI gateway (canned responses). No seams invented for testing.
- **Direct module-interface tests only where HTTP cannot reach the logic:** Timer command application and re-materialization edge cases, entitlement derivation from the Plan Registry, outbox dispatcher delivery semantics, backfill verifiers.
- Migration backfills are tested by their verifiers: every backfill ships an invariant/orphan/count check whose output is preserved as migration evidence.
- Prior art: none — the current repository exposes no automated test suite, so the Phase 1 harness is net-new and becomes the repository standard.

## Out of Scope

- Web-app, desktop-app, and marketing-site interface design (the v2 web UI proceeds in parallel under its own effort; the backend only preserves legacy contracts until its cutover).
- Exact pricing, commercial plan values, and trial duration.
- Marketing-site architecture.
- Customer-managed, self-hosted, and on-premise deployments.
- Active-active multi-region operation and per-customer regional deployment.
- Completing formal SOC 2 or ISO 27001 certification (readiness only).

## Further Notes

- Decision authority: ADR-0001–0017 in the repository plus the wayfinder map ([issue #1](https://github.com/Lamakira/docuflow/issues/1)) with its closed decision tickets and two research artifacts (provider candidates; current-backend inventory and migration constraints). Where this spec and an ADR disagree, the ADR wins.
- Vocabulary: `CONTEXT.md` is the glossary; every term capitalized here (Workspace, Membership, Timer Command, Plan Registry, …) is defined there and must be used verbatim in code-facing naming.
- Deliberately deferred to implementation, per the map: exact public API resource catalogue and webhook event list; exact audit event catalogue, control-matrix values, retention schedule values, DPA text, incident severity ladder, vendor-onboarding checklist, access-review cadence; exact per-table lineage/backfill matrix, verifier queries, flag inventory, and phase calendar. Resolve each inside its owning phase/module, recording catalogue-level choices in the migration evidence trail or new ADRs as warranted.
- Implementation should proceed phase by phase in ADR-0017 order; phases overlap but never reorder their dependencies (jobs before backfills, Workspace seam before Clerk, carve-outs after the seam lands per area).
- Reassessment triggers recorded across ADRs: EU identity-residency or enterprise-procurement customer (Clerk), hosting-on-AWS or EU-residency customer (SES), measured retrieval thresholds (managed search), enterprise BYOK demand (KMS scope).

items.title: Add flow telemetry contracts: raw datagram envelope, ingestion service, normalised flow record
items.body:
## Context

Riptide's flow pipeline currently ingests UDP directly into `riptide-flows`, which parses, enriches and persists in one process. We want to move ingestion behind a broker: `udpramp` captures datagrams statelessly, a gRPC gateway forwards them to Kafka, and `riptide-flows` becomes the consumer that parses, enriches and persists.

That handover needs a published wire contract. Today the closest thing is `udpramp/proto/envelope.proto` (`udpramp.v1.FlowEnvelope`), which is frozen from v0.2.0 and already carries exporter identity, listener tuple and loss attribution. It lives in the udpramp repo under Apache-2.0 and has no Java/Go/Rust distribution.

Research write-up: `riptide-flows/_bmad-output/planning-artifacts/research/technical-normalised-flow-protobuf-contract-udpramp-to-riptide-research-2026-08-03.md`

## Proposal

Add a `deltav.flows.v1` package under `proto/deltav/flows/v1/` with three schemas:

1. **`flow_envelope.proto`** — the raw-carrying envelope. Fields 1-10 keep udpramp's frozen tag assignments verbatim so the two are wire-compatible (protobuf matches by tag, not by type name). Three additions:
   - `ramp_exporter_sequence` (11) — a per-exporter sequence. `ramp_sequence` is monotonic per (instance, pipeline) but the Kafka partition key is the exporter, so a partition observes an interleaved subsequence and its gaps are not loss. This makes gap detection partition-local.
   - `tenancy` (12) — gateway-stamped tenant/organisation/zone/system, which riptide persists but the envelope cannot currently supply once per-listener config stops being the discriminator.
   - `gateway_received_at_unix_nanos` (13) — attributes latency and loss to the gateway hop separately from the ramp-to-gateway leg.

2. **`flow_ingestion_service.proto`** — the gateway RPC. A single bidirectional stream; the datagram class rides in the envelope, so routing needs no per-protocol method. The response carries a cumulative durability high-water mark so at-least-once is expressible, which the existing delta-v `TelemetryAck` cannot express because it carries only a timestamp.

3. **`normalised_flow.proto`** — the decoded flow record, for consumers that want parsed flows rather than raw datagrams. Promoted fields mirror riptide's `Flow` interface plus exporter identity, with a `(enterprise_number, element_id)` extension bag for unpromoted IPFIX Information Elements (RFC 7012 abstract types).

## Ownership

This repo becomes canonical for the envelope. `udpramp` migrates its generated types over in a follow-up; tag assignments are identical so nothing changes on the wire in the meantime.

## Notes

- Additive only, no existing schema touched, so `make breaking` should pass clean.
- Enum values and RPC request/response type names follow the buf DEFAULT ruleset, so some names differ from the udpramp originals. Only tag numbers carry wire meaning.
- `normalised_flow.proto` does not yet model sFlow's sampled packet headers and sample pool, which have no equivalent in riptide's `Flow` interface. Documented in-file as a known gap.

# AI CLI Tools Community Digest 2026-11-11 > Generated: 2026-11-11 01:34 UTC | Tools covered: 7 - [Claude Code](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code) - [OpenAI Codex](https://github​.com/openai/codex) - [Gemini CLI](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) - [GitHub Copilot CLI](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli) - [OpenCode](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode) - [Pi](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi) - [Qwen Code](https://github​.com/QwenLM/qwen-code) - [Claude Code Skills](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills) --- ## Cross-Tool Comparison This report synthesizes the state of the AI CLI ecosystem as of November 11, 2026, based on community activity across seven major platforms. ### 1. Ecosystem Overview The AI CLI ecosystem has transitioned from a "prototype" phase to a period of intense infrastructure hardening, with a focus on multi-agent orchestration, persistent state management, and enterprise-grade security. Developers are shifting their priorities from simple prompt-to-code interfaces to complex "agentic" workflows, necessitating robust sandboxing, session durability, and inter-agent communication protocols. Platform-specific stability—particularly on Windows—remains the primary barrier to widespread professional adoption, alongside growing pains related to the Model Context Protocol (MCP) lifecycle management. ### 2. Activity Comparison *Note: Values are snapshots as of 2026-11-11. Figures refer to the provided digest data.* | Tool | Hot Issues (Tracked) | Key PRs / Active | Release Velocity | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **Claude Code** | 10 | 1 | Moderate | | **OpenAI Codex** | 10 | 10 | High | | **Gemini CLI** | 10 | 10 | Moderate | | **Copilot CLI** | 10 | 1 | High | | **OpenCode** | 10 | 10 | High | | **Pi** | 10 | 10 | High | | **Qwen Code** | 2 | 10 | High | ### 3. Shared Feature Directions * **Agent Sandboxing & "Seatbelts":** Every major tool is grappling with user demands for restricted execution environments to prevent destructive shell commands (e.g., `git reset --force`, `rm -rf`). (Notable: *OpenCode, Gemini, Copilot*) * **MCP Infrastructure Hardening:** The community is consistently hitting walls with MCP session tear-downs, memory leaks, and auth-token persistence. (Notable: *Claude, Copilot, Qwen*) * **Durable State/Persistence:** Move away from local SQLite files toward durable, shared storage (e.g., Chord stores) and persistent workspaces across sessions. (Notable: *Pi, Qwen, OpenCode*) * **Multi-Agent Coordination:** Moving beyond single-agent isolation toward "team" structures where sub-agents report status and coordinate tasks. (Notable: *Claude, Gemini, Qwen*) ### 4. Differentiation Analysis * **Claude Code:** Heavily focused on **Enterprise/DevOps parity** and cross-machine agent orchestration. The tool is being groomed for high-complexity architectural tasks. * **OpenAI Codex:** Positioning itself as the **IDE-integrated heavy hitter**, with intense focus on macOS/Windows desktop stability and browser-based remote pairing. * **Gemini CLI:** Pushing into **AST-aware intelligence**, focusing on reducing token bloat through structural code analysis rather than raw file context. * **Qwen Code:** Unique focus on **Social-Enterprise Channels** (WeChat/QQ/Email integrations) and "Fleet" dashboarding for managed agent deployments. * **Pi:** Focused on **Data Durability**, specifically leveraging distributed systems (Chord) to ensure that agent session history is never lost during directory moves or crashes. ### 5. Community Momentum & Maturity * **Rapid Iterators:** *OpenAI Codex* and *OpenCode* show the highest volume of PR activity, suggesting they are aggressively patching regressions and pushing new features. * **Highest Community Sentiment:** *Claude Code* (via engagement metrics like comment volume on [#28300]) and *OpenCode* (via user-driven feature requests for "seatbelts") demonstrate the most vocal and engaged power-user bases. * **Emerging Maturity:** *Qwen Code* and *Pi* appear to be approaching a more stable, production-ready state by focusing on back-end infrastructure (distributed stores/managed agent loops) rather than purely UI-driven features. ### 6. Trend Signals * **The "Agent-to-Agent" Protocol Era:** The demand for standardizing how agents talk to each other (cross-session messaging) marks the end of the "siloed agent" era. We expect interoperability protocols to become a critical procurement requirement in 2027. * **Infrastructure over Intelligence:** Community frustration is shifting away from model "smartness" and toward "reliability." Users are willing to trade latency for stability, favoring tools that provide granular control over agent lifecycle and resource usage. * **Platform Friction:** The Windows CLI experience is significantly lagging behind macOS across almost every ecosystem, creating a clear market opportunity for developers who can solve terminal/process-management instabilities on the Windows platform. --- ## Per-Tool Reports
Claude Code — anthropics/claude-code ## Claude Code Skills Highlights > Source: [anthropics/skills](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills) This report synthesizes activity from the `anthropics/skills` repository as of November 11, 2026. ### 1. Top Skills Ranking These represent the most active development threads currently moving through the PR pipeline: * **[mcp-builder](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1742)**: Fixes critical compatibility issues for `mcp>=2.0.0`, specifically updating streamable client imports and header configuration. *Status: Open.* * **[skill-creator](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1298)**: A comprehensive overhaul to improve trigger evaluation reliability, addressing subprocess pipe failures on Windows and runtime interference. *Status: Open.* * **[webapp-testing](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1980)**: Security-focused update replacing `shell=True` with safer command execution to mitigate potential injection risks. *Status: Open.* * **[docx-tooling](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1792)**: Enhances document automation by adding timeout error reporting and strict verification of revision marks to ensure "clean" exports. *Status: Open.* * **[proofcore-contract-auditor](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1771)**: A specialized Web3 utility for static analysis of Solidity/Rust smart contracts with blockchain-anchored audit proofs. *Status: Open.* * **[pyxel-retro-dev](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/525)**: Enables end-to-end retro game development within Claude, including headless execution and frame-by-frame state inspection. *Status: Open.* ### 2. Community Demand Trends Analysis of open issues reveals three primary areas of community frustration and demand: * **Trust and Governance**: There is strong pushback against the current `anthropic/` namespace usage for community skills ([#492](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/492)), with users requesting better identity separation to prevent "trust boundary" abuse. * **Operational Reliability**: Developers are struggling with the "trigger rate" of skills ([#556](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/556)). There is high demand for more robust testing harnesses that don't produce false negatives during evaluation. * **Team Collaboration**: Organizations are clamoring for native skill-sharing features ([#228](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/issues/228)) to move away from the manual "download/upload" file-sharing cycle currently required by Claude Code. ### 3. High-Potential Pending Skills These active PRs show significant momentum and are likely to impact the ecosystem once resolved: * **[Notion Spec to Implementation](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1245)**: A productivity-centric skill that bridges product requirements in Notion directly into actionable implementation tasks. * **[md2video-audio](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1703)**: A novel content-generation skill that compiles Markdown into MP4 presentations with synthesized voiceovers. * **[scnet-hpc](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1615)**: A sophisticated HPC (High-Performance Computing) automation skill aimed at researchers managing cluster workflows, SSH profiles, and Slurm jobs. ### 4. Skills Ecosystem Insight **Summary:** The community is currently shifting focus from "skill discovery" toward "skill infrastructure," with the most urgent demand being the professionalization of the `skill-creator` toolset to ensure reliable triggers and secure, organizational-level sharing. --- # Claude Code Community Digest – 2026-11-11 ### 1. Today's Highlights The community is currently focused on stabilizing remote and multi-agent workflows, with significant reports concerning authentication races and MCP integration bugs in the latest builds. Development remains heavily influenced by power users requesting advanced inter-agent communication protocols and more granular control over desktop app lifecycle events. ### 2. Releases * **v2.1.322**: [Release Notes](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/releases/tag/v2.1.322) * Introduced "fast mode" for Vertex AI across global, US, and EU regions, with a fallback mechanism to standard speed if restricted. ### 3. Hot Issues 1. **[#28300] Agent-to-Agent Protocol**: Highly anticipated feature for multi-agent collaboration across machines. High engagement (59 comments) indicates a strong desire for decentralized agent orchestration. [Link](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/28300) 2. **[#100377] CCR v2 Registration Failure**: Critical bug causing `claude.ai` project threads to fail on macOS. Developers report 400 errors during worker registration. [Link](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/100377) 3. **[#107232] Long-running API Requests**: Persistent issue where the client fails to handle API requests exceeding 5 minutes, significantly impacting complex architectural tasks. [Link](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/107232) 4. **[#102952] Desktop UI Aesthetics**: High community sentiment (18 likes) for restoring the "glowing code-glyph ripple" background on the desktop home screen. [Link](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/102952) 5. **[#87954] Cross-session Communication**: Request for a first-class channel allowing separate user sessions to exchange messages and coordinate tasks. [Link](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/87954) 6. **[#105334] MCP Elicitation Bugs**: Desktop app reportedly declines MCP elicitation requests silently despite advertising support, hindering interactive tool usage. [Link](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/105334) 7. **[#108601] Standing Instruction Override**: A critical concern where long-running sessions ignore explicit "oversee only" instructions, highlighting potential model alignment issues during multi-step tasks. [Link](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/108601) 8. **[#108217] TUI Performance (Windows)**: Image pasting (Alt+V) causes a 12-second event loop block, severely impacting TUI responsiveness. [Link](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/108217) 9. **[#104422] Unconsented Auto-updates**: Frustration regarding desktop app restarts during active work hours; users are demanding update deferral controls. [Link](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/104422) 10. **[#108131] Missing Generation Indicator**: A recent regression in the desktop app (v4.23118.0) where the working status indicator for active sessions has disappeared. [Link](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/issues/108131) ### 4. Key PR Progress * **[#74722] Conventional Branch Naming**: Merged support for `/commit-push-pr` to automatically use `type/description` formats based on the diff, aligning with Conventional Branch 1.0.0. [Link](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code/pull/74722) ### 5. Feature Request Trends * **Multi-Agent Orchestration**: Massive interest in enabling inter-session communication (`SendMessage` tool) and Agent-to-Agent protocols. * **Cloud/Local Parity**: Users are pushing to close the functional gap between cloud-hosted project sessions and local CLI/Remote Control capabilities. * **Granular Control**: Requests for better user-defined control over auto-updates and permission bypasses in "auto" mode. ### 6. Developer Pain Points * **Authentication Fragility**: Multiple reports of OAuth session races and expired token issues when running multiple interactive sessions or VS Code extensions simultaneously. * **Platform-Specific Stability**: Windows users are encountering recurring issues with file system locking (`rg.exe` processes) and UI freezes, while macOS users face regressions in session monitoring. * **Silent Failures**: High frustration regarding MCP and project registration errors that provide minimal feedback, making debugging difficult for end-users.
OpenAI Codex — openai/codex # OpenAI Codex Community Digest: 2026-11-11 ### 1. Today's Highlights The Codex ecosystem is currently focused on stabilizing the Windows desktop experience and improving headless/remote authentication workflows. Significant activity centers on resolving memory leaks in MCP server processes and patching broken UI/browser integration following recent desktop app updates. ### 2. Releases * **[rust-v0.167.1](https://github​.com/openai/codex/compare/rust-v0.167.0...rust-v0.167.1):** Maintenance release. * **[rust-v0.169.0-alpha.9](https://github​.com/openai/codex/):** Latest alpha iteration. * **[rust-v0.167.0-alpha.4.2](https://github​.com/openai/codex/):** Minor pre-release update. ### 3. Hot Issues 1. **[#56655](https://github​.com/openai/codex/issues/56655):** VS Code extension UI fails to initialize on Windows (74 comments, 85 👍). High visibility bug blocking core IDE integration. 2. **[#30408](https://github​.com/openai/codex/issues/30408):** MCP server process memory leak (9GB+ RSS) due to improper lifecycle management (72 comments). 3. **[#59895](https://github​.com/openai/codex/issues/59895):** Local project data disappearance on Windows after app updates (52 comments). 4. **[#57641](https://github​.com/openai/codex/issues/57641):** "Browser access host unavailable" error following desktop update 26.1023.6123.0 (50 comments, 33 👍). 5. **[#49453](https://github​.com/openai/codex/issues/49453):** Persistent browser access denial for `127.0.0.1` despite user override (50 comments). 6. **[#31925](https://github​.com/openai/codex/issues/31925):** Request to restore Option+Space "Quick Chat" on macOS (25 comments, 50 👍). 7. **[#56600](https://github​.com/openai/codex/issues/56600):** Android Remote pairing failures for both QR and manual codes (14 comments). 8. **[#42315](https://github​.com/openai/codex/issues/42315):** Sync failure: iOS Remote on Windows omits Codex projects (14 comments). 9. **[#59546](https://github​.com/openai/codex/issues/59546):** Built-in automation restrictions conflicting with documented scheduling capabilities (12 comments). 10. **[#9286](https://github​.com/openai/codex/issues/9286):** SSH permission errors in sandbox due to `nobody` ownership (12 comments). ### 4. Key PR Progress * **[#60695](https://github​.com/openai/codex/pull/60695):** Implements a Signer Service backend for streamlined macOS notarization. * **[#60683](https://github​.com/openai/codex/pull/60683):** Optimizes composer footer layouts to fit terminal space dynamically. * **[#60675](https://github​.com/openai/codex/pull/60675):** Performance fix: skips redundant screen clears/reads when switching side chats. * **[#60671](https://github​.com/openai/codex/pull/60671):** Adds `sign-only` mode for macOS CLI packages to improve security workflows. * **[#60665](https://github​.com/openai/codex/pull/60665):** Adds content helper for forwarding MCP blocks in Code Mode. * **[#60663](https://github​.com/openai/codex/pull/60663):** Defer exec-server sandbox preparation to the host, fixing cross-OS path issues. * **[#60662](https://github​.com/openai/codex/pull/60662):** Enables gateway device-code sign-in for headless TUI sessions. * **[#60651](https://github​.com/openai/codex/pull/60651):** Enables model and reasoning effort selection for Cloud conversations. * **[#60647](https://github​.com/openai/codex/pull/60647):** Fixes PowerShell working directory errors in the MXC sandbox. * **[#60639](https://github​.com/openai/codex/pull/60639):** Refactors App tools refresh logic to improve MCP runtime responsiveness. ### 5. Hot Discussions * **Show and Tell:** * **[#54474](https://github​.com/openai/codex/discussions/54474):** Repair tool for Windows Computer Use localization (Korean Chrome). * **[#60358](https://github​.com/openai/codex/discussions/60358):** Best practice habits for safe unattended agent/tool execution. * **[#60593](https://github​.com/openai/codex/discussions/60593):** `RegressGuard` for detecting regressions in prompt-based CLI replies. ### 6. Feature Request Trends * **Persistent Visibility:** Users want consistent indicators for usage/rate limits within the desktop UI (#25561). * **Interoperability:** Bidirectional task handoff between ChatGPT (mobile) and Codex (desktop) remains a top priority (#32519). * **Accessibility/Control:** Enhanced control over browser file-upload capabilities via `setInputFiles` in the IAB (#20785). ### 7. Developer Pain Points * **Windows Instability:** A high frequency of "Computer Use" timeout errors, capture failures, and localized UI issues (e.g., #57101, #59303, #60254). * **Lifecycle Management:** Orphaned processes and memory leaks are significantly impacting long-term reliability for desktop users (#30408). * **Environment Parity:** Difficulty syncing configurations across remote, CLI, and desktop environments, particularly regarding authentication/gateways.
Gemini CLI — google-gemini/gemini-cli ## Gemini CLI Community Digest (2026-11-11) ### 1. Today's Highlights The Gemini CLI ecosystem is currently focused on hardening agent stability and optimizing memory management during intensive model operations. Recent updates prioritize fixing critical runtime crashes and improving security around file-system interactions and Git command execution. ### 2. Releases * **v0.69.0-preview.0**: Introduces a `/stats` heatmap for tracking daily token usage and critical fixes for literal `$` character preservation in templates. * **v0.68.0**: Includes general documentation updates to clarify the project's scope, limitations, and tool-launching patterns. ### 3. Hot Issues 1. **[#22323](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/22323)**: Subagent recovery reports "GOAL success" after hitting `MAX_TURNS`, creating false positives. 2. **[#21409](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/21409)**: Generalist agent hangs during sub-agent delegation. Highly critical; users forced to disable sub-agents. 3. **[#19873](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/19873)**: Proposal to leverage bash affinity for OS sandboxing; key for performance and security. 4. **[#22745](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/22745)**: Epic tracking AST-aware file processing to reduce token bloat and improve context accuracy. 5. **[#21968](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/21968)**: Anecdotal reports of Gemini failing to invoke custom skills/sub-agents autonomously. 6. **[#22267](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/22267)**: Browser Agent ignoring `settings.json` overrides, limiting configuration flexibility. 7. **[#24246](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/24246)**: API 400 errors encountered when exceeding 128 tools in scope. 8. **[#21983](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/21983)**: Browser sub-agent failures specifically on Wayland environments. 9. **[#23571](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/23571)**: Model "littering" the workspace with temporary scripts due to restrictive bash execution policies. 10. **[#22672](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/22672)**: Urgent need to prevent the agent from performing destructive Git operations (`reset`, `--force`) without verification. ### 4. Key PR Progress 1. **[#30220](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/30220)**: Preserves Unicode characters and strips ANSI fragments for cleaner session previews. 2. **[#30217](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/30217)**: Fixes a major V8 heap OOM crash during PDF ingestion. 3. **[#30171](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/30171)**: Hardens `isDangerousCommand` to detect obfuscated recursive/forced removals (`rm -Rf`, etc). 4. **[#30219](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/30219)**: Resolves 400 errors by tracking tool calls via the active chat instance instead of compressed history. 5. **[#30095](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/30095)**: Mitigates Windows-specific Git command permission bypasses. 6. **[#30207](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/30207)**: Fixes nightly build failures caused by bloated, stale bundle chunks. 7. **[#30009](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/30009)**: Integrates the Google OSS Exit Gate for standardized NPM publishing. 8. **[#30214](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/30214)**: Expands PuTTY-family SSH client recognition to include `TortoiseGitPlink`. 9. **[#30216](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/30216)**: Adds necessary unit test coverage for quota/API error classification. 10. **[#29960](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/29960)**: Improves telemetry accuracy by tracking CLI version instead of Node runtime version. ### 5. Feature Request Trends * **AST-Driven Intelligence**: A strong push for moving beyond raw file reading toward AST-aware tools (e.g., `ast-grep`) to improve agent search precision and reduce context window usage. * **Self-Governance**: High demand for the agent to become "self-aware"—correctly identifying its own CLI flags and hotkeys to guide the user effectively. * **Persistent Task Tracking**: Moving from "in-context" memory (prone to rot) to persistent, file-based CRUD task management. ### 6. Developer Pain Points * **Sub-agent Fragility**: Users are frequently encountering hangs or silent failures when the agent delegates tasks to sub-agents. * **Context Bloat**: Large file reads are consuming excessive tokens, leading to a desire for "Tactful Extraction" logic. * **Agent Safety**: Concerns regarding the model performing destructive actions (like `git reset` or arbitrary file deletion) without sufficient safeguard warnings or user confirmation.
GitHub Copilot CLI — github/copilot-cli # GitHub Copilot CLI Community Digest: 2026-11-11 ### 1. Today's Highlights The latest updates to the Copilot CLI (v1.0.110-0/1) bring experimental agent interactivity, allowing users to mask-dialog password prompts directly within the CLI. Significant focus has shifted toward refining sandbox security—introducing CIDR-based host rules—and improving terminal UI consistency, though community attention remains heavily fixed on resolving stability regressions in MCP (Model Context Protocol) integrations. ### 2. Releases * **v1.0.110-1**: Fixed session resumption conflicts where multiple windows could write into an active session. Improved UI alignment for custom status lines and enabled control character visualization. * **v1.0.110-0**: Added experimental support for answering `git`, `ssh`, and `sudo` password prompts via masked dialogs. Improved account switching and provided better recovery actions for unavailable accounts. * **v1.0.109 / 109-1**: Introduced IPv4/IPv6 CIDR support for sandbox networking and added support for **Claude Fable 5.2**. Improved environment variable handling for sandbox path settings. ### 3. Hot Issues 1. **[#4438](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4438)**: `disable-model-invocation: true` prevents skills from being reachable even via explicit call. A high-priority usability hurdle for custom project skills. 2. **[#5171](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/5171)**: Regression causing NumLock-off numpad navigation and Delete key to be ignored in Windows Terminal. 3. **[#5404](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/5404)**: Launching `copilot` in a git repo on Windows causes an unhandled exception that kills the parent PowerShell session. 4. **[#5242](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/5242)**: MCP configuration watch registration failures due to Linux `inotify` limits leading to abandoned sessions in containerized environments. 5. **[#5402](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/5402)**: MCP Entra silent sign-in failing for single-tenant apps due to incorrect authority usage (`/common`), forcing daily re-authentication. 6. **[#5405](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/5405)**: Vision/Playwright tools failing to pass image pixels to models, returning only file paths or generic success messages. 7. **[#5388](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/5388)**: Ineffective credential masking for `GH_TOKEN` in GHE Cloud environments, potentially exposing sensitive tokens. 8. **[#5411](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/5411)**: Critical startup failure on macOS Monterey due to missing native "runtime" addon. 9. **[#5283](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/5283)**: Remote environment hosting failing for Copilot Free users, despite settings indicating support. 10. **[#5398](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/5398)**: Native canvas windows appearing blank on macOS 26.7, rendering visual tools unusable. ### 4. Key PR Progress * **[#4770](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli/pull/4770)**: Documentation update for opting out of WebSocket responses, providing a vital workaround for users on restrictive networks. *(Note: No other PRs were updated in the last 24h window beyond the linked document.)* ### 5. Feature Request Trends * **Model Control**: Users are requesting finer granularity in model routing, specifically the ability to block specific models from "Copilot Fusion" or auto-select modes ([#5369](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/5369)). * **Plugin Autonomy**: Increased demand for deeper integration capabilities, such as allowing plugins to set MCP OAuth options (redirect ports, ClientIDs) to support enterprise-managed servers ([#5410](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/5410)). * **Dependency Decoupling**: A push to allow the CLI to use a system-installed `gh` (GitHub CLI) rather than relying on the bundled binary ([#4456](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/4456)). ### 6. Developer Pain Points * **MCP Complexity**: The "more-info-needed" tag density on MCP-related issues suggests significant fragility in the current MCP architecture, particularly concerning auth persistence, stdio child process management, and network environment failures. * **Windows Stability**: A noticeable spike in Windows-specific platform issues (shell termination, keyboard input regression, auth failures) is currently hindering developers using PowerShell/Windows Terminal. * **Visibility**: Developers are frustrated by the "black box" nature of failures, particularly regarding failed image pixel transmission and ambiguous credential storage errors that lack actionable diagnostics.
OpenCode — anomalyco/opencode # OpenCode Community Digest | 2026-11-11 ### 1. Major concerns regarding agent control, potential "rogue" behavior, and database stability have triggered high-priority triage, while community efforts continue to refine the desktop and TUI experience. ### 2.
