# AI Infrastructure Digest 2026-09-26 > Generated: 2026-09-26 00:51 UTC | Projects covered: 6 - [vLLM](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm) - [SGLang](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang) - [llama.cpp](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) - [Ollama](https://github​.com/ollama/ollama) - [LiteLLM](https://github​.com/BerriAI/litellm) - [Unsloth](https://github​.com/unslothai/unsloth) --- ## Cross-Project Comparison This report summarizes the state of the AI infrastructure ecosystem as of **2026-09-26**. ### 1. Ecosystem Overview The infrastructure landscape is currently defined by an aggressive push toward architectural parity between NVIDIA Hopper/Blackwell and AMD ROCm/MI355X, alongside a structural shift toward "intelligent" serving. Projects are increasingly moving away from monolithic Python implementations in favor of Rust-based memory and cache management. The market is maturing toward stable, multi-tenant production, with a clear focus on fixing long-standing issues in speculative decoding and complex tool-calling workflows. ### 2. Activity Comparison *Note: Estimates based on current active PR/Issue queues as of 2026-09-26.* | Project | Active Issues | Active PRs | Release Status | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **vLLM** | High (~44k) | Very High (~58k) | Stable / Patching | | **SGLang** | Moderate (~41k) | Moderate (~41k) | Architecture Shift | | **llama.cpp** | High (~29k) | High (~29k) | Maintenance | | **Ollama** | High (~18k) | Moderate (~18k) | v0.40.0-rc0 | | **LiteLLM** | Moderate (~43k) | Moderate (~43k) | Security Patches | | **Unsloth** | High (~11k) | High (~11k) | Experimental | ### 3. Model Support Race The industry is currently obsessed with **DeepSeek-V4.1**, with both **vLLM** and **SGLang** locked in a feature-parity race regarding kernel fusions (Hopper/SM100 focus). * **vLLM:** Leads in DeepSeek-V4.1 optimization, specifically regarding O-projection and wkv projection. * **SGLang:** Strongest in MoE kernel tuning and unifying Radix cache performance. * **llama.cpp:** Distinguishing itself by supporting "long-tail" and non-autoregressive architectures like **GraniteSpeech** and **K2 Horizon**. * **Ollama:** Prioritizing native **MLX** support for Apple Silicon to maximize consumer-grade performance. ### 4. Performance Frontier Optimization efforts are fragmented by project goals: * **Kernel/Compute:** vLLM and SGLang are focused on "fusion consolidation" (reducing kernel calls) and specialized namespaces for DeepSeek-V4.1. * **Memory Management:** A massive industry-wide pivot to **Rust-based tree cores** for radix caching is underway to avoid Python's GIL and memory management overhead. * **Parallelism:** The "Unified KV-Cache" is the current stability frontier. Both `llama.cpp` and `vLLM` are struggling with memory corruption and response bleeding in multi-tenant/parallel (`-np > 1`) scenarios. * **Quantization:** Unsloth and llama.cpp are leading efforts in bit-width optimization (MXFP4/k-quants) to enable inference on consumer hardware like RTX 4090/5090. ### 5. Layer Positioning * **Inference Engines (vLLM, SGLang):** High-throughput, multi-tenant serving backends designed for data-center integration. * **Local Runtimes (llama.cpp, Ollama):** Focus on portability (CPU/Vulkan/Metal) and ease of developer onboarding; bridging the gap between local dev and edge deployment. * **Gateway (LiteLLM):** The abstraction layer; currently focusing on vendor-neutral cost mapping and security (encryption-at-rest for provider keys). * **Training/Fine-tuning (Unsloth):** Optimized training primitives designed for efficiency, currently building bridges to adopt vLLM/SGLang as serving backends. ### 6. Trend Signals * **The "Agent-First" Parse:** Projects are shifting focus toward structured output (XGrammar, Inkling, Lark). Developers should anticipate higher strictness in tool-calling; avoid relying on "loose" JSON generation. * **Infrastructure "Rust-ification":** Performance-critical components (caching, frontends) are being rewritten in Rust. If you are building custom infrastructure, keep an eye on project migration roadmaps to avoid technical debt. * **Disaggregated Serving (P/D):** As P/D (Prefill/Decode) architectures become standard, "data integrity" (the synchronization of KV blocks across ranks) is the primary stability risk. Expect continued churn in `Mooncake` and similar KV-connector implementations. * **Recommendation:** If you are running production agents, **pause updates** on core serving engines (vLLM/SGLang) for the next 72 hours until current regressions in logprobs and KV-cache alignment are addressed. --- ## Per-Project Reports
vLLM — vllm-project/vllm # vLLM Technical Digest: 2026-09-26 ### 1. Today's Highlights Development activity is heavily focused on refining **Speculative Decoding (MRV2)** and **DeepSeek-V4.1** inference performance, with a push toward fixing high-concurrency bugs in disaggregated serving environments (P/D). Significant engineering effort is currently being directed at optimizing Triton kernels for new hardware (SM100/GB200) and hardening the recently introduced Rust frontend. ### 2. Releases & Breaking Changes * **No new releases** in the last 24h. * **Note:** The Rust frontend (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`) remains experimental and is not yet feature-equivalent to the Python server; users should track progress via [#44280](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/44280). ### 3. New Model & Hardware Support * **DeepSeek-V4.1:** Active performance optimization for SM100/SM103 architectures, including specific kernel fusions for O-projection and wkv projection ([#58634](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58634), [#58678](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58678)). * **ROCm/MI355X:** Ongoing performance optimization plan for `Qwen3.8-2.4T-A95B` on `gfx950` silicon ([#57149](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/57149)). ### 4. Performance & Optimization * **Kernel Fusions:** A massive 6x speedup achieved for Mamba block-table alignment by consolidating 7 kernels into one ([#58737](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58737)). * **Speculative Decoding:** * Host dispatch latency reduced by ~11us/step via optimized metadata building ([#58732](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58732)). * Adaptive verification (DSpark) showing ~179% increase in request throughput (0.83 -> 2.32 req/s) in specific GLM-5.2 benchmarks ([#52992](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/52992)). * **JIT Warmup:** New PR to cover sparse top-k and DFlash Triton specializations to prevent mid-inference JIT stalls ([#58559](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58559)). ### 5. Stability & Regressions * **Speculative Decoding/MRV2 (High Severity):** * [#58485](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/58485): Thinking budget corruption causing reasoning failures. * [#58784](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58784): MRV2 attempting to verify non-existent draft slots (Fix PR open). * **Tool-Calling (Medium Severity):** * [#55152](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/55152): Structural tag rejection in `llguidance` backend breaking `tool_choice` logic. * [#58792](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58792): Inkling tool names leaking into streaming output (Fix PR open). * **Scheduling/Streaming (Medium Severity):** * [#57447](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/57447): Logprobs not correctly preserved across streaming continuations (Fix PR open). ### 6. What This Means for Application Developers * **Disaggregated Serving (P/D):** If you are running complex multi-rank setups, be aware of ongoing fixes for Mooncake/KV-connector block alignment issues ([#55097](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/55097)). Data integrity here is being actively hardened. * **Tool-Calling/Agents:** If using `tool_choice` or complex streaming formats, be cautious with the latest stable releases as parser logic for reasoning and tool-calling is currently seeing heavy churn (especially regarding `inkling` and `qwen3` parsers). * **Infrastructure:** Ensure your monitoring accounts for the "KV cache reserved pool" vs "Active KV cache" as reported in [#43400](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/43400); vLLM’s pre-allocation strategy often results in high memory footprints that are standard, not leaks.
SGLang — sgl-project/sglang # SGLang Digest: 2026-09-26 ### 1. Today's Highlights The focus remains on stabilizing the DeepSeek-V4.1 architecture across diverse backends, with significant engineering effort migrating kernel operations to specialized `dsv4` namespaces to improve modularity and JIT performance. Infrastructure maintenance is elevated, with active CI hardening efforts and a shift toward adopting Rust-based tree cores for unified radix cache management. ### 2. Releases & Breaking Changes * **No official releases** recorded in the last 24h. * **Default Migration:** A major architectural shift is underway to make the **Rust TreeCore** the default for radix caching; PR [#39627](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39627) synchronizes Python/Rust behaviors to ensure a seamless transition for existing deployments. ### 3. New Model & Hardware Support * **DeepSeek-V4.1 (AMD/ROCm):** Substantial progress on AMD support, including implementation of FP4 indexer, compressor, and router kernels ([#41019](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41019)). * **Gemma 3/4:** Performance-focused kernel work continues for Gemma3n, specifically optimizing shared-KV attention to minimize memory overhead ([#41295](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41295)). * **XGrammar:** PR [#39380](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39380) adds support for Lark grammars, expanding the project's structured output capabilities. ### 4. Performance & Optimization * **DeepSeek-V4.1 Fusions:** New fusion kernels for Hopper architecture, including ratio-2 decode pooling and RMSNorm, aim to streamline the compute boundary ([#41294](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41294)). * **MoE Kernel Tuning:** Optimization for MXFP4 MoE runners on consumer hardware (e.g., RTX 4090) addresses severe throughput deficits by pinning `num_warps` in `triton_kernels` ([#41292](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41292)). * **General Optimization:** Sharing the CuTe DSL AR (All-Reduce) fusion core across DeepSeek and GLM-5.x families to ensure consistent high-performance scaling ([#37196](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/37196)). ### 5. Stability & Regressions * **[Critical] HiCache/Hybrid Models:** A bug in `attach_hybrid_pool_to_unified_cache` causes instance-wide crashes on secondary host pools due to unhandled `cudaHostRegister` failures ([#40926](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/40926)). * **[High] Logprob Leakage:** A bug in `process_batch_result_prefill` results in prompt logprobs being served to the incorrect request when batch members are retracted or finished ([#36938](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/36938)). * **[Medium] Apple Silicon:** OOM issues reported due to incorrect device memory capacity reporting for `mps`, causing `mem_fraction_static` to default to overly aggressive values ([#39675](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/39675)). * **[Medium] Memory Amplification:** Multimodal tensor views are triggering significant pickle memory amplification (518x), likely due to improper reference handling ([#33388](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/33388)). ### 6. What This Means for Application Developers * **Latency/Throughput:** If you are running DeepSeek-V4.1 or Gemma variants on high-end NVIDIA (Hopper) or consumer hardware, monitor upcoming updates closely, as kernel-level fusions are currently providing substantial efficiency gains. * **Stability:** If you utilize hybrid Mamba/SSM architectures or `HiCache`, be aware of the ongoing `cudaHostRegister` stability issues; it is recommended to verify your environment stability until the fix for [#40926](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/40926) is merged. * **Tooling:** If your agent workflow relies on specific grammar formats, the upcoming support for Lark via XGrammar will simplify the integration of complex schema constraints.

Stability & Regressions * **Unified KV-Cache Issues (High)**: Ongoing reports of verbatim response bleeding and prompt processing degradation in parallel/multi-tenant scenarios (`-np > 1`) on HIP/ROCm platforms [#25992](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/25992), [#28495](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/28495). * **Vulkan Compilation**: Fixed regression in cooperative matrix support for legacy `glslc` versions [#29409](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29409). * **Server Endpoints**: Improved error handling for embedding requests to prevent internal 500 errors [#29060](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29060). #### 6. What This Means for Application Developers * **Multi-tenant Reliability**: If you are deploying `llama-server` in production with parallel slots (`-np`), be aware of the ongoing instability in the unified KV-cache kernels. Monitor logs for prompt processing degradation or incorrect response concatenation until the recent fixes/adjustments to `kv-unified` are fully validated. * **API Improvements**: Developers building tools on the server API should expect cleaner error states for malformed requests; moving to 400 status codes for client-side errors simplifies integration with standard API gateways. * **Quantization Strategy**: If you are bottlenecked by VRAM on CUDA, experiment with the new conversion chunking flag (`GGML_CUDA_CUBLAS_CONVERT_CHUNK_SIZE`) to trade a minor performance hit for improved model fit.

Releases & Breaking Changes * **No new releases in the last 24h.** * **Dependency Note:** TRL support ceiling is being lifted to `1.13.0` ([PR #11137](https://github​.com/unslothai/unsloth/pull/11137)), which may require dependency updates for users pinning strictly to older TRL versions. ### 3. items.title: Work: research — model GCP and migration-overlap cost scenarios
items.body:
## Outcome

A dated, reproducible public-price cost model with explicit low/expected/high assumptions and separate first-release, retained-store and migration-overlap totals, usable as preparation for later approvals without granting spend or operational authority.

## Authority, scope and parallelism

The maintainer explicitly authorized planning and ticket creation for these three independent read-only research tasks on 2026-09-07. This is the narrow early-discovery authorization permitted by #78, not early acceptance or implementation of a later milestone. The complete task definition is published before any lifecycle promotion; Ready remains unclaimed and subject to fresh admission.

Scope-Paths is none because no current or historical repository file may be changed. Inputs may be inspected read-only across workers; each task has its own report and checkpoint. The root session remains coordination-only. A later source/document/diagram/test/tooling change needs a separate bounded execution task, exact scope, dedicated worktree and applicable approvals.

Canonical shared plan: #2. Native grouping: #75. Downstream consumers: #75 first-release costed approval; separate later-phase estimates inform #78–#81. No output from this ticket accepts or releases those consumers.

## Inputs and evidence boundary

- Read the current AGENTS.md, SECURITY.md, docs/development/parallel-work.md, docs/current-status.md, docs/architecture/overview.md, docs/operations/deployment-composition.md, docs/operations/delivery.md, infra/README.md and infra/bootstrap.md, plus #2/#75/#77/#78 and current checkpoints. Read current IaC as unapplied source, not as a live resource inventory.
- The accepted first-release baseline is separate web/API containers on Cloud Run, Artifact Registry and Google Cloud telemetry in us-west1, OpenTofu/GCS state, short-lived federation and interim provider URLs. No required standing staging environment or load balancer is assumed for M1.
- Use official public pricing and quota documentation for Google Cloud, Neon, Scaleway and Vercel, plus applicable public CI and external tooling/agent prices. Reading public documentation needs no cloud account access. Cite dates, currencies, regions, tiers and units; unavailable or contract-only prices remain explicit unknowns or parameterized lines, never zero.
- No USD 30/month ceiling applies. The request is transparent estimates, measured attribution, configurable alerts and bounded resources, not unlimited spend. Actual bills, account plans, usage, traffic, data sizes and exact migration duration are not available inputs and must not be invented or fetched from provider accounts.
- This model requires neither dashboard nor producer inventory completion. Use explicit scenarios and replace assumptions only when corroborated evidence arrives. M1 operation approval still requires its exact then-current revision, bounds and authorization under #75; this research is not that approval packet.

## Bounded work

- Model first-release web/API compute including idle/startup and probes, request/CPU/memory/concurrency assumptions; registry/artifact storage and scans/builds; GCS state/versioning/backups; telemetry ingestion/retention/query; secrets; networking; safe temporary validation/recovery resources; and CI plus external tooling/agent costs. Separate recurring fixed, usage-based and temporary charges.
- Keep retained Neon/Scaleway and continuing Vercel charges in distinct later-migration/overlap worksheets rather than silently charging them to M1 or assuming they disappear. Include cross-cloud GCP-to-Neon/Scaleway and dashboard egress directions, request costs, retention, temporary copies and overlap duration assumptions; do not propose moving the retained providers.
- Treat optional domain/load-balancer services as separate later scenarios, not a required M1 baseline. Label free-tier/credit/discount eligibility and avoid relying on it without evidence or counting shared allowances more than once. Record taxes, currency conversion and unsupported price terms explicitly.
- Propose cost attribution dimensions, configurable alert inputs and measurable concurrency/retry/retention/resource bounds with a cost/safety rationale. These are recommendations and verification questions only: no alert, budget, hard cap, account, provider query or cloud resource is created or changed.

## Acceptance

- [x] Deliver a dated source-price table and transparent units/formulas, with low/expected/high usage assumptions. Each modeled amount is traceable to an official rate and scenario; unsupported prices and missing account-specific terms stay visible and parameterized.
- [x] Provide separate subtotals for M1 recurring and temporary validation, retained-store/Vercel overlap, later optional hosting changes, and external CI/tooling/agent costs. Show billed-direction networking assumptions and avoid double-counting compute, free allowances, shared stores or overlap.
- [x] Validate arithmetic independently by recomputing representative line items and all scenario totals; show sensitivity to traffic, minimum instances, probes, retention, egress and overlap duration. Do not present assumed usage or provisional totals as measurements or a firm invoice forecast.
- [x] Provide a measurement/attribution and configurable-alert checklist naming evidence needed later, proposed bounded-resource inputs and stop/escalation questions. Do not claim alerts, cost notifications or runtime bounds are configured or verified.
- [x] Give #75 a first-release estimate summary and explicit revalidation requirements tied to its future exact reviewed revision; give later milestones distinct retained-provider/overlap assumptions to refine just in time. No fixed USD 30 ceiling, unlimited-spend authority or operational approval is introduced.
- [x] Deliver a public-safe Markdown report plus a reconstructable CSV/JSON table or equivalent formula table in this issue's supported checkpoint/handoff. Record sources, calculation method, included/excluded components, confidence and exactly what remains unknown; use synthetic/scenario values only.
- [x] Verify no billing/account identifiers, credentials, production usage records, private discounts, raw IaC state/plans or sensitive diagnostics were collected or published, and no provider, host, repository file, budget, alert or deployment was changed.

## Deliverable and handoff

A dated public-safe price/source table, reproducible scenario worksheet, separate phase subtotals, sensitivity analysis, and attribution/alert/input checklist. Publish compact sanitized tables or code blocks through this issue's supported checkpoint/handoff; working files remain outside repository worktrees. Account-specific evidence and authorization are deferred to their separately approved private process.

Completion means the report satisfies the checks above and its declared review/handoff is accurately recorded, not that a file exists or code CI is green. Missing operational facts must be explicit and routed to later verification, not guessed. Do not mark any implementation milestone complete or expand this task to resolve excluded questions. Other issue/plan updates and any principal handoff follow their separate authority; an agent cannot dismiss its own claim history.

## Exclusions

# OpenClaw Ecosystem Digest 2026-11-07 > Issues: 365 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-11-07 02:20 UTC - [OpenClaw](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw) - [Hermes Agent](https://github​.com/nousresearch/hermes-agent) - [IronClaw](https://github​.com/nearai/ironclaw) - [QwenPaw](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw) - [ZeroClaw](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw) --- ## OpenClaw Deep Dive # OpenClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-07 --- ## 1. Today's Overview OpenClaw remains in a high-velocity, high-contention maintenance phase: **365 issues** and **500 pull requests** were updated in the last 24 hours, with **160 issues closed** (43.8% of touched issues) and **123 PRs merged/closed** (~24.6% of touched PRs). No new release shipped today, and the most-commented issue in the tracker is a **P0 crash-loop regression** ([#160959](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/160959), 80 comments) that has been open since late September, signaling that some release-blocking defects are outliving multiple release cycles. The PR queue is the main health concern: **377 PRs remain open** versus 123 closed today, and a visible share of the top-commented PRs are drafts, placeholders, or "needs proof" candidates rather than merge-ready work. Activity is strong, but throughput is skewed toward intake and triage rather than landing fixes — consistent with a project under heavy user load and aggressive automated triage (`clawsweeper:*` labels on nearly every issue). --- ## 2. Releases **No new releases today.** The Latest Releases section is empty. Context from issue traffic: the current stable line appears to be **2026.10.10**, with a prerelease **2026.11.5-beta.1** referenced in [#141474](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/141474) and [#193962](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/193962). Notably, [#193962](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/193962) reports that affected users on 2026.10.10 **cannot reach the fix in 2026.11.5-beta.1 via `openclaw update`** because the installed updater's 10-second SQLite header probe times out — a distribution-channel blocker worth prioritizing before the next stable cut. --- ## 3. Project Progress **Merged/closed PRs today (selected):** | PR | Change | |---|---| | [#194384](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194384) | `fix(cron)`: one-shot finalization and enable/disable transitions now work on PostgreSQL 16 (`function json(unknown) does not exist`); also repairs PostgreSQL 18 cache conformance assertion | | [#194399](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194399) | `fix(media)`: interrupted attachment downloads are now cancelled instead of running until process exit | | [#194407](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194407) | `fix(ci)`: preserves compiled-worker reuse when Vitest metadata grows | | [#194405](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194405) | `test(ui)`: fixes flaky configured-provider icon test (scheduled run 42319656353) | | [#194411](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194411) | `fix(plugins)`: restores missing OpenClaw ID Access artwork (unblocks artwork check) | | [#194190](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194190) | `fix(ui)`: same-day timestamps show time only in tight rows | | [#194152](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194152) | `ui`: dialog closes and ghost icon actions unified onto `IconButton` | **Issues closed today (selected):** [#166017](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/166017) (MCP session idle-TTL default not applied → 256-child spawn-broker exhaustion), [#178291](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/178291) (P0: 2026.10.4→10.5 chat update fails post-activation Doctor), [#164923](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164923) (short-term promotion 0/512 in one workspace), [#155457](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/155457) (Anthropic malformed streamed JSON args), [#168794](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/168794) (Codex relay >32 MiB image → 502), [#165433](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/165433) (reconnect envelope rejection), [#164690](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164690) (duplicate stdio MCP spawn under `claude-cli`). **Assessment:** the day's landed work is predominantly **correctness and CI/test-hygiene**, not user-facing features. The most consequential closure is [#166017](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/166017) — a hard-cap exhaustion bug that bricked all exec/read/MCP starts — but the fix is not yet confirmed shipped in a stable release. --- ## 4. Community Hot Topics **#160959 — [P0] Gateway blocks for minutes while capturing large external plugins (2026.9.6 regression)** · 80 comments · [link](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/160959) The single hottest thread in the project. Since plugin generation capture landed (#144252), a Gateway with a large external/workspace plugin dependency tree blocks its event loop for **minutes** at startup and on every prepared-runtime republish. Labeled `impact:crash-loop`, `P0`, `clawsweeper:no-new-fix-pr`. The underlying need is architectural: plugin capture must move off the main V8 thread or become incremental/cached. Related liveness evidence appears in [#166641](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/166641) (`web_fetch` fallback synchronously capturing plugins). **#164294 — Gateway state DB WAL auto-checkpoint never completes** · 39 comments · [link](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164294) A PASSIVE checkpoint is pinned by an in-process reader (`checkpointedFrames=866`, `logFrames=17091`, `consecutiveBlocked` climbing). Users are effectively watching unbounded WAL growth with no remediation path. Needs a long-lived-reader audit of `state/openclaw.sqlite`. **#177656 — [P1] Native host exec returns shared-state integrity-admission error** · 30 comments · [link](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/177656) ≥28 failures on stable 2026.10.5, child effects unproved, no fix. Error: `Direct shared-state reader requires current integrity admission`. This is the highest-severity issue without a linked fix PR. **#150635 — Dreaming deep phase never promotes (short-term recall eviction)** · 25 comments · [link](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/150635) At the 512-entry cap, nightly ingestion stages hundreds of zero-recall entries that evict genuinely recalled ones, so promotion never occurs. Coupled with [#164923](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164923) (closed today), this points to a systemic **memory-tier capacity/eviction policy** problem rather than two isolated bugs. **#191944 — `gateway stop` / `stop --force` fail on macOS** · 23 comments · [link](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191944) `ServiceInspectionError: Process ancestry could not be fully inspected`. A basic lifecycle operation is broken on a first-class desktop platform — high UX blast radius for low implementation complexity. **PR-side:** the most notable open candidates are [#194376](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194376) (`feat(gateway)`: admission boundary for `sessions_send` wake starts — addresses concurrent-sender bypass of batching/rate limits), [#182383](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182383) (`feat(plugin-sdk)`: access-policy revision caching, security-sensitive), and [#194133](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/194133) (UI menu-row anatomy normalization). The queue also contains explicit non-work — [#191509](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191509) ("empty iOS handoff placeholder — do not use") and [#188726](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188726) (investigation placeholder) — which inflates the open count. --- ## 5. Bugs & Stability Ranked by severity. "Fix PR" indicates a linked/merged candidate exists in the data. | Sev | Issue | Symptom | Fix PR? | |---|---|---|---| | **P0** | [#160959](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/160959) | Gateway event-loop blocked for minutes by plugin capture; crash-loop | No | | **P1** | [#177656](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/177656) | Native host exec: shared-state integrity-admission error, 28+ occurrences | No | | **P1** | [#191847](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191847) | 2026.10.10 regression: large session repeatedly OOMs the 512 MB SQLite worker; **every** turn fails with "admission is closed" | No | | **P1** | [#192959](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/192959) | Gateway refuses to start after K8s pod restart (fsGroup remount invalidates client credential dir) | No | | **P1** | [#185656](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/185656) | Large zstd transcript archive exceeds Node string limit in media-persistence migration — **regression of #170847 despite merged fix #170853**; blocks updates | Merged but ineffective | | **P1** | [#182647](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/182647) | Cloud-worker turns fail pre-inference: "Session capability metadata requires worker preparation" | `queueable-fix` | | **P1** | [#166641](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/166641) | `web_fetch` cold fallback synchronously captures plugins on Gateway main thread → liveness stalls (V8 profile captured) | No | | **P1** | [#155563](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/155563) | 2026.9.5 regression: `service-child-relay`/`group-anchor`/MCP groups retained after successful turn | No | | **P1** | [#126950](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/126950) | Telegram `tgcb1:` opaque callback payloads silently dropped for non-plugin callers (message loss) | Linked PR open | | **P1** | [#157182](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/157182) | Control UI forces `/chat/main` and retries forever when ambient main session isn't visible (security-flagged) | No | | **P1** | [#162087](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/162087) | 9.7: scheduled `announce` fails for pre-9.7 account-mode cron jobs (missing `ownerOrigin`) | No | | **P2** | [#164294](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164294) | WAL checkpoint permanently blocked | No | | **P2** | [#141474](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/141474) | `sessions_yield` strands `agents_wait` forever; `outputSchema` inert on `claude-cli` — **fix only in 2026.11.5-beta.1, not stable** | In prerelease | | **P2** | [#193962](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/193962) | SQLite header-probe timeout fix (#187197) unreachable from 2026.10.10 via `openclaw update` | Fix exists, distribution blocked | | **P2** | [#182891](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/182891) | Prompt cache never reused — `cache read dropped N -> 0` on every request | No | | **P2** | [#191944](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/191944) | macOS gateway stop fails (process ancestry inspection) | No | | **P2** | [#158127](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/158127) | 2026.9.6 multi-agent runtime publication failures + Codex startup timeouts | No | | **P2** | [#167609](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/167609) | Code Mode reports guest TypeErrors as `internal_error` (live repro on main `e29577b7d7d`) | `fix-shape-clear` | | **P2** | [#123792](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/123792) | Assistant turns persisted/rendered twice with `claude-cli` backend | No | **Stability read:** the dominant failure cluster is **Gateway main-thread blocking and SQLite worker pressure** (#160959, #166641, #191847, #164294, #185656). A second cluster is **runtime lifecycle leakage** (#155563, #166017 now closed, #164690 closed). A third is **update/installation integrity** (#185656, #193962, #178291) — worrying because it can trap users on known-bad versions. Two P1 regressions (#185656, #191847) are confirmed present in the current stable line. --- ## 6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals **Cost & observability** - [#13219](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/13219) — Per-model usage logging for cost tracking (open since Feb 2026, 10 comments, 👍1). Repeatedly reinforced by [#143017](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/143017) (21.3M cache-write tokens measured) and [#130257](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/130257) (delegated ACP child run $14.14 vs parent $0.04, unattributable). **Strong candidate for near-term roadmap**: three independent cost-visibility issues with production numbers attached. - [#178373](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/178373) — No run-level turn/token budget; tool-loop detection opt-in (defaults off); retained history re-billed every turn. **Agent/session management** - [#166678](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/166678) — Hide agents from pickers while keeping them spawnable (WebUI/macOS/iOS), 👍1. - [#158800](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/158800) — Browse/fork prior channel-chat segments after `/new` in Control UI. - [#103067](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/103067) — Centralize chat-session naming; define subagent session lifetime & cross-channel persistence. **Channels & integrations** - [#136271](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/136271) — msteams: dynamically resolve team SharePoint site for channel uploads. - [#162087](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/162087) — cron `announce` account-mode ownership (bug, but drives a delivery-model decision). **UX & configuration** - [#163739](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/163739) — Make Ctrl+Shift+A (Archive) configurable; collides with browser shortcuts, 👍1. Low effort, clear win. - [#79223](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/79223) — Configurable Dream Diary language (hardcoded English prompt in `memory-core`), 👍2 — a recurring complaint from non-English workspaces. - [#164620](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/164620) — Setting to disable the hosted plugin catalog feed (`clawhub.ai` hardcoded). - [#130247](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/130247) — Cron jobs cannot end: no `--until`/`--max-runs`, no cumulative run counter. **Prediction:** the highest-probability next-cycle items are **cost/usage aggregation (#13219 family)**, **cron lifecycle bounds (#130247)**, and **keybinding configurability (#163739)** — all are narrow, well-specified, and backed by repeated reports. The memory/dreaming work (#150635, #79223) likely needs a design decision (`clawsweeper:needs-product-decision`) before implementation. --- ## 7. User Feedback Summary **Pain points, by frequency of signal:** 1. **Startup/upgrade fragility.** Users on 2026.9.6→2026.10.10 report Gateways that block for minutes, migrations that fail on large archives, and updates that cannot be applied to escape the broken version (#160959, #185656, #193962, #178291). This is the single largest source of dissatisfaction. 2. **Memory feature disappointment.** The "dreaming"/short-term-recall system is widely reported as not working as advertised — 0/512 promotion in one workspace while siblings hit 50–90% (#164923, #150635). Users are doing careful comparative debugging themselves, which suggests documentation/observability gaps. 3. **Cost opacity.** Multiple users quantify large, unattributable spend (#143017: 21.3M cache-write tokens; #130257: 100× parent/child cost asymmetry). The prompt cache is reported as never reused (#182891), directly converting into billed tokens. 4. **Platform-specific lifecycle breakage.** macOS `gateway stop` (#191944), Kubernetes fsGroup restarts (#192959), Android polling an unknown agent every 0.8 s (#167316, closed). Desktop/container users feel like second-class citizens relative to the Linux systemd path. 5. **Multi-agent complexity.** Runtime publication superseded errors, Codex startup timeouts, duplicate MCP spawns, 145 MB wrapper overhead per stdio child (#158127, #164690, #164017-family). Operators running many agents report unpredictable resource growth. **Satisfaction signals:** reports are consistently detailed, reproducible, and version-pinned — the user base is technically sophisticated and invested. Several closures today (#166017, #164923, #178291) drew substantive multi-week threads, indicating users do track fixes through to resolution. The main dissatisfaction is **time-to-fix on P0/P1 items**, not responsiveness to reports. --- ## 8. Backlog Watch **Long-unanswered, high-value issues:** | Age | Item | Why it matters | |---|---|---| | ~9 months | [#13219](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/13219) Per-model usage logging (Feb 2026) | Cheapest possible answer to the loudest cost complaints; still `needs-product-decision` | | ~6 months | [#79223](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/79223) Dream Diary language (May 2026) | Hardcoded prompt in `memory-core`; trivial fix, international users blocked | | ~4 months | [#112638](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/112638) `session.maintenance` enforce mode doesn't bound the store | Silent unbounded disk growth; `maxEntries`/`maxDiskBytes` are effectively advisory | | ~4 months | [#103067](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/103067) Centralize chat-session naming / subagent lifetime | Foundational for multi-agent UX; keeps generating duplicate reports | | ~3 months | [#126950](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/126950) Telegram opaque callbacks dropped | Message loss on a primary channel; linked PR open but stalled | | ~3 months | [#130247](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/130247) / [#130257](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/130257) Cron has no end condition; ACP run cost unattributable | Both filed by the same operator; scheduler lacks basic lifecycle semantics | | ~2.5 months | [#123792](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/123792) Double-rendered assistant turns (`claude-cli`) | Visible data-integrity/UX defect on Control UI + Android | **Stale PRs needing maintainer attention:** - [#75225](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/75225) — `feat(agents)`: expose configured descriptions in `agents_list`. Open since **2026-04-30**, `proof: sufficient`, `status: ⏳ waiting on maintainer`. Over six months with a sufficient proof packet is a process failure, not a technical one. - [#125969](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/125969) — `fix(gateway)`: scope image capability discovery. Open since 2026-08-18, `ready for maintainer look`. - [#130231](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/130231) — `ci(i18n)`: non-publishing locale refresh. Open since 2026-08-26, flagged `merge-risk: 🚨 security-boundary`, `needs proof`. - [#182383](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/182383) — `feat(plugin-sdk)`: access-policy revision caching (XL, security-sensitive). Needs a security reviewer, not more author iteration. - [#161362](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/161362) — `fix(agents)`: stop warning that documented core tool groups need a plugin. `security-review-required`, waiting on author since 2026-09-29. **Recommendation:** the open-PR backlog (377) is now large enough to obscure real work — several top-listed PRs are explicitly non-mergeable placeholders ([#191509](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/191509), [#188726](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/188726)). Closing or converting those to draft issues, and prioritizing the two P0/P1 regressions with no fix PR ([#160959](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/160959), [#177656](https://github​.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/177656)), would materially improve both perceived and actual project health. --- ## Cross-Ecosystem Comparison ⚠️ Comparative analysis generation failed. --- ## Peer Project Reports

PR [#8610](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8610) opened today | **High** — backward-compatible default `full` | | **Model deletion in Console model pool** | [#8195](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8195) → [#8410](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8410) / [#8611](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8611) | Two competing PRs | **High**, but **PR duplication needs maintainer arbitration** | | **Tab title reflects current session name** | [#8605](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8605) | New, 1 comment | Medium — small, well-localized (`KB` component, route-name-only title source) | | **Creator UI overhaul** (button contrast, model-start state desync, forced shared API key across image/video/LLM models) | [#8591](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8591) | New, 1 comment | Medium — #3 (per-modality credentials) is a config-model change, not just UI | | **Reranker model center** with service test, multi-query precision history, auto-verify | PR [#8472](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8472) | Open, size/XXL, under review since 2026-10-28 | Medium — large surface, mirrors existing Embedding model center | | **Cross-agent collaboration guidance & identity model** | [#2420](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/2420) | Closed after 7.5 months, no linked PR | **Low near-term** — closed as feedback, but the need is structural | **Prediction:** the 2.3.x line likely ships **Console polish** (#8608, #8609, #8611, tab titles), **IM channel display control** (#8610), and **provider/model config validation hardening** (#8550, #8607). The memory subsystem (reranker center #8472, tag index #8580) is the most likely **2.4** headline feature area. --- ## 7. User Feedback Summary **Pain points, in order of frequency:** 1. **Silent failures with useless error messages.** The single most repeated complaint: reranker enabled with empty key → "unexpected error" ([#8276](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8276)); out-of-range config accepted → provider silently disappears ([#8549](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8549)); tags generated → index never built → 503 ([#8580](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8580)). Users are doing the debugging work themselves and locating exact file/line — a sign the project is **under-instrumented**, not under-documented. 2. **Windows is a second-class platform.** GBK/CP936 files silently byte-stripped by `errors="ignore"` ([#8234](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8234)); `\\?\` path canonicalization breaking SQLite URIs ([#8585](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8585)); hanging cancellation tests ([#8604](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8604)). Chinese Windows users are a **core, vocal constituency** — the GBK report describes Notepad/legacy `.txt`/`.csv`/`.md` notes losing data with **no log line**. 3. **Deployment friction in constrained environments.** Air-gapped/offline installs where Qwen3/3.5 are unreachable but DeepSeek R1 works ([#1453](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/1453)); non-root Docker Hub startup failure ([#8517](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8517)); nginx reverse-proxy SSE buffering ([#8516](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8516)). Self-hosted enterprise users are hitting **first-run blockers**. 4. **Plugin ecosystem immaturity.** Install fails with a bare "No package metadata was found" ([#8595](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8595)); plugin routes break sidebar state ([#8590](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8590)). The extension API is being used, but **the loading/registration contract is still leaky**. **Use cases evidenced:** multi-workspace Matrix bridging, cross-agent collaboration and delegation, Creator (image/video generation) pipelines, offline/air-gapped deployment, third-party backend routing (Codex/Qoder/Kimi), scheduled agent tasks over IM, and long-term memory recall. **Satisfaction signals:** reporters are precise, reproducible, and cooperative ("Happy to split this into three issues"); first-time contributors are filing docs fixes ([#8606](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8606)) and validation patches ([#8550](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8550)). **Dissatisfaction signals:** zero 👍 across the entire window, repeated "permanently broken / never rebuilds / cannot be decided" phrasing, and a 7.5-month-old collaboration-feedback thread closed without a linked fix. --- ## 8. Backlog Watch Items needing maintainer attention, ranked by risk: 1. **[#8580](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8580) — Memory tag index 503** · OPEN, 4 comments, **no fix PR, no assignee signal** Highest-severity open bug with no owner. Every user who enables `auto_memory_generate_tags` is silently broken. 2. **[#8592](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8592) — Creator REJECT permanently 422** · OPEN, 3 defects bundled Needs a maintainer decision on **splitting into three Issues** so defect 1 (the blocker) isn't buried under defects 2–3. 3. **[#8517](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8517) — Hub Docker non-root Permission denied** · OPEN since 2026-10-31 Blocks a whole deployment class; reporter could not even capture a version tag, which itself hints at packaging/tagging gaps. 4. **[#8410](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8410) vs [#8611](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8611) — duplicate "remove models from pool" work** Two contributors solving the same Issue ([#8195](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8195)). **Needs immediate arbitration** to avoid contributor burnout — this is the clearest process risk in today's data. 5. **[#8234](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8234) & [#8236](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8236) — size/XXL & XL, open since 2026-10-14, "Under Review"** GBK/CP936 decoding fix (data-loss class) and Ollama `num_ctx` context-window fix have been sitting **3+ weeks** without merge. Both are high user impact; #8234 in particular silently destroys user file content. 6. **[#8472](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8472) — reranker model center, size/XXL** · open since 2026-10-28 Large feature PR with no review comments recorded; at risk of bit-rot. 7. **[#8100](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8100) — resolved media capabilities at runtime** · open since 2026-10-03 (**5+ weeks**) A one-line-class correctness fix (image-capable models rejected and image content stripped) stuck in review. Also **[#8274](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8274)** (chat-switch state loss, since 2026-10-16). 8. **[#5110](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/5110) — Quote/reference for follow-up** · open since 2026-06-11 Now unblocked by [#8609](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/pull/8609); the Issue should be linked to the PR so it closes on merge. 9. **[#2420](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/2420) — cross-agent identity confusion** · CLOSED with no linked fix Closed as feedback, but "identity confusion between agents" and "collaboration coherence" are **architectural**, not cosmetic. Recommend a follow-up design Issue so the closure doesn't read as dismissal. --- **Bottom line:** QwenPaw is in a **productive, contributor-driven consolidation phase** — high fix throughput, fast issue-to-PR turnaround, and a clear focus on validation, lifecycle correctness, and Console ergonomics. The risks are concentrated in (a) **four critical open bugs with no fix PR**, (b) **duplicate/competing PRs** on the model-management path, and (c) a **review queue of large PRs aging 3–5 weeks**. A 2.3.x patch release closing [#8549](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8549), [#8533](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8533), [#8596](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8596) and [#8365](https://github​.com/agentscope-ai/QwenPaw/issues/8365) would be a well-supported next step.
ZeroClaw — zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw # ZeroClaw Project Digest — 2026-11-07 ## 1. Today's Overview ZeroClaw is in a high-throughput hardening phase: 17 issues were touched in the last 24h (10 closed, 7 open/active) and 50 PRs were updated (14 merged/closed, 36 still open), with **no new release**. The closed-issue set is dominated by security and identity-access fixes — OIDC bearer verification limits (#12047), X-Forwarded-For spoofing (#12052), RPC session exhaustion (#11962) and a RUSTSEC-blocking dependency (#12272) — indicating the maintainers are clearing a release-gate backlog rather than shipping features. At the same time, several new S1/S2 defects landed today, including a permanently poisoned provider session (#12263) and a boot-time transcript overwrite that risks message loss (#12279). Overall project health looks strong on responsiveness (fast close rate, multiple follow-up PRs filed within hours), but the open security-adjacent bugs in approval and peer-resolution paths deserve attention. *Data note: only 2 of the 14 merged/closed PRs and the top 20 of 50 updated PRs were included in the supplied dataset; PR comment counts were unavailable.* ## 2. Releases No new releases in the last 24h, and none listed in the latest-release feed. No changelog, breaking-change or migration notes to report. Several open PRs carry the `release:v0.9.0` label (#9746, #12239, #12270, #12282), suggesting the next version is being staged but is not yet cut. ## 3. Project Progress **Closed issues (10) — fixes landed or resolved:** | Issue | Area | Outcome | |---|---|---| | [#12047](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12047) | Gateway / OIDC | Attempt limiter + outbound cap added via [PR #12233](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12233) | | [#12052](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12052) | Gateway / XFF spoofing | Rate-limit keying moved to proxy-appended hop via [PR #12114](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12114) | | [#11962](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/11962) | Runtime / daemon | Idle RPC sessions now releasable (64-session cap) | | [#12176](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12176) | Tools / MCP | Deferred tool list ordering stabilized — restores prompt caching | | [#12272](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12272) | Dependencies | `vodozemac` RUSTSEC-2026-0445 / -0451 unblocked; Security gate green again | | [#12248](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12248) | Runtime / approval | No approval prompt for tool names absent from the turn | | [#12178](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12178) | Tools | `deliver_file` description no longer instructs URI citation in reply text | | [#12155](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12155) | Onboarding | Quickstart cancel message now matches actual config state | | [#12217](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12217) | Docs | Email tools-only setup clarified re: IMAP listener | | [#12249](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12249) | Gateway / web | Config pages hidden from accounts lacking `config` grant | **Notable open PRs advancing work:** [PR #12281](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12281) (forwarded-loopback SOP cancel fix, follow-up to #12114), [PR #12239](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12239) (holding authority through session effects, p1/release-gate), [PR #12276](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12276) (streaming Telegram voice synthesis), [PR #12275](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12275) (MCP local config controls), [PR #12270](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12270) (daemon dashboard via relay, #10315 phase 2). ## 4. Community Hot Topics 1. **[Issue #10926](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10926)** — *Matrix `send_via` treats peer user identities as room destinations* — **9 comments**, open since 2026-09-17, labeled `status:accepted`, `priority:p2`, `risk:medium`. The most-discussed item in the window. Underlying need: a coherent distinction between *peer identity* and *channel destination* in the outbound routing model — the same conceptual gap appears in today's #12283 (peer-group `ignore` handling) and in [PR #12116](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/12116) (Discord peer rejection). Three separate reports point to peer-resolution semantics being the project's most fragile abstraction. 2. **[Issue #12047](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12047)** (3 comments, closed) and **[Issue #12052](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12052)** (2 comments, closed) — both identity-access gateway bugs reported by the same author and fixed within days. Underlying need: operators deploying behind reverse proxies and external IdPs want *consistent* trust-boundary rules across pairing, webhook, enrollment and config routes. 3. **Long-running high-risk PRs** — [#9809](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9809) (multi-model provider profiles, open since 2026-08-07, `needs-author-action`), [#9746](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/9746) (per-agent ownership scoping, `priority:p1`, `release-gate`), [#11076](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/pull/11076) (`agy_cli` tool, `size:XL`). These carry the widest label sets and touch many subsystems; they are the de facto centers of design debate even without visible comment counts. ## 5. Bugs & Stability Ranked by severity as reported: | Severity | Issue | Status | Fix PR? | |---|---|---|---| | **S1 — workflow blocked** | [#12263](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12263) Strict provider rejects a long tool-heavy session **forever** (422 `missing field tool_call_id`); conversation permanently unusable after ~38 messages / ~10 tool rounds | OPEN | None visible | | **S1 — workflow blocked** | [#12272](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12272) `vodozemac` 0.11.0 RUSTSEC advisories fail `cargo deny` on every PR | CLOSED | Resolved same day | | **S2 (possibly S0)** | [#12279](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12279) Channel startup caps a long transcript without a lock, **overwriting a message appended in between** — data loss in a boot window; reporter notes triage may prefer S0 | OPEN | None visible | | **S2 — security** | [#12260](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12260) RPC `cron/add` and `cron/patch` pass `approved = true` for shell commands, treating any RPC caller as an operator approval | OPEN | None visible | | **S2 — security** | [#12283](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/12283) `resolve_peer_set` applies peer-group `ignore` per group over a `HashMap`, so outbound sends can reach ignored peers | OPEN (filed today) | None visible | | **S2** | [#10926](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issues/10926) Matrix `send_via` misroutes to peer user identity as a room | OPEN, accepted | None visible | | **S2** | [#11962](https://github​.com/zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw/issu --- > ⚠️ 内容超过 GitHub Issue 上限，完整报告见提交的 Markdown 文件。

# AI CLI Tools Community Digest 2026-11-11 > Generated: 2026-11-11 02:12 UTC | Tools covered: 7 - [Claude Code](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code) - [OpenAI Codex](https://github​.com/openai/codex) - [Gemini CLI](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) - [GitHub Copilot CLI](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli) - [OpenCode](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode) - [Pi](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi) - [Qwen Code](https://github​.com/QwenLM/qwen-code) - [Claude Code Skills](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills) --- ## Cross-Tool Comparison # **Cross-Tool AI CLI Ecosystem Comparison Report** *Generated: 2026-11-11 | For Technical Decision-Makers & Developers* --- ### **1. Ecosystem Overview** The AI CLI tool landscape in late 2026 is characterized by rapid evolution toward **multi-agent orchestration**, **enterprise-grade reliability**, and **cross-platform consistency**. While all major tools are converging on core capabilities—session persistence, model governance, and secure agent execution—differences in maturity, infrastructure, and community engagement are becoming pronounced. Stability issues dominate feedback across platforms, signaling that the industry has moved beyond feature velocity to prioritize **trust, control, and operational resilience**. The emergence of dedicated agent ecosystems (e.g., OpenCode’s subagent limits, Gemini’s `BeforeSubAgent` hooks) reflects a shift from single-model assistants to programmable, collaborative AI workflows. --- ### **2. Activity Comparison** | Tool | Issues (Top 10) | PRs (Last 24h) | Discussions | Release Status | Notes | |------|------------------|------------------|-------------|----------------|-------| | **Claude Code** | 10 | 1 | N/A | ✅ v2.1.322 | Slow feature delivery despite rising demand; UX regressions prominent | | **OpenAI Codex** | 10 | 10 | 5 | ✅ Stable + Alpha | High activity; security fixes dominant; strong community engagement | | **Gemini CLI** | 10 | 10 | N/A | ✅ v0.69.0-preview.0 | Active development; focus on subagent extensibility and safety | | **GitHub Copilot CLI** | 10 | 0 | N/A | ✅ v1.0.110-1 | Critical stability fixes; minimal PR progress; high-priority bugs unresolved | | **OpenCode** | 10 | 10 | N/A | ✅ v2.2.7 | Rapid iteration; urgent security concerns (sandboxing, STOP enforcement) | | **Pi** | 10 | 10 | 1 | ✅ v1.5.2 | Infrastructure upgrades (Chord stores, Radius sync); backend-first momentum | | **Qwen Code** | 10 | 10 | N/A | ✅ v0.27.2 | CI/CD instability persists; active testing and agent stability work | > 🔍 *Note*: GitHub Copilot CLI and Pi have discussions enabled but no threads reported in this digest. Others use Issues/PRs as primary channels. --- ### **3. Shared Feature Directions** Across the ecosystem, several cross-tool requirements reflect maturing developer expectations: - **Agent Security & Control** - **Tools**: OpenCode (#2242), Gemini CLI (#15272), Pi (#11928), Qwen Code (#16497) - **Need**: Sandboxing agents to prevent unauthorized file system access; enforce explicit `STOP` commands; prevent auto-approval of destructive actions. - **Session Persistence & Continuity** - **Tools**: Claude Code (#107232), OpenAI Codex (#56655), OpenCode (#62991), Qwen Code (#15738), Pi (#10956) - **Need**: Long-running sessions (>5 min) without timeout or state loss; stable resume behavior across reboots and updates. - **Cross-Platform Consistency** - **Tools**: OpenAI Codex (#57641), Qwen Code (#16863), Pi (#10074), Gemini CLI (#15272) - **Need**: Uniform behavior across Windows/macOS/Linux—especially in UI rendering, browser access, and Unicode handling. - **Model Visibility & Governance** - **Tools**: Claude Code (#108898), GitHub Copilot CLI (#5369), OpenCode (#63216), Pi (#11969) - **Need**: Transparent model selection, fallback logic, and ability to block specific models (e.g., Fable 5.2) in Auto/Fusion modes. - **Developer Experience & Debuggability** - **Tools**: All tools report UI feedback gaps (e.g., missing generating indicators), flaky tests, and poor error visibility. --- ### **4. Differentiation Analysis** | Dimension | Key Observations | |---------|------------------| | **Feature Focus** | - **Claude Code**: Scalability (Vertex fast mode), multi-agent collaboration, and enterprise workflow integration. - **OpenAI Codex**: Core stability, macOS signing, and TUI optimization—security-first engineering. - **Gemini CLI**: Subagent architecture, async execution, and research-mode experimentation. - **GitHub Copilot CLI**: Enterprise access control (GHE, CIDR), password input via agent commands, and model routing. - **OpenCode**: Agent sandboxing, security hardening, and local inference support (LM Studio). - **Pi**: Backend infrastructure (Chord store migration, Radius sync), provider flexibility (Entra ID), and session recovery. - **Qwen Code**: Web Shell integrations (WeChat/QQ/email), team collaboration, and managed agent resilience. | **Target Users** | - **Enterprise DevOps**: GitHub Copilot CLI, Pi, OpenAI Codex (Azure OpenAI support). - **Agent Builders & Researchers**: Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Pi (subagent hooks, async exec, Chord storage). - **Cross-Platform Devs**: OpenAI Codex, Qwen Code (multilingual, mobile-friendly UI). - **China-focused Teams**: Qwen Code (WeChat/QQ integration), OpenCode (local model support). | **Technical Approach** | - **Pi & Gemini CLI**: Emphasis on internal state management (Chord stores, lifecycle hooks). - **OpenCode & Qwen Code**: Push for agent-level security (sandboxing, permission gating). - **OpenAI Codex & GitHub Copilot CLI**: Focus on client-side stability and network resilience. --- ### **5. Community Momentum & Maturity** - **Highest Momentum**: - **OpenAI Codex** and **Qwen Code** show the most consistent activity (10+ PRs/day, active discussions, frequent releases). - **OpenCode** and **Gemini CLI** are rapidly iterating on foundational agent capabilities—indicative of a **high-maturity, innovation-led** ecosystem. - **Stalled or Declining Velocity**: - **Claude Code** has only one PR in 24h despite growing user demand—suggests **feature fatigue** or prioritization shifts. - **GitHub Copilot CLI** reports zero PRs in last 24h—despite critical bugs like `disable-model-invocation: true` breaking skills—raising concerns about **maintenance capacity**. - **Maturity Signal**: Tools with **structured subagent systems** (Gemini CLI, OpenCode, Pi) and **infrastructure-layer upgrades** (Pi’s Chord store migration) are demonstrating **platform-level maturity**, moving beyond CLI utilities to full-stack AI development environments. --- ### **6. Trend Signals** 1. **Security-by-Design is Non-Negotiable** > 7+ tools now cite sandboxing, `STOP` enforcement, and credential masking as top priorities. This signals that **AI code generation is no longer a “try-it-out” tool**—it must be safe for production use. 2. **Long-Running Workflows Are the New Benchmark** > API timeouts >5 minutes, silent session loss, and memory leaks are recurring themes. The industry is shifting from "quick fix" bots to **persistent, stateful AI collaborators**. 3. **Agent-to-Agent Communication Is the Next Frontier** > Multi-agent collaboration (Claude Code #28300), A2A auth (Gemini #17602), and subagent resumability (Gemini #17758) indicate a **move toward distributed AI teams**—not just individual assistants. 4. **Local & Offline Capabilities Are Gaining Traction** > LM Studio support (OpenCode), `llama.cpp` integration (Pi), and offline agent execution are increasingly requested—driven by privacy, cost, and compliance needs. 5. **Infrastructure Over UI Is the New Differentiator** > Tools investing in **session catalogs, storage backends (Chord), and sync protocols (Radius)** are building long-term value beyond GUI polish. --- ### ✅ **Recommendation for Developers & Teams** - **Prioritize tools with active PRs and robust agent architectures** (e.g., **Gemini CLI**, **OpenCode**, **Pi**) for scalable, secure AI workflows. - **Avoid tools with stalled PR pipelines** unless you can self-host or contribute fixes (e.g., **Claude Code**, **GitHub Copilot CLI**). - **Use open-source tools (OpenCode, Pi, Qwen Code)** for maximum control and auditability—especially in regulated environments. - **Monitor CI/CD stability**—flaky test suites (Qwen Code, OpenAI Codex) may indicate underlying architectural fragility. > 📌 *Bottom Line*: The AI CLI space is transitioning from **feature race** to **trust and reliability race**. Choose tools where community momentum aligns with your need for **security, persistence, and extensibility**. --- ## Per-Tool Reports
Claude Code — anthropics/claude-code ## Claude Code Skills Highlights > Source: [anthropics/skills](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills) **Claude Code Skills Community Highlights Report** *Data as of 2026-11-11 | Source: github.com/anthropics/skills* --- ### **1. Top Skills Ranking** *(Based on community engagement, PR complexity, and functional impact)* 1. **`proofcore-contract-auditor`** ([PR #1771](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1771)) - *Functionality*: Automated static analysis of Solidity/Rust smart contracts with cryptographic proof anchoring on the TON Blockchain via ProofCore’s zero-storage Merkle protocol. Targets Web3 developers needing trustless audit trails. - *Discussion Highlights*: High interest from blockchain developers; praised for bridging AI reasoning with decentralized verification. - *Status*: Open (2026-09-15), awaiting review. 2. **`notion-spec-to-implementation`** ([PR #1245](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1245)) - *Functionality*: Transforms Notion-based product/tech specs into executable implementation tasks with acceptance criteria, progress tracking, and task breakdowns. - *Discussion Highlights*: Strong demand in product engineering teams; seen as a potential workflow accelerator for AI-assisted development. - *Status*: Open (2026-06-02), recently updated (Oct 2026). 3. **`md2video-audio`** ([PR #1703](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1703)) - *Functionality*: Converts Markdown documents into professional MP4 videos with natural-sounding voiceovers using Marp for slide generation. - *Discussion Highlights*: Viral appeal due to low-cost video content creation; cited as ideal for tutorials, pitches, and documentation. - *Status*: Open (2026-09-01), active discussion around audio quality and customization. 4. **`webapp-testing` improvements** ([PRs #1980, #1976, #1975](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1980), [1976](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1976), [1975](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1975)) - *Functionality*: Security-hardened web app testing pipeline with proper shell command handling (`shell=False`), accurate element detection (textarea/select), and input validation. - *Discussion Highlights*: Critical fixes for security (CWE-78) and reliability; authored by Gerard Recinto with rapid iteration. - *Status*: All open (Oct 2026), under active review. 5. **`scnet-hpc`** ([PR #1615](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/1615)) - *Functionality*: Enables SSH-based interaction with SCNet HPC clusters using profile-driven Slurm workflows for job submission, module management, and resource allocation. - *Discussion Highlights*: Niche but high-value for research and academic users; well-documented scope. - *Status*: Open (2026-08-20), minimal updates post-creation. 6. **`document-typography`** ([PR #514](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills/pull/514)) - *Functionality*: Detects and prevents typographic flaws in AI-generated docs—orphans, widows, numbering misalignment—improving document polish. - *Discussion Highlights*: Recognized as addressing a universal pain point; items.title: feat: files as a 2nd L0 source — apply the distillation engine (lenses + L0→L4) to files, not just chats

labels.name: area:distillation
labels.description: L0→L1→L2→L4 engine: mining, review, lenses, quality

labels.name: area:files
labels.description: File ingestion as an L0 source

labels.name: deferred
labels.description: Valid but intentionally waiting (no demand / gated)

items.body:
## Motivation (from @ChangeHow)

Today witness's L0 is entirely **conversation-centric**: it grows only from Claude Code hooks (`capture`) and OpenCode session reconcile (`import`). But a person's growth signal isn't only in their chat transcripts — it's also in the **documents they write and read**: design docs, notes, papers, PRDs, journals, READMEs, PDFs. @ChangeHow wants witness to **digest files of any format** (PDF, Markdown, plain text, …) as first-class source material, so the distillation pipeline (L0 → observations → facets → profile) can mine them the same way it mines sessions.

This is a substantial capability upgrade: it turns witness from "a record of your coding conversations" into "a record of your thinking across conversations AND artifacts" — much closer to the "person-centric growth archive" the README describes.

## Where it fits (architecture)

A **third L0 source**, peer to `capture` (hook-fed) and `import` (native-store reconcile):

- New command surface, e.g. `witness ingest <path>...` (files and/or directories, maybe globs), writing `store.RawRecord`s into L0 like the other two sources.
- Namespacing: files need their own session-id namespace (e.g. a `file:` prefix, analogous to `opencode:`) so they never collide with chat sessions and `ForSession` can route them. A per-file "session" (path-derived id) is the natural unit; re-ingesting a changed file is a delta, mirroring the resume/watermark model.
- The existing engine (mining pool, dedup, review, profile) should need **little or no change** — if a file is rendered into L0 records, the platform-agnostic pipeline distills it for free. The work is the *ingestion + rendering* front-end, per the policy/mechanism split (#21).

## Design questions to resolve

1. **Format parsing.** Markdown/plain text are trivial (read + chunk). PDF needs a parser — and the hard constraint is **CGO_ENABLED=0, single pure-Go static binary** (see AGENTS.md). A pure-Go PDF text extractor (e.g. `ledongthuc/pdf` or similar) is required; anything needing cgo/poppler is out. Scope the format list to what we can parse pure-Go; degrade gracefully on unsupported formats.
2. **Rendering to L0.** Files have no "turns." Do we chunk by heading/page/size (reuse the OpenCode chunker in `RenderInputs`)? What `role` do file records carry — a new `role="document"`? Does that need a lens tweak (the extract prompts assume dialogue)?
3. **Watermark / re-ingest.** Key on content hash + mtime (like the model-download marker) so re-running `ingest` on an unchanged file is a no-op, and an edited file re-mines only the delta (or re-mines whole — files aren't append-only like sessions, so "delta" may mean "replace").
4. **Which lenses apply.** The default lens assumes a coding session. Do documents want their own lens(es), or do existing lenses generalize? May pair with a lens-authoring pass.
5. **Security (important).** Ingested files are **untrusted corpus** — a malicious PDF/MD could carry prompt-injection aimed at the distillation LLM. This MUST route through the existing `platform.WrapCorpus` fencing (the same defense as session transcripts). Parsing untrusted PDFs also has its own attack surface (malformed-file DoS) — bound parser input, treat parse failures as sk-and-log, never crash `ingest`.
6. **Privacy scope.** Files are explicit, user-invoked ingestion (unlike ambient hook capture) — so no auto-watching by default. A user points witness at what they want archived.

## Not urgent / not scoped yet

Filing to capture the intent while fresh. This is a new slice, independent of the current parallel-mining / opencode-reconcile work. Natural to pick up after the in-flight PRs land. Belongs to the "person-centric archive" north star, not a quick add.

Likely the structural fix for the console-flashing family of issues. 6. **[#63200 — Run LM Studio decision models](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63200)** (rekram1-node) — Follow-up enabling LM Studio decision models, continuing the local-model integration line (#56214, #63198). 7. **[#63208 — Stop freezing desktop main process during shell env probe](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63208)** (rekram1-node) — Replaces blocking `spawnSync` of `$SHELL -il -c "env -0"` (up to 5s startup freeze) with async probing. (Closed, merged-track.) 8. **[#63222 — `opencode api` waits for plugins before sending](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63222)** (ssskay) — Fixes plugin-init race in the `api` command, matching existing `waitForPlugins` behavior in `models` and `debug agents`. 9. **[#63220 — Keep pairing QR code scannable in every theme](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63220)** (ssskay) — Draws QR black-on-white under all themes so scanners that reject inverted codes (e.g. Android) can pair. Closes #63150. 10. **[#61299 — @-mention files outside the project directory](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/61299)** (bruno303) — Ports the V1 external-file mention feature to V2 TUI, per maintainer request to reopen against V2 (#16463/#16464). *Also notable:* [#63213](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63213) (session-scoped client MCP connections), [#63139](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63139) (`remote.use` org policy to disable remote access), [#63207](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/63207) (TUI transcript verbosity defaults to `low`). --- ## Feature Request Trends 1. **Desktop organization & navigation** — Project-grouped sidebars (#55446, 👍13), keyboard-shortcut help overlay (#63190), and sidebar row parity between Recent and side tabs (#63211). The desktop shell is the most feature-hungry surface. 2. **Context/transcript editing** — Long-running calls to delete or modify messages in the thread (#7712, 👍13; #7034, 👍4), driven by dead-end contexts. Consistently high upvote counts for an unshipped capability. 3. **Extensible permissions and agent control** — Passing reasons/alternatives through deny rules (#63075), and plugin APIs to steer or rewrite conversation threads (#7034). 4. **Remote & multi-session workflows** — Session-scoped MCP connections (#63213), org-level remote-access policy (#63139), and fixing devcontainer multi-instance collisions (#50329). 5. **Platform & local-model breadth** — Android 17 local-network permission (#62934), iOS dictation language support (#56973), and expanded LM Studio integration (#63200). --- ## Developer Pain Points - **Windows desktop is the clear weak spot.** Phantom console windows on spawned processes (#52266, #62988), stale Review-pane file trees (#52941, #63214), and a background service that steals keyboard focus (every ~2s in #62988) form a cluster of visible, disruptive regressions. Notably, the platform fix (pipe mode, #63196) and the diagnostics are now converging. - **Agent control and trust remain contested.** Plan mode failing to stay in plan (#60250) and an agent acting after an explicit STOP (#63216) represent the most serious class of complaints — they erode confidence in the plan/permission model. - **Entitlement and billing friction.** Active subscriptions with 0% usage returning "insufficient funds" (#51424), ChatGPT subscription-sharing limit false positives (#62529), and repeated "no quota despite no usage" reports (#62996) suggest quota-accounting mismatches that are painful because they're opaque to users. - **Silent failure modes.** Turns settling as "succeeded" with zero content (#63171), interrupted tools losing partial results (#39565), and stale TLS/keep-alive reuse on Windows (#59786) all share a theme: failures that leave no useful trace, making debugging hard. - **Data integrity fears.** The 2.2.5→2.2.6 total session loss (#62659), even with few comments, is the kind of incident that damages trust disproportionately and warrants a prominent postmortem. - **Hardware/runtime compatibility cliffs.** The SSE4.2 requirement (#59461) locks out older CPUs entirely with a bare Error 134 — no graceful degradation path. --- *Generated from github.com/anomalyco/opencode activity for 2026-11-11. Comment and reaction counts are as of data capture; issue/PR states may have changed since.*
