items.title: [M1][ADR] Activate the benchmark-winning local embedding in Runtime

labels.name: needs-triage
labels.description: Maintainer needs to evaluate this issue

milestone.title: M1 — daily-driver single tenant
milestone.description: stometa daily-drives ContextEngine on ObsidianCentral + Feishu docs through a minimal UI with real local embeddings. DoD: 116/116 raw-note parsing; File/Obsidian + Feishu connectors via connector-runner; Qwen3-0.6B@384 local embeddings; FTS+pgvector+RRF; golden set v1 + layered judges with one calibration; 7-job minimal UI; 7 consecutive days of real use; security-gate stays PASS; everything local/loopback.

items.body:
## Parent

Child of #143 ([Epic] M1 — daily-driver single tenant).

## Why

The 2026-07-29 coverage audit found gap **G1**: #128 benchmarks local embedding
models offline, but nothing in the plan ever *activated* the winner. M1 would
therefore have shipped a measured recommendation and a Runtime still running the
old deterministic twin embedding. This issue closes that loop.

It is also the issue where an embedding swap becomes dangerous, which is why the
title carries `[ADR]`. Changing the embedding profile invalidates every stored
vector: query vectors from model B compared against document vectors from model A
return meaningless neighbors that *look* like results. Nothing in the current
code prevents that, so the rules have to be written down and accepted as an ADR
before any code lands.

## What to build

A written, accepted ADR plus the implementation that activates the
benchmark-winning local embedding model as the Runtime embedding profile:

- **Provider profile identity bound to the Release.** A Release records the
  exact model identity — id, revision/digest, dimension, normalization, pooling,
  prompt prefix — so a `ContextPackage`'s provenance resolves to the exact
  profile that produced its vectors.
- **Mixed-profile refusal.** Querying with profile B against vectors embedded
  under profile A refuses rather than returning neighbors.
- **Query-embedding cost charged to `PackageBudget`.** A resolve that embeds a
  query debits the budget; an exhausted budget refuses rather than proceeding
  unmetered.
- **Fail-closed on provider unavailability.** Provider down, timeout, or
  malformed response yields `EmbeddingProviderUnavailable` and a refused resolve.
- **Full-corpus re-embed**, verified: after activation no Fragment retains a
  vector from the previous profile.
- **Activation only through the existing explicit promote path**: a new Release
  generation promoted by the release operator (ADR-0073).
- **Measured acceptance**: retrieval metrics from #129's judges for the activated
  profile, compared explicitly against the recorded 3.8% twin baseline.

## How

Authority: ADR-0066 (Fragments are embedded before publication), ADR-0073
(explicit Release candidates and operator-authorized promotion), ADR-0067
(vector candidates discovered in the current Runtime transaction), plus the new
ADR this issue writes. Where this issue and any non-ADR document disagree, the
ADR wins.

**The ADR is written and accepted first; implementation must not land before
it.** It records the provider profile identity bound to the Release, the
query-embedding cost charged to `PackageBudget`, the 384-dimension profile
binding, the full-corpus re-embed requirement, and the fail-closed behavior on
provider unavailability. It lives under `docs/decisions/`, is linked from
`docs/decisions/README.md`, follows the house frontmatter shape, and carries a
revisit trigger — the repository's Definition of Done requires non-obvious
decisions to be recorded as ADRs, and this is the most consequential one in M1's
retrieval path.

**Mixed-profile silent mixing is the single most dangerous failure here.** Treat
its refusal as the primary invariant, not a nice-to-have guard.

**Never fall back to a second model.** On provider failure the resolve refuses.
No fallback model, no degraded lexical-only answer presented as if complete, no
missing-context fallback — a missing-context fallback is a zero under `AGENTS.md`
and no retrieval-quality win offsets it. The existing contract is
`EmbeddingProviderUnavailable` (`engine/supply/embeddings.py:28`, validated
through `validate_embedding_batch` at `:41`).

**Publication authority stays where it is.** Activation happens only by
promoting a new Release generation through the release-operator-authorized
promote path. No code path may activate a profile as a side effect of ingestion,
scan, or evaluation; ContextControl and ContextLearning never publish
(`AGENTS.md`, ADR-0073).

**Dimension is a hard boundary.** The stored schema is 384-dimensional
(`CONTEXT_FRAGMENT_EMBEDDING_DIMENSION`, `engine/supply/embeddings.py:12`;
`EmbeddingProfile` bounds dimension to 1–4096). If the benchmark winner's native
dimension is not 384, the reduction method becomes part of the recorded profile
identity. A change to the stored dimension would be a schema migration and a
**separate** decision to escalate to the maintainer — never something absorbed
silently inside this issue. As pinned today, both benchmarked models are
compared at 384, and the primary's registry entry already records the reduction
explicitly (`l2 -> truncate 1024->384 -> l2`).

**Cost is a real event on the maintainer's machine.** Surface the measured
per-document embed latency and wall-clock from #128's report before executing a
full re-embed, rather than discovering the cost mid-run.

**Honest acceptance.** If the winner does not beat the recorded 3.8% twin
baseline, that is a finding to surface, not a reason to quietly re-tune the gate.
Do not change the security gate or veto semantics to accommodate an activation.
Do not commit model weights or provider credentials.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] The activation ADR exists under `docs/decisions/`, is accepted, is linked
      from `docs/decisions/README.md`, follows the house frontmatter shape, and
      carries a revisit trigger. No implementation lands before acceptance.
- [ ] A provider profile with any unresolved identity field is not
      constructible. (`tests/unit/test_provider_profile_identity.py`)
- [ ] The Release records the exact profile, and a Package's provenance resolves
      to it; two Releases with different profiles are distinguishable.
      (`tests/integration/test_release_profile_binding.py`, real PostgreSQL 17)
- [ ] Querying under profile B against profile-A vectors **refuses**.
      (`tests/integration/test_mixed_profile_refusal.py`, real PostgreSQL 17,
      two profiles)
- [ ] A resolve that embeds a query debits `PackageBudget`; an exhausted budget
      refuses. (`tests/integration/test_query_embedding_budget.py`, real
      PostgreSQL 17)
- [ ] Provider down / timeout / malformed response yields
      `EmbeddingProviderUnavailable` and a refused resolve — no fallback model,
      no degraded-but-presented-complete answer.
      (`tests/unit/test_provider_unavailable_fail_closed.py`, fake failing
      provider)
- [ ] After activation, a residual-vector query returns zero rows: no Fragment
      retains a prior-profile vector.
      (`tests/integration/test_full_reembed.py`, real PostgreSQL 17)
- [ ] No ingestion, scan, or evaluation path activates a profile; only the
      explicit release-operator promote path does.
      (`tests/integration/test_activation_requires_promote.py`, real
      PostgreSQL 17)
- [ ] The activated profile's pilot metrics are recorded with profile identity
      attached, and the report states the delta against the recorded 3.8% twin
      baseline explicitly.
      (`tests/integration/test_pilot_metrics_recorded.py`, real PostgreSQL 17 plus
      #129's judges)
- [ ] Verification: `make lint`, `make typecheck`, `make test`,
      `make db-up && make integration`, `make security-gate` all green, with
      fresh output recorded in the PR.

Suggested order: the two pure tests first, then the real-PostgreSQL ones
(`make db-up` first). Use a fake deterministic provider in tests — real model
downloads must never become a test dependency.

## Status

Not started; the ADR does not exist yet. Highest accepted ADR number in
`docs/decisions/` today is 0080, so this ADR takes the next free number.

What already exists to build on: the `EmbeddingProvider` Protocol,
`EmbeddingProfile`, `EmbeddingProviderUnavailable`, and
`validate_embedding_batch` (`engine/supply/embeddings.py:12,18,28,32,41`);
ADR-0066's embed-before-publication rule, already implemented (commit
`546e63c`); the pgvector candidate index (`adapters/pgvector.py:29`, commit
`2be5274`); and the explicit `promote-release` command under the separate release
identity from ADR-0073 (commit `45f0a3f`, see `STATUS.md`). The Runtime currently
runs a deterministic twin query embedding under the ADR-0068 loopback dogfood
composition — that twin is what this issue replaces.

What is not yet decided: the winner itself. #128's tracked frozen result
(`docs/evaluation/2026-07-29-embedding-benchmark.json`) records
`"result": "pending_corpus"`, so no model has actually won anything yet. The
pinned candidates in `eval/embedding-benchmark/model-registry.json` are
`Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B` @384 (primary) and `intfloat/multilingual-e5-small`
@384 (baseline), both local `sentence-transformers` snapshots, consistent with
the maintainer's local-first decision.

## Blocked by

- #128 — this issue activates "the benchmark-winning" model, and the benchmark
  has not produced a winner: its frozen result still reads `pending_corpus`.
  Writing the activation ADR's non-model clauses (Release binding, budget
  metering, fail-closed, promote-only activation) can begin in parallel, but the
  ADR cannot be accepted while the model it activates is unknown.
- #129 — supplies the locked pilot and the retrieval judges that produce the
  acceptance metrics. It merged in `3f16fde`, but its own corpus delivery and
  threshold preregistration remain pending, so the measured-acceptance criterion
  above is not yet reachable.

Deliberately **not** blocked by #139 (keystone seam 3, governed
model-inference port, M2). Seam 3 covers typed rewrite/rerank/select operations;
#139's own body states it *complements* the existing `EmbeddingProvider` seam at
`engine/supply/embeddings.py` rather than replacing it. Embedding activation
therefore rides the existing seam, and holding M1 behind an M2 seam would be a
sequencing error.

# Brain daily reports — integrated communication channel

This issue is the **durable** daily-report channel for brain's audit loop. Every daily run appends its report here as a comment, so the owner (and any agent in a later session) can read it from a phone and reply in-thread.

## Channels this report is posted to (all four participants)

| channel | transport | who reads it | durability |
|---|---|---|---|
| this GitHub issue | GitHub comments | owner, all agents, any session | durable (survives sandbox resets) |
| SwarmChat `#reports` | live chat server | watcher, shadow, forge, openhands, cloud, owner | live only (local server) |
| SwarmChat `#audits` | live chat server | same | live only |
| Claude inbox | edge-config store | the owner's other agent | durable |

**Participants:** owner · ChatGPT/Forge · OpenHands · Cloud.

## What each report contains

1. brain self-audit result (purpose/depth audit, the nine-role company, Forge).
2. Each repo audited today, measured against its production plan (`docs/audits/plans/<repo>.md`): goal, progress, the ordered "what to fix" list with evidence, and the next item.
3. The repo-queue cursor and the next repo in rotation.
4. One yes/no question for the owner if a decision is needed.

_Channel established 2026-11-07 by the OpenHands agent on behalf of the owner._

items.title: Decision: where cloud state lives — Cloudflare only (A) or Convex for catalog/app state (B); Convex-for-everything ruled out

labels.name: decision
labels.description: A choice the founders need to make

items.body:
## Question
Where does each part of Signalbox's cloud state live, and on which platform? Per #840, every part sits behind a module interface, so this is a choice of adapter, not a rewrite. T3 Code's thread model stays as it is.

## Options
- **A. Cloudflare only.** Thread DOs (items plus live stream), a catalog in D1 or Postgres with our own sync for the sidebar, R2, and an external search engine.
- **B. Convex for catalog and app state** (folders, roles, thread list and status, presence, notifications, usage ledger, automation records), **plus Cloudflare for thread items and the live stream**, R2 and external search.
- **C. Convex for everything**, including thread items and live deltas. Cloudflare only for runners, ModelGateway, Dynamic Workflows and R2.

In every option, runners, ModelGateway with the CLIProxyAPI pools, Dynamic Workflows (sandboxed user automation code) and R2 or S3 stay on Cloudflare. Convex's AI Gateway can't front CLIProxyAPI, and its VM components (including Boat's) can't replace MachineBackend.

## Cost premium over A ($/user/month, month 12, measured usage)
"Heavy" is one real dogfood user's measured T3 Code and Codex history. "Typical" is 1/5 of that. Every formula and price is in the design notes (cost-premium.md).

| | Heavy, 100 users | Heavy, 5,000 users | Typical, 100 | Typical, 5,000 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| **B over A** | +$0.78 | +$0.64 | +$0.40 | +$0.27 |
| **C over A** | +$12.87 (Pro) | +$4.80 (Business, dedicated) | +$3.76 | +$1.75 |
| C with Convex's built-in search | +$36 | about +$1,100 | +$46 | about +$5 |

- C's premium is mostly live streaming. One-second updates are billed as Convex calls for every watching device; on DOs the same traffic costs about $0.01. Keeping the stream on a DO cuts C to about +$2.50–3.10.
- Convex's built-in search bills every query for the whole shared index, so it's ruled out as the history index.
- Most uncertain inputs: the live delta rate, how many devices watch a stream, whether DOs really sleep between messages, and Convex's billing for built-in indexes.

## Other findings that shape this
- Per-thread DOs aren't the flaw; using them as the only database is. Every actor-per-entity system pairs its actors with a central index (Temporal, Restate, Rivet, tldraw, Cloudflare's Agents SDK). Missing today: a catalog, a search index fed from threads, a thread-to-thread inbox (Warp's protocol shape), and a fix for the resume bug behind "Syncing messages…" (#779).
- Convex-style layers on Cloudflare: Lunora is closest to the right design (per-DO writer, index-range invalidation, per-tenant sharding), but it's one maintainer, about 509k lines, not Effect. Concave speaks Convex's protocol on DOs but is unmaintained compiled code with a single writer. Concile isn't really Convex-compatible. Building our own is estimated at 10–15k lines and 3–6 months to production.
- Lock-in exits: self-hosted Convex (Postgres) for B and C; celld (Apache-2.0) runs Workers and DOs on our own machines for A and B.
- Search, in every option: one logical index partitioned by content home and assembled per query from the searcher's current access. It covers excerpts, not full tool output, keyword first. The engine is turbopuffer or our own SQLite FTS, pending a spike.

## Recommendation
**C is out**: +$5–13 per heavy user, which is significant by Yannic's yardstick. **A vs B is the real choice**: B costs about $0.30–0.80/user more and buys Convex's DX and live sync for the catalog and app layer, which is where cross-thread features live. A is cheapest and has no second vendor, but we build catalog sync ourselves (Lunora-style).

Lean: **B**, behind the #840 catalog module interface, so it can later move to self-hosted Convex or our own DO layer without touching features. Thread items and the stream stay in DOs. Fix the resume protocol (#779) and add the thread inbox and search index now, since those are needed in A or B.

## Decision needed (Yannic)
- [ ] A or B?
- [ ] Thread search before this lands: a throwaway on today's stack now, or wait?

## Sources
The research records on this issue, on #847 (Convex on Cloudflare), on #791 (one index) and on #788 (history measurement).

items.title: Reconsider iron-proxy as Haku Console's egress adapter
items.body:
## Direction update — 2026-10-03

The selected direction is to migrate remaining Iron consumers to **Agentplane egress**, not to adopt Iron as Haku Console's new egress adapter. #5140 is the refreshed consumer inventory/retirement tracker. Public-coder OpenClaw preparation/cutover (#8849, #8850) are merged, with live acceptance still tracked in #8857; the KubeVirt devbox deliberately remains on Iron pending #8856.

Treat the Iron/embedded-mitmproxy comparisons below as **historical investigation**, not an implementation mandate. Carry forward applicable identity, credential-redemption, revocation, no-bypass, protocol and fail-closed requirements into the Agentplane design. Do not start new Iron adapter integration based on the old proposal. Remaining Haku consumers need inventory and explicit disposition under #5140; this direction update is not a claim they are already migrated or permission to delete their dependencies.

Keeping this issue open as historical/design context while the remaining requirements are reconciled; link any residual actionable requirement from #5140 before closing it as superseded.

---

## Why reconsider this now

#4670 selected an embedded mitmproxy adapter and #5140 tracks retiring the remaining iron-proxy fences. Both decisions rely on the statement that iron-proxy has no per-request hook and therefore cannot ask Console for a decision.

That premise is stale. The exact iron-proxy revision currently built by this repository (`c90f4fe`) already contains an external gRPC `TransformService`. A configured transform receives each matching CONNECT/request/response and may reject it or return a modified request/response; transform errors fail the request with `502`. Current upstream also has a configurable polling control-plane client that hot-swaps allowlists, secrets, transforms, MCP policy, and Postgres routes.

Reconsider whether iron-proxy can replace `haku/egress`'s embedded mitmproxy adapter while keeping Haku Console authoritative. This issue is an investigation and architecture decision, not a presumption that switching is correct.

Upstream seams:

- per-request gRPC transform: <https://github.com/ironsh/iron-proxy/blob/c90f4fe31607552ed05675fc7ad239d94b431af2/proto/transform/v1/transform.proto>
- transform implementation: <https://github.com/ironsh/iron-proxy/blob/c90f4fe31607552ed05675fc7ad239d94b431af2/internal/transform/grpc/grpc.go>
- managed control-plane client: <https://github.com/ironsh/iron-proxy/blob/7f947f2f8413c933851e7353471e07dffe24baa9/internal/controlplane/client.go>

## Invariants that must survive

- Every admission is bound to a live authenticated Haku session/Agent. Network position, client IP, one shared proxy credential, or request JSON is not identity.
- Console timeout/unavailability fails closed. A previously synced configuration must not continue granting ended sessions, revoked grants, or retired credentials indefinitely.
- Removing proxy environment variables gives the sandbox no bypass around the proxy.
- Reachability and credential redemption remain separate authorities.
- Credential redemption remains Agent/session-, destination-, and request-scoped.
- Real credentials, session tokens, placeholders, cookies, and configured secret fields do not enter logs, metrics, traces, generated configuration, or tunnel annotations.
- Prefer placeholders remaining inert and safe to disclose. If a topology makes a placeholder a cross-tenant bearer capability, call that out rather than continuing to describe it as non-secret.
- Preserve complete DNS-answer validation, prohibited/mixed-address rejection, and dialing only a validated address. A per-grant internal-origin exception must not turn into a proxy-wide private-address waiver.
- HTTP/2/gRPC, Git-over-HTTPS Basic substitution, response streaming, bounded request-body behavior, WebSockets/SSE, and large transfers keep working.
- Grant expiry/release/revocation bounds every later request, CONNECT, and reconnect. Any degraded-operation lease is explicit and short.
- Cilium remains a static ceiling and the proxy cannot dynamically widen it.

## Topologies to compare

### One shared iron-proxy

Operationally smallest and preserves the warm-pool benefit of one uniform fence destination. It also concentrates every reachable destination and real credential in one process.

Polling alone does not supply per-request identity. Iron-proxy's managed `principal_id` identifies the proxy assignment, not the HTTP client; its secrets transform selects by destination and placeholder, not Agent/session. A shared proxy driven only by synced configuration would therefore need roughly one mapping per `(Agent or session, credential presentation)`. Those placeholders become bearer capabilities inside the shared proxy: any connected Agent that learns another's placeholder can spend it.

Evaluate a hybrid instead:

- polling supplies the coarse allowlist ceiling and transform wiring;
- `Proxy-Authorization` carries `HAKU_SESSION_TOKEN` on CONNECT;
- the gRPC transform asks Console synchronously for identity, grant, and redemption decisions;
- CONNECT returns only an audit-safe opaque correlation handle, never the session token, in tunnel annotations; inner decrypted requests present that handle back to the Console adapter;
- credential bytes travel only over a protected colocated or mTLS transform channel and are applied to that request.

Open gaps in the current transform protocol:

- it exposes CONNECT headers and propagates transform annotations to inner requests, but has no first-class authenticated-client/session field or connection ID;
- it does not expose the complete DNS answer or selected upstream address, so Console cannot directly enforce its current resolve-and-pin contract;
- iron-proxy's upstream deny guard is proxy-wide and cannot express Haku's exact-origin, per-grant `allow_prohibited_address` exception;
- establish whether a safe opaque tunnel-handle adapter is sufficient or whether small upstream protocol changes are required.

### One iron-proxy per Agent

The proxy's managed principal and configuration can correspond to one Agent. Placeholders may remain inert relative to other Agents if NetworkPolicy ensures only that Agent's sessions can reach its listener. Attribution and revocation are simpler than in a shared proxy, while multiple simultaneous sessions of one Agent still share a fence and credential set.

Costs/questions:

- number of long-lived proxy pods and CAs/listeners;
- warm-pool claim routing and whether a pod can be pre-fenced without security-critical relabeling;
- aggregate resource cost and rollout fan-out;
- per-Agent versus central audit collection and querying;
- whether session-scoped grants still require the synchronous gRPC decision path.

### One iron-proxy per sandbox/session

Provides the cleanest attribution and smallest credential blast radius. The synced proxy principal can be the session, and placeholders need not separate mutually untrusted callers because only one sandbox reaches the listener.

Costs/questions:

- one additional container or pod per active sandbox, startup latency, memory, certificate/listener lifecycle, and image rollout fan-out;
- never use a sidecar in the Agent pod as the sole network boundary: containers share a network namespace, so policy cannot distinguish proxy egress from Agent egress. If colocated, identify an independent enforcement mechanism; otherwise use a separately selected pod/service;
- warm-pool provisioning and cleanup;
- central audit ingestion and correlation despite distributed proxy instances;
- whether the reduced adapter complexity outweighs the fleet-management cost.

Also evaluate a deliberately small set of shared proxies partitioned by access profile or trust class if it materially improves the trade-off without recreating ambiguous identity.

## Console outage and revocation semantics

Current managed mode behaves asymmetrically:

- before the first successful sync, iron-proxy is not ready and fails closed with `503`;
- after one successful sync, polling failures keep the last applied pipeline active indefinitely;
- control-plane-delivered secret values are static in memory and carry no lease or expiry;
- an invalid update preserves the old pipeline;
- an explicit revoked response terminates the proxy, but an unavailable Console cannot deliver it.

Polling-only operation therefore does not meet Haku's revocation or outage invariant. Compare and choose explicitly:

1. synchronous per-request Console decisions: Console down means `502` and no admission;
2. a leased sync contract: every configuration carries `valid_until`, readiness expires without renewal, and iron-proxy needs an upstream or local patch;
3. a bounded degraded lease: last-known policy remains usable for a deliberately small interval, with its exact maximum revocation delay accepted and tested.

Do not accept `synced_once` as permanent authorization readiness.

## Investigation work

- [ ] Build a minimal Haku-compatible gRPC `TransformService` and route an iron-proxy CONNECT plus decrypted inner request through it.
- [ ] Prove Agent/session authentication without putting the session token in iron-proxy audit traces or tunnel annotations.
- [ ] Prove timeout, adapter crash, malformed response, and Console outage all deny without upstream contact.
- [ ] Determine the smallest upstream additions needed for complete DNS-answer validation/address pinning and per-request internal-origin exceptions, or document why iron-proxy's native guard safely replaces those Console-owned decisions.
- [ ] Exercise Haku's existing Git Basic substitution, HTTP/2 BuildBuddy traffic, large upload/download, streaming, WebSocket/SSE, and request-body substitution cases through the candidate adapter.
- [ ] Measure shared, per-Agent, and per-sandbox resource cost, startup time, rollout behavior, warm-pool compatibility, and audit ergonomics.
- [ ] Threat-model placeholder guessing, disclosure, replay, cross-Agent use, rotation, and revocation for each topology.
- [ ] Decide whether polling is useful for coarse configuration, whether it needs a lease, and whether real credential values should ever be delivered in its payload.
- [ ] Compare implementation and maintenance cost against the current `haku/egress` adapter, including which custom code and tests would be deleted versus retained.
- [ ] Update #4670's decision record and #5140's retirement premise after the result; do not retire the existing iron-proxy path solely on the stale no-hook claim.

## Decision output

Produce one recommendation among:

- keep embedded mitmproxy;
- shared iron-proxy plus synchronous Console transform;
- per-Agent iron-proxy;
- per-sandbox/session iron-proxy;
- a justified partitioned hybrid.

The recommendation must state the authority owner during Console outage, maximum revocation delay, placeholder secrecy model, credential/process blast radius, DNS enforcement owner, warm-pool implications, audit topology, and measured resource/latency cost.

items.title: Release Radar A1 — truthful forecast diagnostics and selected-model consistency
items.body:
## Chairman-directed Release Radar upgrade: first bounded capability

Operation: `release-radar-a1-diagnostic-truth-20260905-sol-001`
Parent organizational workstream: `WS:RATES-INFLATION-COMMAND` (existing; no new workstream).
State at creation: **SPEC_ONLY / WAITING_CAPACITY / needs_placement / no implementation START**.
Preferred avenue: **CTO Sol** on an eligible Codex engineering surface. Why: bounded but cross-layer statistical-semantics and Python/Jinja/executed-JavaScript work. Why not Fable: the architectural boundary and proof contract below are frozen; no unresolved principal-level cross-repository build is delegated.

Current live Chairman intent explicitly directs CEO Sol to assess Release Radar robustness, improve forecast accuracy, initiate the build, and continue without asking for another authorization. This issue records the bounded source/product contract; it does not itself create an Executive Job, assign a discovered reader, authorize merge/deploy, or prove execution.

Protected procedure: `mastermindx-market-intelligence/Mastermind@0d9cf2f58f9a6a1fe895d5d199abc18735201e24`, Skillpack `mastermind.sol_skillpack.v1` 1.0.1, bootstrap-major 1. Macro investigation pin: `f69302500c0067e5c7f087a79cbaafe523720fd1`.

## Observable mission / why

A researcher opening the real CPI or PPI Release Radar card can tell which forecast is selected, what the diagnostics actually measure, what is unavailable, and whether performance is established—without mistaking missing attribution for 0% residual, a heuristic for probability of accuracy, or champion attribution for an explanation of a blended forecast. The same interpretation must be carried by the existing machine artifact, not only hand-written UI copy.

This is a product-truth vertical, not a model-retuning PR. It is the first step toward trustworthy target/horizon modeling and empirical calibration, not a claim that renaming labels improves forecast accuracy.

## Verified findings

At the investigation pin, `data/release_forecast/latest.json` blob `01bc339e00f8ca4bff574593bb1571e0cdb8f9f0`:

* PPI has five populated features, `components=null`, `confidence_v2=null`, `confidence_components_v2=null`, coverage flags 1.0 / 0.8 / 0.2 and maturity 0. Its screenshot nevertheless presents 80/20/0 as confidence composition. Backend-null versus rendered-zero is established; the exact current frontend fallback line must still be inspected locally. Do not use the research mockup as proof of deployed JavaScript.
* CPI champion persistence attribution is about 46.47% of absolute standardized-feature contributions; it is NOT absent-data share. The four audited contributions are energy +0.091486, shelter -0.001378, persistence +0.081062, pipeline -0.000527. These exclude the fitted intercept and do not explain the separate blended point.
* Legacy `confidence` is an interval-width-rank/input-completeness diagnostic, not a calibrated probability of being right. CPI `confidence_v2` is a different attribution heuristic.
* The artifact explicitly withholds accuracy claims, marks the legacy cross-vintage target experimental, and reports no clean forward CPI champion evidence. A clean shadow lane and a champion lane must not lend each other sample counts.
* `coherent_ridge_v1` has a frozen exact T-1 contract. Absence before that horizon is not by itself a pipeline failure. Display only a source-backed reason; otherwise reason is unknown.
* The PPI payload has a Sept-4 input snapshot for a Sept-10 release but carries legacy `cutoff_label=T-1`. A static label or file build time is not a verified information cutoff.

Sources: `engine/release_components_cpi.py`, `engine/release_provenance.py`, `engine/release_targets_v11.py`, `engine/release_combined.py`, `scripts/build_release_forecast.py`, `research/release_forecast/PREREG_COHERENT_RIDGE_V1.md`, and the current published artifact, all re-read at immutable pins before implementation.

## Precedence / no-rebuild / collisions

Current protected Skillpack and universal routing/dialogue laws -> current `research/DO_NOT_REBUILD.md` and `DEC:RIC-CANONICAL-COMPOSITION-BOUNDARIES` -> accepted RIC recovery freeze -> this bounded Chairman-directed product ruling -> older MRI descriptions where not superseded. This ruling changes display interpretation only; no frozen model or score contract is amended here.

Existing F1 `ric-f1-release-event-20260828-sol-001`, MAS-204, Slack `C0BSBM78V1N/1787975946.019219` remains separate. The complete thread was re-read: its latest visible edge remains Aug-29 CONTINUE/watch, with no later START. This does NOT establish the old local worktree is currently effect-free. Preserve its original native task/worktree and reconcile through its owner; do not claim or replace it from this issue.

Known shared-file collision: open Draft/HOLD PR #6685 touches `templates/dashboard.html.j2` and `site/macro.html` for the Grey Deer hero/dialog, not Release Radar by its stated scope. Inspect actual hunks and obtain a disjoint-section/owner compatibility receipt before editing those shared files. Do not merge, rebase, or repair #6685 here.

PR #6593 already owns correction of `agentos/workstreams/WS-RATES-INFLATION-COMMAND.md`; leave that path untouched. Do not duplicate F0 status repair. Query all current open PR changed paths and current native source owners again before START; search-title absence is not a collision proof.

## Frozen A1 scope

Macro only:

1. Add a small pure presentation/diagnostic adapter within the existing release-forecast family (prefer `engine/release_diagnostics.py`, not a new store/service).
2. Wire its additive read-only diagnostic projection in `scripts/build_release_forecast.py`, only after the existing F1 shared-producer ownership boundary is reconciled.
3. Update only the existing Release Radar sections of `templates/dashboard.html.j2` and its actual existing includes/consumer; use the canonical site build for generated output. No broad dashboard redesign or manual splicing of `site/macro.html`.
4. Behavioral Python producer tests and executed JavaScript/render tests in the existing Release Radar suites; a dedicated `tests/test_release_diagnostics.py` is permitted.
5. A source-backed research ruling and one additive Agent OS continuation/discovery record for this upgrade, validated against the existing schemas. Do not edit #6593's workstream path.

No model function, weight, feature selection, target transformation, forecast point, quantitative interval calculation, benchmark, score eligibility, ledger row, official actual, source receipt, training data, registry promotion, schedule owner, trading/rank/size/gate authority, or ingestion cadence may change in A1.

## Required user and machine behavior

* Separate feature availability, provenance/vintage quality, verified freshness, economic basket/prior coverage, model attribution, and empirical performance. No one synthetic confidence bar may mix denominators.
* Null or absent attribution remains unavailable, never zero. PPI must not synthesize the CPI decomposition from feature coverage. All-zero attribution contributions have an undefined denominator, not a measured 0/0/0 composition.
* Label CPI's existing decomposition as standardized model attribution excluding the baseline/intercept; label persistence explicitly. Show it only for its own forecast identity. Do not infer an exact intercept from rounded visible values. If baseline is unavailable, state that explicitly.
* The primary point, interval, labels, comparisons, and diagnostic metadata must bind to the same selected forecast. Preserve the current primary-selection policy. Selecting a blend may show its actual recorded input weights and points; champion economic attribution is separate, clearly labeled, or unavailable for the blend. No synthetic ensemble economic waterfall.
* Replace unqualified `Confidence: N%` with accurate diagnostic naming or a truthful `Calibration not established` state. Never show heuristic confidence as probability of accuracy. Preserve raw legacy fields for compatibility; machine consumers receive explicit semantics and evidence scope.
* `p10-p90` is nominal 80%; `p25-p75` is nominal 50%. Do not create p05/p95 or call the present band 90%. Legacy heuristic intervals can only be labeled experimental/uncalibrated, not empirically validated. Missing/nonfinite/reversed bands are unavailable in presentation, without rewriting their historical records.
* Monthly CPI/PPI change is `% month-on-month, seasonally adjusted`; contribution and difference units are percentage points. Do not use pp as the label for the level of a monthly percent-change forecast.
* Use source-backed information cutoff and release identity. If only a date is known, say date precision; do not invent 08:30, midnight, timezone, or T-1. Build timestamp, observation period, public availability, and last ingestion are distinct. Unknown/stale/partial never becomes fresh from file generation.
* `coherent_ridge_v1` may display `not scheduled at this horizon` only when its actual eligibility diagnostic proves that; generic zero count alone must not be interpreted as a reason.
* Performance comes from the current eligible, correction-resolved, exact model/target/horizon lane with sample count. Missing lane match is `unavailable`, not n=0 fabricated from another lane. Benchmark-only claims remains benchmark-only. Street consensus remains unavailable unless a real existing licensed source proves otherwise.
* Nulls, NaN/infinities, booleans in numeric fields, malformed percentages, absent manifests, and mismatched model identities degrade explicitly; rendering must not crash or invent values. Add diagnostics without mutating the input payload.

## Ordered execution and proof

1. Eligible placed receiver ACKs the exact eventual child root with actual native and GitHub identities; reads this issue, full root, current same-SHA Skillpack and source. No self-assignment by finding the issue.
2. Reconcile F1 shared-producer and #6685 shared-template ownership; record exact current pins and hunks. Missing exact-source access is a typed blocker, not permission to approximate.
3. Write discriminating RED tests using the audited PPI/CPI fixture shapes, blend/champion switches, null attribution, all-zero contributions, bad numerics, unknown cutoff, unavailable calibration and all benchmark-only states.
4. Implement the pure adapter, producer projection and real renderer integration together. Preserve every existing numeric model/benchmark/ledger field; verify deep equality before/after after removing only the additive diagnostic subtree.
5. Run producer integration and executed-JavaScript tests, existing authority/defect/epoch and template-site-sync fences, and the full relevant suite. Assert no read-back of presentation diagnostics into numerical forecasts/scoring.
6. Generate the site via the real builder; prove dark/light, EN/ZH at 1440, 768 and 390 widths. Test screenshot-like CPI/PPI payloads and all failure states; capture the actual current production payload as distinct evidence. Local screenshots are not production deployment proof.
7. Maintain one branch and Draft/HOLD PR, verified source-continuity checkpoint before long CI/review exposure, exact-head CI/security, and independent non-author review.
8. Return immutable head/tree/paths, tests, browser and real-input receipts, numeric-invariance results, unresolved gates, and an additive durable handoff. Do not mark Ready, merge, deploy or continue into A2. Sol separately adjudicates release; final acceptance requires real production page and machine-consumer proof.

## Continuation / terminal law

Until placement: `WAITING_CAPACITY / needs_placement`; no receiver-specific watcher or invented runtime Job. Once assigned, use one accepted exact-carrier continuation path on each side, and report WATCH_UNAVAILABLE after concrete surface checks rather than claim one exists. PICKUP_ACK, START, RESULT, merge and production remain distinct. After each nonterminal return re-enter the same exact-carrier wait path. Sol owes explicit CONTINUE/REQUEST_REPAIR or terminal STOP. Terminal child-source removal must preserve any independently valid aggregate seat watcher.

## Following roadmap — not part of A1

A2: separately preregister/admit the already locally tested missing-error-scale interval amendment, with distribution-version/score-cohort isolation and all nullable consumers; no silent amendment to combined_v1 history.
B: coherent first-print/proxy targets and explicit T-14/T-7/T-1 model contracts, extending existing owners.
C: economically faithful CPI component challenger (correct vintage weights, actual services-ex-shelter scope, publication-safe energy, stock-rent versus asking-rent distinction).
D: PPI goods/services/trade-margin/construction challenger; no 100% economic-coverage claim from five available regressors.
E: matched-cohort MAE/RMSE/bias, nominal 50/80% coverage plus width/proper interval score, preregistered promotion, and live release-to-product learning/reliability proof.

No new collector, forecast truth store, score ledger, runtime lifecycle, queue, calendar or publication plane. More attractive diagnostics do not prove greater accuracy.

# AI Infrastructure Digest 2026-11-02 > Generated: 2026-11-02 00:34 UTC | Projects covered: 6 - [vLLM](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm) - [SGLang](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang) - [llama.cpp](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) - [Ollama](https://github​.com/ollama/ollama) - [LiteLLM](https://github​.com/BerriAI/litellm) - [Unsloth](https://github​.com/unslothai/unsloth) --- ## Cross-Project Comparison # Cross-Project Comparison Report — AI Infrastructure Digest **Date: 2026-11-02 | Coverage: vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, Ollama, LiteLLM, Unsloth** --- ## 1. Ecosystem Overview The AI infrastructure stack is in a hardening phase rather than a feature-expansion phase: no project in this sample shipped a release in the last 24 hours, yet every tracker shows heavy issue/PR churn concentrated on **correctness, memory accounting, and stability under concurrency**. The day's most consistent cross-project theme is a **DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 quality and stability gap** — vLLM, SGLang, and llama.cpp each carry open bugs on DSV4-family correctness, scheduling, or backend crashes, indicating reference-implementation maturities have not yet caught up to model releases. Simultaneously, a **Rust-ification of control planes** is visible across layers (vLLM's Rust frontend, LiteLLM's Rust router core and forwarding server), targeting hot-path overhead rather than model math. Hardware coverage continues to broaden (SM100/SM120, ROCm gfx950, NPU, Hexagon, OpenCL/Adreno), but **SM120 specifically emerges as a production risk** across vLLM and SGLang. Finally, the training/fine-tuning layer (Unsloth) is extending parallelism and quantization reach (FP8 LoRA, unified DP/TP/PP/CP mesh), signaling that the same workloads serviced by inference engines are growing in scale upstream. --- ## 2. Activity Comparison *Note: exact counts are not published in the digests; the table reflects qualitative activity and explicit figures where cited.* | Project | Layer | Active Issue Themes | Active PR Themes | Release Status (24h) | Key Numerical Signals | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **vLLM** | Serving engine (server/cloud) | ~8 ranked stability items; 3 engine-crash bugs | Rust frontend parity; NVFP4/GPTQ batch-invariance; RL weight-reload RFC | **None** | RFC #54477 validated across **17 model families**; ~**18% pooling regression** on torch 2.11; Rust roadmap #44280 at **50 comments** | | **SGLang** | Serving engine (server/cloud) | DSV4.1 crash + allocator OOM; SM120 GLM-5.3 issues | SM100 NVFP4 kernels; AMD MI350X MiniMax; XPU paged-experts | **None** | Allocator OOM at only **29% KV pool**; SM120 prefill **2–7K vs 12.5K tok/s** vs vLLM/marlin; CUDA coredump tracker at **352 comments** | | **llama.cpp** | Local/edge runtime | SYCL multi-GPU cluster; CUDA sm_75 regression; Vulkan DSV4 gibberish | Unified-KV FA; per-size CUDA graph arenas; MoE ClassLRU cache | **6 releases (b12027–b12032)** | MoE ClassLRU: **+6% QFN / +7% GLM decode, −8% uploads**; SYCL `--cpu-moe` **100–1000× slowdown**; HIP MTP prefill **−80%** | | **Ollama** | Local runtime + API surface | Parser correctness (tool calls, harmony); long-context degradation | Per-model prompt cache budgets; scheduler eviction; CORS hardening | **None** | Repeat-limit abort at **101 identical tokens**; MLX cache fixed at **8 GiB**; embed context off by **1–2 tokens** | | **LiteLLM** | LLM gateway / proxy | Cost/budget enforcement bugs; cross-tenant cache leak | Large Rust router core migration (~10 stacked PRs); Rust forwarding server | **None** | Cost overbilling **1,000,000×**; ~**10+ Rust PRs** in flight; GHCR tag/release provenance gap | | **Unsloth** | Fine-tuning / training | Studio UX and platform fixes (mostly closed) | FP8 LoRA; `UNSLOTH_PARALLEL` unified mesh; hub snapshot pinning | **None** | fp16 overflow example: `B=5000 × alpha 16 = 80000 > 65504`; Gemini picker capped at **20 models** pre-fix | **Reading:** llama.cpp is the only project shipping releases, consistent with its continuous-build model. The server-grade engines (vLLM, SGLang) and control-plane layers (LiteLLM) are in deep refactor cycles, where regressions are expected and pinning discipline matters. Ollama and Unsloth are in bug-sweep mode. --- ## 3. Model Support Race **New model/architecture landings in this window:** | Model / Arch | vLLM | SGLang | llama.cpp | Ollama | Unsloth | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **DeepSeek-V4 / V4.1** | Batch-invariant sparse indexer (#64441); multi-image packing (#65030); HC expansion (#64816); MXFP8 indexer autotune (#60543) | **Bug-heavy**: scheduler crash (#47218), allocator OOM (#43486), prompt-render divergence (#46348), SM120 index-order instability (#46798) | Vulkan `-fa on` gibberish (#31480, fix PR #31505) | — | — | | **Qwen3.5 / Qwen3-Next** | Fused QK-norm+RoPE ROCm enablement (#51406) | Qwen3.5 seq-classification request (#41110); GDN prefill + Triton recurrence (#38806) | — | 0.8B `q4_K_M` request (#19436) | — | | **GLM-5.x** | Stale top-k fix (closed #63170) | **SM120 fa4 CUDA-graph crash** (#42012) — triton only | — | — | — | | **MiniMax-M3.1** | NVFP4 KV sparse-prefill workspace (#64856) | **Landing**: MI350X/MI355X gfx950 support (#46693, kernel stack merged) | — | — | — | | **Mistral / Tekken** | `developer`→`system` role fix (#65031); byte-fallback tokenization fix (#64743) | — | — | — | — | | **Kimi K3** | — | NPU MLAProlog (#47373) | — | — | — | | **LFM3** | — | — | Tensor-split enabled (#31431) | — | — | | **Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe** | — | — | mtmd SALM support in review (#31471) | — | — | | **Gemma 4** | — | — | Graph optimizations in review (#31356); test-arch enablement | — | — | | **Qwen3.8-27B (hybrid attn/MTP)** | — | — | — | **Support gap**: GGUF load failure (#19459) | — | | **Maple-Preview (TQ1_0/TQ2_0)** | — | — | CUDA kernels in review (#31512) | — | — | **Who's ahead:** - **vLLM leads on DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 depth** — it is shipping *optimizations* for the architecture (sparse indexer, vision packing, MXFP8 autotune) while SGLang is still firefighting *correctness and memory* on the same model family. - **SGLang leads on accelerator breadth** — the only project landing MiniMax-M3.1 on AMD MI350X/MI355X and Kimi K3 on NPU in this window, plus an XPU paged-experts RFC. Its multi-vendor reach is a differentiator, at the cost of a wider bug surface. - **llama.cpp leads on edge/mobile format breadth** — Hexagon stride fix, OpenCL IQ3_S with Adreno kernels, ternary CUDA, LFM3 tensor split. This is the only project pushing into sub-server form factors. - **Ollama lags on new-arch ingestion** — Qwen3.8-27B hybrid-attention GGUFs still fail to load; harmony analysis-channel thinking support is the notable forward step. --- ## 4. Performance Frontier **Where optimization effort concentrates today:** **Kernels (highest absolute effort)** - SGLang: SM100 NVFP4 DualGEMM+SwiGLU, PDL-safe GEMM, grouped GEMM, fused MoE (#47589); single SM100-tuned RMSNorm JIT template (#47503); Qwen3 prefill QK-norm+RoPE fusion (#47785). - vLLM: ROCm FlyDSL decode monokernel (#63440); fused DSpark draft sampling on gfx950 (#63181); FlashInfer autotune expansion (#60543). - llama.cpp: OpenCL IQ3 Adreno GEMM/GEMV; unified-KV FA `flash_attn_ext_rows` (#29510) spanning CUDA/Vulkan/SYCL/Metal/OpenCL/Hexagon/WebGPU. **KV / cache management** - llama.cpp: unified-KV flash attention (mask-filtering elimination) and **MoE ClassLRU expert cache** (+6–7% decode, −8% uploads) — the most quantified cache win in the window. - Ollama: per-model prompt cache budgets (#19450) superseding a single global budget; scheduler eviction rework (#19449). - SGLang: NPU sparse-KV offload with PD disaggregation + LRU caching (#43579); supernode-wide L1/L2 agentic cache roadmap (#43098). **Quantization** - FP4/FP8 dominance: NVFP4 across vLLM (KV, sparse indexer) and SGLang (dual-gemm, SM100, TP4 bundle). - Ternary/1-bit: llama.cpp OpenCL IQ3_S + Maple TQ1_0/TQ2_0 CUDA; vLLM BitNet request (#33142). - Training-side FP8: Unsloth FP8 LoRA on 16-bit bases (#16423). **Distributed serving / parallelism** - Unsloth: `UNSLOTH_PARALLEL` unified DP/TP/PP/CP mesh (#16407) — the clearest training-scale parallelism advance. - SGLang: DSpark indexer-CP on NVFP4; TP4 NVFP4 serving bundle (#47807); Agentic Cache Scheduling roadmap. - vLLM: benchmarking RFC for reproducible BYO-GPU PR evals (#61698). **Batching / scheduling** - llama.cpp: per-size CUDA graph arenas for small batches ≤8 tokens, avoiding speculative-verify recapture (#31156). - vLLM: batch-invariance work across NVFP4/GPTQ (correctness under batching, not just speed). - Ollama: fit-aware eviction at the 80% threshold. **Observation:** The frontier has bifurcated. **Cloud/server engines (vLLM, SGLang) are pushing 4-bit/FP4 kernels on the newest accelerator generations**, while **edge runtimes (llama.cpp) are pushing cache and graph-scheduling efficiency on format-varied hardware.** The two rarely overlap, and a third track — **distributed training parallelism** — sits with Unsloth. --- ## 5. Layer Positioning ``` ┌───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ APPLICATION / AGENT LAYER │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ GATEWAY │ LiteLLM — routing, budgets, cost tracking, │ │ │ provider translation, virtual keys │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ SERVING ENGINE │ vLLM │ SGLang │ │ (server/cloud) │ throughput- │ multi-vendor accelerators, │ │ │ optimized, │ broadest hardware reach, │ │ │ Rust frontend │ diffusion + LLM │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ LOCAL RUNTIME │ Ollama │ llama.cpp │ │ │ UX-focused │ lowest-level ggml/backend, │ │ │ API wrapper │ broadest quant + form │ │ │ over backends │ factor coverage │ ├───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ TRAINING / │ Unsloth — LoRA/QLoRA/FP8 fine-tuning, │ │ FINE-TUNING │ parallelism mesh, Studio GUI │ └───────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ ``` **Key differentiation:** - **vLLM and SGLang are direct competitors** at the server engine layer. vLLM optimizes the *reference-architecture path* (DeepSeek-V4 depth, batch invariance, Rust frontend for hot-path overhead). SGLang pursues *hardware breadth* (AMD/NPU/XPU) and *diffusion serving*. Where they overlap (SM120, DSV4.1), they share the same bugs — suggesting common upstream dependencies (FlashInfer, Triton). - **Ollama and llama.cpp are stack-adjacent, not competitors.** Ollama is a user-facing runtime and API surface that consumes llama.cpp backends and MLX; its differentiators are scheduler policy, prompt caching, and API ergonomics. llama.cpp is the substrate — its innovations (unified KV, MoE cache, per-size graphs) propagate upward into Ollama and other consumers. - **LiteLLM sits at the gateway layer,** orthogonal to inference. Its Rust migration is about reducing proxy overhead, not model performance. Its critical risk profile is **billing and multi-tenancy**, not throughput. - **Unsloth operates upstream of serving.** Training outputs feed inference engines, and its FP8/parallelism work expands what can be fine-tuned — but it shares almost no operational concerns with the serving tier. --- ## 6. Trend Signals **Signal 1 — DeepSeek-V4/V4.1 is the ecosystem's stress test.** Three of four inference projects carry open DSV4-family bugs, and vLLM's bug list (engine crashes, KV-connector failures, sparse-indexer divergence) mirrors SGLang's (scheduler crash, allocator OOM, prompt-render divergence). This is a **maturity gap between model release cadence and engine support**, not a single project's failure. *Application developers should treat DSV4.1 serving as beta-grade through at least this quarter and pin verified builds.* **Signal 2 — SM120 (RTX PRO 6000 / Blackwell workstation) is not production-ready for frontier models.** SGLang's fa4 CUDA-graph crash on GLM-5.3-Flash and its 2–7K vs 12.5K tok/s DeepSeek-V4-Flash prefill gap, combined with vLLM's SM120 TurboQuant workspace bug and an open SM120 support request (#40802), indicate **kernel coverage lags SM100 by roughly one release cycle.** *If you are evaluating RTX PRO 6000 for cost-efficient serving, budget for backend triage or wait for kernel roadmap items to land.* **Signal 3 — Control planes are being rewritten in Rust.** vLLM (frontend feature parity, 50 comments) and LiteLLM (router core, Redis client, forwarding server — ~10 stacked PRs) are both moving hot-path control logic to Rust, with **byte-compatible Redis layouts to allow mixed-version rolling deploys**. This is a coordinated pattern: Python orchestration on the edges, Rust on the request path. *Operators should test dual-process topology changes (LiteLLM forwarding server) and Rust-frontend gating (`VLLM_USE_RUST_FRONTEND=1`) in staging before enabling.* **Signal 4 — Cost and budget enforcement in gateways is unreliable.** LiteLLM's open 1,000,000× overbilling bug, team-member budget bypass via fallback, and crash on null token counts mean **spend caps cannot be trusted as hard guardrails today.** Combined with the cross-tenant exact-match cache leak (semantic caches scoped, exact-match not), gateway operators face both billing and isolation risk. *Reconcile against provider invoices; disable exact-match caching across tenants; treat budget caps as best-effort.* **Signal 5 — MoE expert caching is the practical VRAM-efficiency winner.** llama.cpp's ClassLRU cache (+6–7% decode, −8% uploads) and Ollama's per-model cache budgets both target the same problem: serving large MoE models on constrained memory. *If you run large MoE models locally or on mixed hardware, this is the highest-ROI optimization area in this window.* **Signal 6 — Speculative decoding has backend-specific failure modes.** llama.cpp's HIP `--spec-type draft-mtp` cuts prefill ~80%, while Vulkan is unaffected; Ollama's MLX runner aborts at 101 repeated tokens. *Speculative decoding is not portable across backends — validate per-deployment rather than enabling globally.* **Signal 7 — Multi-vendor accelerator support is widening, and with it, bug surface.** SGLang is landing AMD MI350X/MI355X and NPU code paths; llama.cpp is adding Hexagon, OpenCL/Adreno, and XDNA requests; vLLM has open SM120/CPU-wheel/BitNet requests. The breadth is real, but **non-NVIDIA paths consistently show stability and memory-accounting gaps** (SYCL `--fit` under-accounts, 100–1000× `--cpu-moe` slowdown, DEVICE_LOST on tensor split). *Multi-vendor deployments should expect a longer stabilization tail than NVIDIA-only fleets.* **Signal 8 — Long-running RL/agent rollout loops are becoming a first-class design constraint.** vLLM's direct-weight-reload RFC (#54477, validated across 17 model families), `reset_prefix_cache()` allocation-order request, and ID-only request-logging proposal (#64654) all point to the same workload shape: **long-lived sessions where weight updates, prefix caching, and observability interact badly.** SGLang's Agentic Cache Scheduling roadmap (#43098) addresses the same problem from the router side. *Application developers building agent rollout infrastructure should design for cache invalidation and weight-reload semantics now, before these land.* **What agent/application developers should watch:** 1. **vLLM #54477 and #64654** — direct weight reload for RL and gateway-friendly request lifecycle logging. 2. **SGLang --- ## Per-Project Reports

Note that the `UNSLOTH_STUDIO_HOME` isolated-install overwrite incident ([#16186](https://github​.com/unslothai/unsloth/issues/16186), [#16185](https://github​.com/unslothai/unsloth/issues/16185)) is now CLOSED — operators relying on per-home venv/cache isolation should still audit existing installs, as the bug could have silently clobbered a baseline venv before the fix. ## 3. New Model & Hardware Support - **Gemini model enumeration fixed**: the picker was capped at the first page of 20 models and used a family allowlist that hid newer releases (`gemini-4-argon`, `gemini-3.8-flash`, `gemini-3.7-flash`). Fix follows `nextPageToken` and drops the allowlist — [#16433](https://github​.com/unslothai/unsloth/pull/16433) (fixes [#16432](https://github​.com/unslothai/unsloth/issues/16432)). - **MoE GGUF config UI**: `MoE Layers on CPU` slider now hidden when `GPU Layers = 0` — [#16429](https://github​.com/unslothai/unsloth/pull/16429) (fixes [#16427](https://github​.com/unslothai/unsloth/issues/16427)). - **CLI VLM gap flagged**: `unsloth inference`/`chat` still cannot accept image input, so VLMs can be trained but not exercised from the CLI — [#16340](https://github​.com/unslothai/unsloth/issues/16340) (closed, likely triaged). Related: `--trust_remote_code` is not plumbed through the CLI, blocking models like `LiquidAI/LFM3-Omni-2B` — [#16331](https://github​.com/unslothai/unsloth/issues/16331). ## 4. Performance & Optimization - **FP8 LoRA on 16-bit bases** — previously `float8_training` was rejected outright with LoRA. Now the frozen base Linear layers run fp8 forward and input-gradient while adapters train normally: `FastLanguageModel.from_pretrained(..., load_in_4bit=False, float8_training=True)` — [#16423](https://github​.com/unslothai/unsloth/pull/16423). - **Unified parallelism flag** — `UNSLOTH_PARALLEL="dp=2,tp=2,cp=2,fsdp=1"` maps to a single device mesh with a capability registry gating valid combinations; pipeline parallel is now configurable from the environment — [#16407](https://github​.com/unslothai/unsloth/pull/16407). - **Multi-LoRA grouped experts numeric fix** — adapter scale was folded into the second factor before the grouped GEMM in compute dtype, causing fp16 overflow (e.g. rank 1, alpha 16, `B=5000` → `80000 > 65504`). Scale now applied after the second GEMM — [#16414](https://github​.com/unslothai/unsloth/pull/16414). - **Pipeline-parallel GradScaler agreement** — fused Adam/AdamW must agree on `found_inf` once per step so all PP stages skip together — [#16417](https://github​.com/unslothai/unsloth/pull/16417). - **LTX worker memory reporting** — `_memory_stats` now reads RSS in MiB correctly (macOS `ru_maxrss` is bytes, not KiB; `/proc/self/statm` absent on macOS). Prior reports were ~1024× inflated peak — [#16438](https://github​.com/unslothai/unsloth/pull/16438). ## 5. Stability & Regressions Ranked by severity (most severe first); all listed Studio items now have fixes merged or in review: 1. **[Critical, CLOSED] Isolated installs clobber baseline venv** — `UNSLOTH_STUDIO_HOME= ./install. --- > ⚠️ Content exceeds the GitHub issue size limit; see the committed Markdown file for the full report.

# Knowledge Ops — Demo Seed Spec

> Source: `specs/tasks/knowledge-ops-demo-seed.md`

> *One script turns the devel workspace into a working tenant with populated collections and a review queue.*

---

## Purpose

Define what `seed_devel_tenant.py` creates so the devel workspace demonstrates all five layers end-to-end.

---

## What the Seed Script Does

### Step 1: Create the `devel` tenant

```python
POST /api/km-labels/tenants/
{
    "tenant_id": "devel",
    "name": "Devel Workspace",
    "domains": ["docs", "specs", "services", "packages", "inbox"],
    "config": {
        "isolation_mode": "pool",
        "default_model": "glm-4.7-flash",
        "embedding_model": "BAAI/bge-m3",
        "embedding_dim": 1024,
        "supported_languages": ["en"],
        "public_collection": "public_docs",
        "internal_collections": ["devel_docs", "devel_specs"]
    }
}
```

### Step 2: Ingest docs into Qdrant collections

Run `ingest_docs.py` three times:

| Command | Collection | Source | Purpose |
|---------|-----------|--------|---------|
| `python ingest_docs.py ~/devel/docs --collection devel_docs` | `devel_docs` | `docs/` | Layer 3 internal knowledge |
| `python ingest_docs.py ~/devel/specs --collection devel_specs --ext .md` | `devel_specs` | `specs/` | Layer 3 design docs |
| `python ingest_docs.py ~/devel/services --collection devel_docs --ext .md` | `devel_docs` | `services/*/README.md` | Layer 3 service docs |

**Skip**: `orgs/`, `node_modules/`, `.git/`, hidden files, files < 100 chars.

### Step 3: Create sample documents in CMS

Insert 3-5 documents into the `documents` table to demonstrate the visibility model:

| Doc | Title | Visibility | Source | Content |
|-----|-------|-----------|--------|---------|
| 1 | "What is Promethean?" | `public` | ai-drafted | Summary of the devel stack from ingested docs |
| 2 | "Deploying Futuresight KMS" | `public` | ingested | From `services/futuresight-kms/README.md` |
| 3 | "Internal Architecture Notes" | `internal` | manual | From `docs/MASTER_CROSS_REFERENCE_INDEX.md` |
| 4 | "New Feature Blog Draft" | `review` | ai-drafted | Draft generated from specs |
| 5 | "API Reference (Archived)" | `archived` | ingested | Old API doc, pulled from public |

Then sync docs 1 and 2 to Qdrant `public_docs` collection (they are `public`).

### Step 4: Create sample review items

Insert 3-5 rows into `km_labels` table to demonstrate Layer 5:

| Item | Question | Answer | Labels |
|------|----------|--------|--------|
| 1 | "How do I deploy futuresight-kms?" | "Run docker compose up..." | correctness: correct, overall: approve |
| 2 | "What is Shibboleth?" | "A Clojure DSL for adversarial prompt evaluation" | correctness: correct, overall: approve |
| 3 | "How do I reset my SSO token?" | "Navigate to Settings → Security" | correctness: partially-correct, overall: needs-edit, gold_answer: "Contact your admin at admin@..." |
| 4 | "What services does this team offer?" | "We offer AI consulting..." | correctness: incorrect, overall: reject |

### Step 5: Sync `public_docs` collection

For each `visibility=public` document:

```
POST Ragussy /api/rag/ingest/text
{
    "text": "<document content>",
    "source": "cms:<doc_id>",
    "collection": "public_docs",
    "metadata": { "tenant_id": "devel", "doc_id": "<doc_id>", "visibility": "public" }
}
```

---

## Script Structure

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Seed the devel tenant with docs, collections, and sample data."""

import httpx
import os
import sys

KM_LABELS_URL = os.getenv("KM_LABELS_URL", "http://localhost:3002")
RAGUSSY_URL = os.getenv("RAGUSSY_URL", "http://localhost:8000")
TENANT_ID = "devel"

def main():
    # 1. Create tenant
    create_tenant()

    # 2. Ingest docs into Qdrant
    ingest_collections()

    # 3. Create CMS documents
    create_cms_documents()

    # 4. Create review items
    create_review_items()

    # 5. Sync public docs to public_docs collection
    sync_public_collection()

    print("\n✓ Seed complete")
    print(f"  Tenant: {TENANT_ID}")
    print(f"  Collections: devel_docs, devel_specs, public_docs")
    print(f"  CMS docs: 5 (2 public, 1 review, 1 internal, 1 archived)")
    print(f"  Review items: 4")
    print(f"\n  Layer 1 widget: POST /api/widget/chat (public_docs)")
    print(f"  Layer 2 CMS: GET /api/cms/documents")
    print(f"  Layer 3 search: POST /api/rag/search (devel_docs)")
    print(f"  Layer 5 review: GET /api/km-labels/devel")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    main()
```

---

## What You See After Seeding

| Layer | Endpoint | Response |
|-------|----------|----------|
| 1. Widget | `POST /api/widget/chat { "message": "What is Promethean?" }` | Answer from `public_docs` with citations |
| 2. CMS | `GET /api/cms/documents` | 5 docs with visibility badges |
| 2. CMS | `GET /api/cms/documents?visibility=public` | 2 published docs |
| 2. CMS | `POST /api/cms/draft { "topic": "Our coding standards" }` | AI-generated draft from `devel_docs` |
| 3. Search | `POST /api/rag/search { "query": "deployment", "collection": "devel_docs" }` | Internal docs about deployment |
| 5. Review | `GET /api/km-labels/devel` | 4 labeled items, 1 needs-edit |
| 5. Export | `GET /api/export/devel/sft` | JSONL training data from approved items |

---

## Files to Create

| File | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `services/futuresight-kms/scripts/seed_devel_tenant.py` | Main seed script |
| `services/futuresight-kms/scripts/seed_cms_docs.py` | CMS document creation helper |
| `services/futuresight-kms/scripts/seed_review_items.py` | Review item creation helper |

## Files to Reference

| File | Why |
|------|-----|
| `services/futuresight-kms/scripts/ingest_docs.py` | Reuse for Qdrant ingestion |
| `packages/futuresight-kms/python/km_labels/routers/tenants.py` | Tenant creation endpoint |
| `packages/futuresight-kms/python/km_labels/routers/cms.py` | CMS document creation (to be built) |
| `packages/futuresight-kms/python/km_labels/routers/labels.py` | Review item creation endpoint |

## Verification

- `python seed_devel_tenant.py` exits 0 with all steps confirmed.
- `GET /api/widget/chat { "message": "What is Promethean?" }` returns answer from `public_docs`.
- `GET /api/cms/documents` returns 5 docs with correct visibility badges.
- `GET /api/km-labels/devel` returns 4 labeled items (1 needs-edit).

## Definition of done

- The devel workspace demonstrates all five layers end-to-end from a single seed run.

---

**Triage 2026-05-29 (incoming → accepted, scored):** Was unscored (`null` points) and body was truncated — filled from worktree spec. Scored **3sp**: the task is writing the seed script definition and the three helper scripts (not implementing CMS routes). The note "Specified 2026-04-01. Blocking questions resolved" in the spec confirms this is ready to implement. Accepted at P2.

---

**Triage 2026-05-29 (accepted → ready):** All four ready-gate conditions pass: 3sp ≤ 5sp; DoD is unambiguous (single seed run demonstrates all five layers, with exact verification endpoints); no hard inter-task dependency is unresolved (policy seam DONE, arity fix IN_REVIEW but not a prerequisite for writing the seed scripts); scope is fully bounded with enumerated payloads, file names, and acceptance checks and no TBDs in the acceptance criteria.
