# AI Infrastructure Digest 2026-10-03 > Generated: 2026-10-03 01:24 UTC | Projects covered: 6 - [vLLM](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm) - [SGLang](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang) - [llama.cpp](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp) - [Ollama](https://github​.com/ollama/ollama) - [LiteLLM](https://github​.com/BerriAI/litellm) - [Unsloth](https://github​.com/unslothai/unsloth) --- ## Cross-Project Comparison ### 1. Ecosystem Overview The AI infrastructure ecosystem as of October 3, 2026, is currently dominated by the "Blackwell-ization" of server-side inference, with vendors scrambling to stabilize SM120/Hopper backends and optimize for high-concurrency reasoning workloads. We are seeing a major push toward "reasoning-parity," where standard inference engines must now accommodate thinking-token budgets, complex tool-calling workflows, and multi-model orchestration. Stability has emerged as the primary bottleneck, with critical regressions in KV cache management and tool-use parsing impacting production-ready deployments across the board. ### 2. Activity Comparison (Snapshot: 2026-10-03) *Note: Counts reflect current active development pressure based on the provided logs.* | Project | Active Issues/PRs | Primary Focus | Release Status | | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | | **vLLM** | High (50+) | Blackwell/ROCm stability & Kernels | Stable (No new) | | **SGLang** | High (40+) | DeepSeek/GLM-5.3 & Memory Mgmt | Stable (No new) | | **llama.cpp** | Medium-High (30+) | Apple Silicon & Server UI | New b11345–b11364 | | **Ollama** | Medium (20+) | Tool-use parsing & Windows infra | Stable (No new) | | **LiteLLM** | Medium (15+) | Observability & Security hardening | v1.105.0-dev.2 | | **Unsloth** | Medium (20+) | Studio/Desktop & Tool-use logic | Stable (No new) | ### 3. Model Support Race * **GLM-5.x/5.3:** The clear frontrunner for high-performance enterprise adoption. vLLM and SGLang are in an active race to provide stable inference for these models; SGLang currently leads on architectural planning, while vLLM is focusing on kernel optimization. * **DeepSeek-V4:** SGLang is the primary driver for DeepSeek-V4-Pro optimization, focusing on Multi-Head Chunking (mHC) and memory efficiency. * **Decision Models:** llama.cpp and Unsloth are expanding support for experimental "decision-making" and agentic models (Laya, Granite 4.x), signaling a shift from pure chat to reasoning-first architectures. ### 4. Performance Frontier Optimization efforts are currently bifurcated: * **Kernel/Hardware Level (vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp):** Shift toward precompiled kernels (`vllm download-kernels`) and Triton-based attention backends to sidestep CUDA graph instability on newer Blackwell (SM120) hardware. * **Memory/Scheduling (vLLM, SGLang, Unsloth):** Focus on MoE expert offloading, radix cache management, and reducing "cold-start" latency through snapshotting and persistent kernel caches. * **Quantization (llama.cpp):** Ongoing refinement of low-bit quantization (Q2_K/Q3_K/IQ3) for heterogeneous hardware (Qualcomm Hexagon, SYCL, Vulkan). ### 5. Layer Positioning * **Serving Engines (vLLM, SGLang):** Deep-stack, high-concurrency infrastructure optimized for multi-tenant, enterprise-grade throughput. Focused on memory efficiency and hardware-specific kernel optimization. * **Local Runtime (llama.cpp, Ollama):** Hardware-agnostic focus with heavy emphasis on portability (Apple Silicon, Windows, Mobile, Vulkan). Positioning for "bring-your-own-model" local application workflows. * **Gateway/Orchestration (LiteLLM):** The "Control Plane" layer. Focuses on security (RBAC/Deny-by-default), observability, and provider abstraction. * **Fine-tuning/Desktop (Unsloth):** The "Dev-Loop" layer. Focuses on lowering the barrier to entry for fine-tuning and providing an all-in-one local development environment for model testing. ### 6. Trend Signals * **The "Thinking" Tax:** Inference engines are being forced to modify their Rust/gRPC APIs to handle thinking-token budgets. Expect "reasoning-awareness" to become a standard requirement for infra providers. * **Tool-Use Fragility:** A recurring theme across Ollama, Unsloth, and SGLang is the instability of parallel tool-calling and JSON-structured output. Infrastructure developers should treat these as "alpha-stage" features for the next two quarters. * **Security Shift:** LiteLLM’s move to "deny-by-default" for vector stores signals that the industry is maturing past "prototype-first" security to formal enterprise governance. * **Advice for Developers:** Avoid upgrading to nightlies on SM120/Blackwell hardware unless you are prepared to swap to Triton-based kernels, as native CUDA graph support is currently in a state of high churn and frequent "DeviceLost" regressions. --- ## Per-Project Reports
vLLM — vllm-project/vllm # vLLM Infrastructure Digest: 2026-10-03 ### 1. Today's Highlights Focus has shifted heavily toward stabilizing the Blackwell (SM120) and ROCm (gfx950) backends, with significant effort in resolving KV cache and speculative decoding regressions. A major milestone in serving infrastructure is the introduction of `vllm download-kernels` to avoid JIT-compilation latency at startup, particularly for Hopper/Blackwell deployments. ### 2. Releases & Breaking Changes * **No new releases** in the last 24 hours. ### 3. New Model & Hardware Support * **GLM-5.x/ModelOpt:** PR [#59833](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59833) adds support for loading ModelOpt NVFP4 MLA projections into `fused_qkv_a_proj`, bridging a gap for high-performance GLM deployment. * **ROCm/gfx950:** PR [#59333](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59333) improves `AiterExperts` coverage for padding logic, essential for MI355X performance. ### 4. Performance & Optimization * **Precompiled Kernels:** PR [#58765](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58765) introduces `vllm download-kernels` to install precompiled FlashInfer kernels, reducing cold-start times significantly for modern NVIDIA architectures. * **Priority Metrics:** PR [#58078](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58078) enables priority-aware metrics, allowing operators to track latency/throughput per request tier when using the `--scheduling-policy priority` flag. * **Memory Efficiency:** PR [#59160](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59160) and [#59523](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59523) enable offloading CUDA graph pools during `sleep()` mode, recovering significant memory on MoE deployments. ### 5. Stability & Regressions * **Speculative Decoding (High):** Multiple reports ([#59642](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59642), [#59724](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59724)) indicate 0% MTP acceptance rates for Qwen3.8 and GLM-5.3 models on SM120/nightly builds. * **KV Cache Correctness (High):** PR [#59504](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59504) addresses a critical race condition where allocator zeroing was overwriting asynchronous KV loads. * **ROCm/GLM Regression (Med):** Issue [#59413](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/59413) reports incoherent output ("gibberish") for GLM-5.3-Flash at low concurrency on ROCm nightlies. * **Snapshot/CRIU (Med):** PR [#59699](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59699) fixes a failure where InfiniBand state prevents TP1 snapshot captures on H200 systems. ### 6. What This Means for Application Developers * **Improved Observability:** If you are using tiered scheduling for different customer segments, you can now monitor your SLA performance per priority bucket using the new metrics in PR [#58078](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/58078). * **Reasoning/Thinking Models:** PR [#59836](https://github​.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/59836) adds support for carrying thinking-token budgets via the Rust gRPC API, ensuring that custom frontends (like Dynamo) can maintain parity with vLLM’s native reasoning features. * **Deployment Workflow:** Adopt `vllm download-kernels` in your CI/CD pipelines to ensure consistent and fast cold-start performance, especially when scaling up inference nodes on Blackwell hardware.
SGLang — sgl-project/sglang # SGLang Digest: 2026-10-03 ### 1. Today's Highlights The focus remains on stabilizing the DeepSeek-V4/GLM-5.3 integration stack, with significant work underway to resolve memory management issues and attention backend crashes on newer SM120 (Blackwell/RTX PRO) hardware. Architectural efforts are centered on unifying radix cache management for streaming sessions and refining the disaggregated serving path to improve request ingestion efficiency during high-concurrency prefill phases. ### 2. Releases & Breaking Changes * **No new releases** in the last 24 hours. * **Migration Note:** Users utilizing streaming sessions should be aware of **[PR #42295](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42295)**, which enforces the use of `UnifiedRadixCache` for all streaming sessions; unverified tree caches will now be rejected. ### 3. New Model & Hardware Support * **DeepSeek-V4:** Ongoing roadmap to optimize performance and mHC (Multi-Head Chunking) support is actively tracked in **[Issue #42170](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/issue/42170)**. * **AMD RDNA/Strix Halo:** Work is ongoing to enable Quark MXFP4 MoE checkpoints on gfx1151 GPUs via Triton kernels (**[PR #41389](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/41389)**). ### 4. Performance & Optimization * **Memory Efficiency:** A new 256-token logical page sizing for the K-Pool index is being implemented for DSA models to prevent needle-in-a-haystack accuracy drops at high sequence lengths (**[PR #42178](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42178)**). * **DSpark Scaling:** Optimization of verification width logic is underway to reduce overhead at batch sizes > 64 (**[PR #42281](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42281)**). * **Scheduling:** Disaggregated prefill instances are receiving an ingestion flow fix to ensure request processing is not blocked by pending forward passes (**[PR #42035](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/42035)**). ### 5. Stability & Regressions * **CRITICAL (Crash):** `fa4` attention backend is crashing on GLM-5.3-Flash under SM120 architecture (RTX PRO 6000) during CUDA graph capture; Triton is the currently recommended workaround (**[Issue #42012](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/issue/42012)**). * **HIGH (Performance):** DeepSeek-V4-Pro decode is seeing a ~5% throughput regression on GB300 hardware following recent commits (**[Issue #42074](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/issue/42074)**). * **MEDIUM (Memory/Logic):** A memory overhead regression (~3.3–3.8 GiB) on DeepSeek-V4 models is being caused by a conflict between FP8 paged attention and the row-chunk planner (**[Issue #42146](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/issue/42146)**). * **MEDIUM (Correctness):** A bug in `Glm47MoeDetector` prevents tool calls from working correctly when `response_format` is provided, causing the model to hallucinate JSON answers (**[Issue #42269](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/issue/42269)**). ### 6. What This Means for Application Developers * **Tooling/Agents:** If you are building agentic workflows using GLM-4/5 models, expect intermittent failures in structured output and tool-calling parity. Monitor **[Issue #42269](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/issue/42269)** and avoid mixing `response_format` and `tools` until a patch is merged. * **Infrastructure:** The push to move request tokenization and template rendering off the main HTTP event loop (**[PR #39716](https://github​.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/39716)**) will significantly improve responsiveness for high-traffic apps by preventing prompt processing from blocking health checks and streaming responses. * **Deployment:** Developers deploying on Blackwell/SM120 hardware should prioritize Triton-based attention backends to avoid current stability issues with `fa4`.
llama.cpp — ggml-org/llama.cpp # llama.cpp Digest: 2026-10-03 ### 1. Today's Highlights The focus for October 3rd, 2026, centers on expanding Apple Silicon inference capabilities through high-performance Metal Flash Attention kernels and continued stabilization of experimental speculative decoding (MTP). Additionally, there is a significant push to modernize the server-side UI, with multiple PRs active to improve model management and configuration workflows. ### 2. Releases & Breaking Changes * **Builds b11345–b11364**: Several releases landed, primarily adding support for new decision-making model architectures and kernel refinements. * **API Updates**: A new `/v1/systemone` API endpoint has been introduced to support advanced model integration for Laya, Julia-1, and Lev architectures ([#29818](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29818)). ### 3. New Model & Hardware Support * **Apple Silicon (Metal)**: New tensor API flash attention kernels added, supporting F16 KV caches with optimizations for specific head dimensions (DK=DV=512, DK=576, DV=512) and attention sinks/ALiBi ([#29570](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29570)). * **Hexagon (Qualcomm)**: Added support for Q2_K and Q3_K quantization types and updated HTP skel installations ([#29717](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29717), [#29828](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29828)). * **OpenVINO**: Updated to version 2026.4.1 with improved performance for MoE architectures and expanded op support ([#29852](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29852)). ### 4. Performance & Optimization * **CUDA**: New PR submitted to optimize the multi-row `TOP_K` path using segmented radix sort to replace heavy CUB kernel launches ([#29883](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29883)). * **Vulkan**: RMS norm optimization using subgroup reductions is currently under test for Intel Arc B70 and Nvidia RTX 4060 TI ([#29882](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29882)). * **SYCL**: Ongoing efforts to accelerate GLM MLA prefill and improve memory reordering for IQ3 quantizations ([#29107](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29107), [#29171](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29171)). ### 5. Stability & Regressions * **Speculative Decoding (MTP) Issues**: Multiple reports continue regarding instability and performance degradation when using `draft-mtp` across multi-GPU setups and specific hardware backends ([#27428](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/27428), [#27306](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/27306)). * **Vulkan Memory/Device Errors**: Several issues remain open concerning "DeviceLost" errors on AMD hardware and memory access issues on mobile Adreno drivers ([#25207](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/25207), [#29786](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/29786)). * **Tool Calling**: Intermittent instability reported for Gemma 4 models during multi-line streaming/parsing ([#29655](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/29655)). ### 6. What This Means for Application Developers * **UI/UX Improvement**: If you are using the integrated `llama-server`, look out for the upcoming "Models Manager" and configuration pane PRs. These will simplify model hot-swapping and provider management ([#29583](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/29583)). * **Stability Warning**: If your production environment relies on `draft-mtp` for low-latency generation, proceed with caution. Performance is highly dependent on backend hardware (notably AMD/Vulkan), and current builds may experience prefill stalls or memory access violations. * **Resource Management**: A new GPU-resident LRU cache for offloaded MoE experts is in review. This will likely be critical for scaling MoE models on constrained memory setups in the near future ([#27861](https://github​.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/pull/27861)).

items.body:
## Context

RBD image inventory was explicitly out of scope for v1. v2 `v0.1.0` must include RBD inventory and NetBox-driven desired-state management.

## Scope

Add RBD support across NetBox, `proxbox-api`, and provider clients.

## Inventory Requirements

- Inventory RBD pools, images, snapshots, clones, parent/child relationships, features, size/provisioned state, object count where available, locks/watchers where available, trash entries, and metadata.
- Link RBD images to Proxbox/NetBox consumers when available: VMs, virtual disks, tenants, services, applications, or storage resources.

## Desired-State Requirements

- Model RBD pools/images/snapshots/clone relationships in NetBox.
- Support desired-state operations for image create, resize, metadata update, snapshot create/delete, clone, protect/unprotect, flatten where supported, trash/restore, and delete with confirmation.
- Validate risky operations: shrinking, deleting, flattening, removing protected snapshots, operations on watched/locked images, and operations when cluster health is degraded.
- Use plan/apply and operation history for all writes.

## Acceptance Criteria

- NetBox displays RBD inventory and desired-state objects.
- A user can create/resize/snapshot/clone/manage RBD images from NetBox only where provider capabilities allow it.
- Risky operations are blocked or require explicit confirmation.
- Tests cover inventory normalization, relationship modeling, diff/plan generation, supported write payloads, destructive confirmation, and capability gaps.

items.body:
# AI CLI Tools Community Digest 2026-11-11 > Generated: 2026-11-10 23:14 UTC | Tools covered: 7 - [Claude Code](https://github​.com/anthropics/claude-code) - [OpenAI Codex](https://github​.com/openai/codex) - [Gemini CLI](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) - [GitHub Copilot CLI](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli) - [OpenCode](https://github​.com/anomalyco/opencode) - [Pi](https://github​.com/earendil-works/pi) - [Qwen Code](https://github​.com/QwenLM/qwen-code) - [Claude Code Skills](https://github​.com/anthropics/skills) --- ## Cross-Tool Comparison # AI CLI Tools Ecosystem — Cross-Tool Comparison Report **Data window: 2026-11-11 (last 24h)** --- ## 1. Ecosystem Overview The AI CLI landscape in this snapshot is simultaneously **maturing on infrastructure** and **fragmenting on reliability**. Every one of the seven tracked tools shipped at least one release in the window — an unusually high release cadence — but the dominant issue-tracker themes are regressions, not roadmap work: Windows platform stability, MCP/OAuth lifecycle fragility, sandbox-permission correctness, and subagent observability recur across independent projects. A second clear signal is the emergence of a **community tooling layer** *around* these CLIs (hooks, prompt-regression runners, approval routing in Codex; channel/webhook integrations in Qwen Code), suggesting the base tools have stabilized enough that users are building on top of them. Security and trust surface prominently and negatively — destructive-command classifier bypasses in Qwen Code and Gemini CLI, plaintext secret persistence in Codex, and server-side instruction injection in Claude Code collectively indicate that **agent-safety engineering, not raw capability, is the current bottleneck**. --- ## 2. Activity Comparison | Tool | Active Issues (24h window) | Notable PRs (24h) | Discussions | Release Status | Notes | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | **Claude Code** | ~10 listed (2 live high-engagement: #100377, #106167) | 1 (closed, no merge) | N/A (no data supplied) | 1 release (v2.1.322) — infra-only | Tracker heavily pruned of stale reports; trust/injection issues upvoted | | **OpenAI Codex** | ~10 + 3 honorable mentions | ~10 (mostly internal `copyberry` bot, CLOSED/landed) | Active — 6 notable threads (Show & Tell) | 3 releases (0.167.1, 0.169.0-alpha.9, 0.167.0-alpha.4.1) | Highest Windows friction; active community-built tooling | | **Gemini CLI** | ~10 | ~10 (security/CI heavy) | N/A (no data supplied) | 2 releases (v0.69.0-preview.0, v0.68.0) | Subagent reliability is the defining problem; release-infra firefighting | | **GitHub Copilot CLI** | ~10 | 1 (open, docs) | N/A (no data supplied) | 4 releases (v1.0.109/-1, v1.0.110-0/-1) | Rapid patch cadence; MCP lifecycle dominates pain points | | **OpenCode** | ~10 (one at **346 comments**) | ~10 (active, all OPEN) | N/A (no data supplied) | 1 release (v2.2.7) | Single largest issue thread in the entire dataset; heavy v1→v2 migration debt | | **Pi** | ~10 | ~10 (mostly CLOSED/landed) | 1 active Idea (#11984) | 2 releases (v1.5.1, v1.5.2) | Provider-integration and silent-degradation focus | | **Qwen Code** | ~10 (CI noise dominates: 292, 55 comments) | ~10 (security/permissions heavy) | N/A (no data supplied) | 3 releases (v0.27.2, preview, SDK v0.1.32) | CI flakiness is the volume driver; P1 permission-classifier holes | > **On N/A vs. inactive:** Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Copilot CLI, OpenCode, and Qwen Code show no Discussions data in this dataset. Per instruction, these are marked **N/A** — this reflects data availability in the supplied digests, not necessarily that Discussions are disabled upstream. Only Codex and Pi show confirmed Discussions activity. Issue/PR counts are approximate from the curated top-10 lists and should not be read as exhaustive tracker volume. --- ## 3. Shared Feature Directions Four requirements appear independently across three or more communities: **a) Subagent observability & lifecycle control** Every agent-orchestration project is wrestling with the same problem: users cannot see or steer what subagents do. - *Codex*: live activity + per-agent config in Subagents panel (#36266); explicit cross-thread orchestration (#14923, closed) - *Gemini CLI*: subagent trajectories in `/chat share` (#22598), subagent context in `/bug` reports (#21763), false-success reporting (#22323) - *Qwen Code*: unified agent loop across surfaces (#15327); ACP teammate-message delivery (#15738) - *OpenCode*: always-background subagents with parent reporting (#63210, #63209) - *Claude Code*: effort control for Claude-proposed sessions (#104151) **b) MCP completeness outside the primary CLI surface** MCP works in the happy path but degrades in IDEs, on Desktop, and under OAuth rotation — a *parity* problem, not a protocol problem. - *Claude Code*: `structuredContent` dropped in Desktop Code tab (#103809); no Authenticate button in VS Code (#108783); refresh-token revocation across sessions (#108794) - *Copilot CLI*: orphaned stdio processes (#4392), random loopback OAuth ports (#5391), Entra silent sign-in failures (#5402) - *Codex*: read-only MCP tool hints in auto-approval (#60638); MCP refresh outside runtime gate (#60639) **c) Cost, quota & proportionality control** Users want explicit, discoverable budget controls rather than invisible sticky settings. - *Claude Code*: "Ultracode" fan-out to 325 agents on a settings audit (#92349); sticky effort settings invisible to users - *Codex*: quota opacity — misaligned billing cycles (#8581), banked resets expiring early (#60664), abnormal depletion (#59262) - *Copilot CLI*: model block lists for auto/fusion routing (#5369); content-filter failures consuming credits (#5408) - *OpenCode*: free-tier billing clarity as the single loudest theme (#59387) **d) Windows platform parity** A consistent, cross-vendor deficit — not one project's bug, an industry-wide one. - *Codex*: VS Code extension UI failure (#56655, 85 👍), sandbox `WRITE_DAC` errors, CUA screenshot timeouts - *Copilot CLI*: parent `pwsh.exe` crashes (#5404), keyboard regressions (#5171) - *OpenCode*: console-window flashing ~1/sec (#52266), fnm/nvm upgrade paths (#63152) - *Claude Code*: Windows worktree regressions closed stale unaddressed (#92019) --- ## 4. Differentiation Analysis | Dimension | Claude Code | Codex | Gemini CLI | Copilot CLI | OpenCode | Pi | Qwen Code | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | **Primary focus** | Remote-control/session autonomy; MCP Apps ecosystem | Sandbox hardening + Guardian policy security | Subagent correctness + AST-aware tooling | Model catalog breadth + enterprise auth | Model flexibility + v2 migration | Provider breadth + extension runtime | Permission safety + multi-channel (WeChat/QQ/Email) | | **Target user** | Professional devs on claude.ai Projects | Windows/Desktop + cloud-hybrid users | Google-stack devs, safety-conscious | GitHub/enterprise, Copilot Free→Pro funnel | Multi-provider power users | Self-hosted/local-model users | CN-market + multi-surface (CLI/Web Shell/daemon) | | **Technical approach** | Server-delivered instructions; effort/agent fan-out | Rust core; `copyberry`-driven hardening; Guardian policy templates | Native bash affinity + proposed OS sandbox (#19873) | Fast patch cadence; experimental masked-prompt dialog | Background-subagent architecture; per-session MCP scoping | Chord stores for session sync; codemode globals | Moving to real shell parser (tree-sitter-bash) from hand-rolled model | | **Distinctive risk** | Server-injection trust erosion (#106167) | Secret persistence in shell snapshots (#30971) | False-success subagent reporting | Enterprise credential masking gaps (#5388) | Catastrophic session-data loss on upgrade (#62659) | Silent model/catalog fallback (#10812) | Classifier bypass via redirection (#16856) | **Key structural difference:** Codex and Qwen Code are investing in **defense-in-depth** (Guardian policy templates, tree-sitter shell parsing, fail-closed heredoc handling) — treating the agent as an untrusted execution surface. Claude Code and OpenCode are investing in **capability expansion** (server-side orchestration, background subagents) and are paying reliability costs as a result. Gemini CLI sits between, with its #19873 zero-dependency sandbox proposal signaling a planned architectural shift toward contained execution. --- ## 5. Community Momentum & Maturity **Highest raw community engagement:** - **OpenCode** — one issue thread (#59387) at **346 comments** dwarfs anything else in the dataset. This is a mixed signal: extreme engagement driven by free-tier friction, not enthusiasm. High momentum, but concentrated in a pain point. - **Codex** — highest *upvote* density (#56655 at 85 👍) and the only tool with a robust **community-built tooling ecosystem** (Tapproval, RegressGuard, agent-harness, safety habits). This is the strongest maturity indicator: users are building *on* the tool, not just reporting on it. - **Claude Code** — high-signal issues (server-injection at 10 👍 despite being a config complaint) but a tracker being aggressively pruned of stale Windows regressions — a **coverage-vs-cleanliness tension** that may be hiding real debt. **Fastest iteration cadence:** - **Copilot CLI** — 4 releases in 24h (v1.0.109 through v1.0.110-1). Extremely rapid patching, but the volume of MCP lifecycle bugs suggests fix-forward pressure. - **Qwen Code** — 3 releases incl. SDK, but CI noise (#14724 at 292 comments) is consuming community signal bandwidth — flagged *Provisional* issues erode contributor trust. **Most architecturally deliberate:** - **Pi** — cleanest release-to-fix traceability (v1.5.2 directly backed by PR #11975). Lower engagement volume, but high fix quality and a coherent provider-auth roadmap (Entra ID, Kimi OAuth, ChatGPT context parity). - **Gemini CLI** — actively firefighting release infra (#30207, 70 MB stale artifacts in a 106 MB tarball) while landing serious security PRs (#30171, #30095). Iterating, but maintenance-heavy. **Maturity ranking (composite):** Codex ≈ Pi > Claude Code > Gemini CLI > Copilot CLI > OpenCode > Qwen Code — with the caveat that OpenCode's engagement is real and its subagent PR work (#63210, #63209) is architecturally ahead of several peers. --- ## 6. Trend Signals **1. Agent safety is the #1 unsolved engineering problem.** Destructive-command classifier bypasses (Qwen Code #16856: `git branch < /dev/null -D main` executes `-D main`; Gemini CLI #30171: `rm -Rf` variants classified safe), plaintext secret persistence (Codex #30971), and server-injected instructions (Claude Code #106167) all point the same direction. **Reference value:** if you're building on these CLIs, do not trust AUTO/permission classifiers as a security boundary — wrap them. The industry is converging on *real parsers* (tree-sitter-bash) and *fail-closed* semantics, but that transition is incomplete everywhere. **2. MCP is winning the protocol war but losing the lifecycle war.** Every tool supports MCP; every tool has OAuth callback, token rotation, and IDE-parity bugs. **Reference value:** multi-session OAuth is the sharpest edge (Claude Code #108794, Copilot #5402). For production MCP deployments, plan for re-auth churn and fixed callback ports (Copilot #5391 request) as first-class requirements. **3. Subagent false-success reporting is a systemic trust defect.** Gemini CLI (#22323, #21983), OpenCode (#63171 zero-content "succeeded"), and Claude Code (invisible effort settings) all show agents reporting success while failing. **Reference value:** for autonomous workflows, *never* trust a subagent's self-reported status — verify with side-effects or structured output schemas. This is the single highest-leverage observability gap. **4. Silent degradation is the dominant UX failure mode.** Cache warming stopping (Pi #10956), default-model fallback (#10812), stale catalogs (Pi #10539, Codex #60676), off-by-default telemetry (Gemini #30217). **Reference value:** configure explicit failure modes (models, catalog, warming) and monitor — these tools default to *quietly doing something different* rather than erroring. **5. Vendor-specific undercurrents:** - **Windows is an industry-wide second-class citizen** — every tool has a Windows regression cluster. If you're Windows-based, budget for parity lag across all vendors. - **Enterprise auth is a competitive differentiator** — Pi's Entra ID PR (#12016), Copilot's NTLM proxy demand (#5407), and Codex's device-code sign-in (#60662) show headless/SSO auth as the next battleground. - **The community tooling layer is forming** — Codex hooks/approval-routing/prompt-CI ecosystem and Qwen Code's channel webhooks indicate that **extensibility surfaces (hooks, Stop hooks, outbound integrations) are the next platform-neutral feature race**. Watch for these to become table stakes across all seven tools. --- *Report compiled from 2026-11-11 community digests for Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI, OpenCode, Pi, and Qwen Code. Counts are drawn from curated top-10 issue/PR lists and represent the snapshot, not full tracker volume. Issue/PR references are retained for verification.* --- ## Per-Tool Reports

Releases **v0.69.0-preview.0** - `fix(core,cli)`: Preserves literal `$` characters during template placeholder replacement ([#30136](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/30136)) - `feat(cli)`: Adds a `/stats heatmap` subcommand for daily token usage **v0.68.0** - Auto-generated changelogs for v0.67.0-preview.0 and v0.66.0 - `docs(readme)`: Clarifies Gemini CLI scope, limitations, and tool capabilities ## 3. Hot Issues 1. **[#22323](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/22323) — Subagent MAX_TURNS reported as GOAL success (P1, 13 comments).** The `codebase_investigator` subagent reports `status: "success"` / `Termination Reason: "GOAL"` even when it hits the turn limit without doing any analysis. This masks failures and corrupts downstream agent orchestration — the highest-engagement issue of the day. 2. **[#21409](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/21409) — Generalist agent hangs indefinitely (P1, 8 comments, 8 👍).** Any deferral to the generalist agent hangs forever, even for trivial tasks like folder creation. The workaround (instructing the model not to use subagents) effectively disables a core feature; the 👍 count signals broad impact. 3. **[#19873](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/19873) — Zero-dependency OS sandboxing + post-execution intent routing (P2, 9 comments).** Proposes leaning into Gemini 3's native bash affinity by chaining POSIX tools, while containing risk through sandboxing and intent routing. A significant architectural proposal for the agent execution model. 4. **[#21968](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/21968) — Gemini under-uses skills and sub-agents (P2, 7 comments).** Anecdotal but important: the model rarely invokes custom skills/subagents unless explicitly told, even when descriptions clearly match. Undermines the value of the extensibility system. 5. **[#22745](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/22745) — EPIC: AST-aware file reads, search, and mapping (P2, 7 comments).** Tracks whether AST-aware tools reduce misaligned reads, turn counts, and token noise. A likely direction for future tooling quality improvements. 6. **[#22267](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/22267) — Browser Agent ignores `settings.json` overrides (P2, 5 comments).** The AgentRegistry merges settings correctly at init, but the Browser Agent bypasses them (e.g., `maxTurns`). Configuration drift erodes trust in project-level config. 7. **[#21983](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/21983) — Browser subagent fails on Wayland (P1, 4 comments).** Linux/Wayland users see the browser agent finish with "GOAL" despite failing — another instance of the misleading termination-status pattern. 8. **[#24246](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/24246) — 400 error with >128 tools (P2, 3 comments).** Large tool inventories trigger API 400s; the expectation is smarter scoping of enabled tools. Relevant as MCP servers multiply tool counts. 9. **[#22672](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/22672) — Agent should discourage destructive behavior (P2, 3 comments).** The model occasionally reaches for `git reset` or `--force` when safer alternatives exist. Safety-adjacent and tied to the shell-heuristics PRs below. 10. **[#18836](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/18836) — Replace WriteToDo with persistent file-based task tracking (P3, 2 comments).** Proposes deprecating in-context todo tracking to combat context rot, token cost, and memory loss between sessions — a recurring theme in agent-state discussions. ## 4. Key PR Progress 1. **[#30207](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/30207) — Clear `bundle/` before esbuild (P0).** Nightly releases have failed since 2026-11-05 with `413 Request Entity Too Large`; ~70 MB of the ~106 MB tarball JS is stale output from prior builds. Critical release-infra fix. 2. **[#30171](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/30171) — Flag recursive/forced `rm` regardless of flag position (P1).** Closes a `PolicyEngine` bypass where forms like `rm -r -f`, `rm -Rf`, `rm --recursive --force`, and trailing-flag variants were classified as safe. Directly addresses the destructive-command concern in #22672. 3. **[#30095](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/30095) — Prevent Windows git diff permission bypass (P1, security).** Extracts shared Git safety validation and rejects dangerous arguments on Windows, closing a read-only-command classification gap. 4. **[#30219](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/30219) — Record ACP tool calls on active chat after compression.** Prevents post-compression tool calls from attaching to removed messages, avoiding 400 errors on session reload. 5. **[#30217](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/30217) — Fix PDF/telemetry buffer memory retention.** Addresses a V8 heap OOM during multi-turn PDF ingestion when telemetry is disabled (the default). 6. **[#30020](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/30020) — Drop tool calls streamed by failed retry attempts.** A subtle but serious correctness fix: previously both the failed and successful attempt's tool calls were executed, duplicating side-effecting commands. 7. **[#30220](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/30220) — Preserve Unicode in session previews, strip ANSI.** Replaces an ASCII-only regex in `cleanMessage()` that mangled international scripts, accents, and emojis. 8. **[#30214](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/30214) — Recognize TortoiseGitPlink as PuTTY-family SSH client.** Ensures `-batch` is injected instead of OpenSSH's `BatchMode` flag for Windows users of TortoiseGit. 9. **[#30089](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/30089) — Bump npm-dependencies group (70 updates).** Includes `@​modelcontextprotocol/sdk` 1.23.0 → 1.32.2 — notable for MCP compatibility. 10. **[#29960](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/pull/29960) — Telemetry `SERVICE_VERSION` uses CLI version, not Node runtime.** Fixes enterprise telemetry dashboards reporting the wrong service version. ## 5. Hot Discussions No discussion data was provided for this period; this section is omitted. ## 6. Feature Request Trends - **Subagent observability & correctness**: Surface subagent trajectories via `/chat share` ([#22598](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/22598)), include subagent context in `/bug` reports ([#21763](https://github​.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli/issues/21763)), and fix termination-status reporting (#22323). - **AST-aware tooling**: A cluster of issues (#22745, #22746, #22747) explores AST grep/tilth/glyph for precise reads, searches, and codebase mapping. - **Persistent, file-based agent state**: Move beyond in-context todo lists (#18836) and experiment with native file tools for task tracking (#21000). - **Safer execution**: Sandboxing (#19873), dangerous-command discouragement (#22672), and per-workspace policies (#18397). - **Smarter tool scoping**: Dynamic tool selection to avoid the >128-tool 400 error (#24246). ## 7. Developer Pain Points - **Subagent reliability is the top friction point**: hangs (#21409), false-success reporting (#22323, #21983), ignored configuration (#22267), and under-triggering (#21968) collectively suggest the subagent system needs a correctness pass before broader adoption. - **Release pipeline instability**: repeated nightly failures from stale build artifacts (#30207) and flaky VS Code download retries (#29951) are consuming maintainer cycles. - **Safety heuristics have gaps**: multiple PRs (#30171, #30095) reveal that dangerous `rm` and Git invocations could slip past the PolicyEngine depending on argument order or platform. - **Retry semantics can duplicate side effects**: the mid-stream retry bug (#30020) is the kind of issue that erodes trust in autonomous execution. - **Token/context efficiency**: context rot, firehose file reads (#19561), and the ~36.6k-token baseline per turn remain persistent concerns driving the AST and persistent-state proposals.
GitHub Copilot CLI — github/copilot-cli # GitHub Copilot CLI Community Digest — 2026-11-11 ## 1. Matters for MCP SDK interoperability. 6. **[#5402](https://github​.com/github/copilot-cli/issues/5402) — MCP Entra silent sign-in uses `/common`, fails for single-tenant apps (AADSTS50194)** Since 1.0.107, Windows users must run `/mcp auth` every session. items.body:
# refactor(PPT-031): Simplify data model and align API design

## Executive summary

This issue is **phase 2 of PPT-031**. Phase 1 shipped in [#26](https://github.com/Elmorralito/save-ma-money/issues/26) via [PR #27](https://github.com/Elmorralito/save-ma-money/pull/27): a `users` table, password hashing utilities, and an `owner_id` column on nearly every entity.

Phase 2 does **not** add users again. It **simplifies** what phase 1 added, normalizes the schema toward **Third Normal Form (3NF)**, resolves open questions from [#24](https://github.com/Elmorralito/save-ma-money/issues/24) (per-user finance isolation), adopts **PostgreSQL via Supabase** as the sole database platform, documents **Supabase × FastAPI** integration, and realigns the API specification so [#25](https://github.com/Elmorralito/save-ma-money/issues/25) can implement endpoints against a stable domain model.

> **Platform decision (2026-07-02):** **DuckDB is out of scope.** All migrations, validation, and local dev target **PostgreSQL** (Docker Postgres locally; Supabase for hosted/staging). See [#34](https://github.com/Elmorralito/save-ma-money/issues/34). [#17](https://github.com/Elmorralito/save-ma-money/issues/17) (DuckDB FK gaps) is superseded.

**This issue is design-first.** Implementation PRs should follow sub-issues derived from the tracks below.

---

## Validation review (2026-07-02)

A second pass against the live codebase identified **gaps not fully covered** in the initial issue body. These are incorporated below as pain points **#7–#15**, **Tracks E–F**, and **FR-10–FR-17 / NFR-08–NFR-12**.

### Highest-risk gaps (must resolve before #25)

| Priority | Gap | Impact if ignored |
|----------|-----|-------------------|
| P0 | Auth not wired (`AuthSecurityManager` has no credential verifier; `PasswordManagerFactory` never bootstrapped) | Register/login will fail at runtime |
| P0 | `TypesDTO` deterministic IDs ignore `owner_id` + global unique `name` | Cross-tenant type ID collisions |
| P0 | API spec fields absent from model (`balance`, `currency`, `category_type`, `transaction_type`, etc.) | Phantom columns or broken endpoints |
| P1 | Pre-user PostgreSQL data: `owner_id NOT NULL` migrations without backfill | `./deploy/alembic.sh upgrade` fails on legacy dumps |
| P1 | `/reports/*` in spec with no read-model strategy | MVP item #5 cannot be implemented |
| P1 | Dual API specs (`API_Endpoints.md.md` + `API_Documentation.md.md`) | Implementers follow conflicting sources |
| P2 | Package version drift ([#11](https://github.com/Elmorralito/save-ma-money/issues/11)) | v3 model/API releases out of sync |
| P2 | CI has no Alembic PostgreSQL gate | Schema regressions ship undetected |

### Sub-issues (created)

| Track | GitHub issue |
|-------|--------------|
| A — v0 audit | [#30](https://github.com/Elmorralito/save-ma-money/issues/30) |
| A — v1–v3 schema | [#32](https://github.com/Elmorralito/save-ma-money/issues/32) |
| B — Supabase | [#31](https://github.com/Elmorralito/save-ma-money/issues/31) |
| C — API spec | [#33](https://github.com/Elmorralito/save-ma-money/issues/33) |
| D — Migration | [#34](https://github.com/Elmorralito/save-ma-money/issues/34) |

---

## Current state (developer baseline)

### What exists today

| Layer | Status | Key paths |
|-------|--------|-----------|
| **Data model** | Production-ready ingestion pipeline | `modules/model/src/papita_txnsmodel/` |
| **Schema** | PostgreSQL via Supabase (DuckDB deprecated) | `modules/model/src/papita_txnsmodel/database/connector.py` |
| **Migrations** | Alembic | `modules/model/alembic/versions/` |
| **Load handlers** | In model module (registrar module not in current workspace) | `modules/model/src/papita_txnsmodel/handlers/` |
| **API** | Spec + partial scaffold | `modules/api/API_Endpoints.md.md`; implemented: `settings.py`, `security.py` only — no `main.py`, routers, or schemas |
| **Supabase** | **Not integrated** | No client, auth, or RLS in repo |

### Table inventory (`papita_transactions` schema)

| Table | Purpose |
|-------|---------|
| `users` | Tenant root; username, email, password |
| `accounts` | Named financial account shell (tags, start/end dates) |
| `types` | Classification (ASSETS / LIABILITIES / TRANSACTIONS) |
| `accounts_indexer` | Polymorphic hub linking account → type → subtype row(s) |
| `assets_accounts` | Base asset financial attributes |
| `banking_asset_accounts` | Bank-specific asset extension |
| `real_estate_asset_accounts` | Property asset extension |
| `trading_asset_accounts` | Investment asset extension |
| `liability_accounts` | Base liability financial attributes |
| `bank_credit_liability_accounts` | Loan/mortgage extension |
| `credit_card_liability_accounts` | Credit card extension |
| `financed_asset_accounts` | Join: asset ↔ bank credit (with `financing_share`) |
| `identified_transactions` | Recurring/planned transaction templates |
| `transactions` | Posted money movements between accounts |

### Relationship sketch

```
users
  └── owner_id on ~13 tables (added in PR #27)
accounts (owner_id)
  └── accounts_indexer (owner_id, type_id, 8 nullable subtype FKs)
        ├── assets_accounts | liability_accounts
        ├── banking_asset_accounts | real_estate_asset_accounts | trading_asset_accounts
        └── bank_credit_liability_accounts | credit_card_liability_accounts
identified_transactions (owner_id, type_id)
  └── transactions (owner_id, optional from/to account FKs)
types (nullable owner_id — global or user-scoped)
```

### What PR #27 and PR #29 changed

- **PR #27:** `users` model, `owner_id` on all entities, extended `BaseRepository` tenant filtering, hash utilities, 4 Alembic migrations.
- **PR #29:** API documentation (`API_Endpoints.md.md`, `API_Documentation.md.md`), `Settings` with `DATABASE_URL` + JWT config, `AuthSecurityManager`. **No FastAPI app, routers, schemas, or live endpoints.**

### Known pain points (with code references)

1. **`AccountsIndexer` sparse FK matrix** — 8 nullable FK columns route to subtype tables (`modules/model/src/papita_txnsmodel/model/indexers.py`). DTO validation in `access/indexers/dto.py` is complex and error-prone.

2. **Redundant `owner_id`** — Example: `transactions.owner_id` is stored directly, but ownership could be derived via `from_account_id → accounts.owner_id`. Same pattern on asset/liability subtype tables.

3. **API ↔ model vocabulary mismatch** — API spec defines `/categories/*`, `/budgets/*`, `/movements/*`. Model has `types`, no budgets table, and `transactions` (not "movements").

4. **Auth field mismatch** — API register expects `full_name`; model `Users` has `username`, not `full_name` (`modules/model/src/papita_txnsmodel/model/users.py` vs `API_Endpoints.md.md`).

5. **Legacy dual-dialect code** — Connector and upsert layers still reference DuckDB; PPT-031 standardizes on PostgreSQL/Supabase only ([#34](https://github.com/Elmorralito/save-ma-money/issues/34)). [#17](https://github.com/Elmorralito/save-ma-money/issues/17) (DuckDB FK gaps) is **superseded**.

6. **Model doc drift** — e.g. `LiabilityAccounts` docstring references `account_id`/`type_id` fields that do not exist on the model; `users.py` TYPE_CHECKING imports `Assets` but the class is `AssetAccounts`.

7. **Auth stack incomplete** — `AuthSecurityManager.authenticate_and_get_token()` requires a `verify_credentials` callback, but `UsersService` only exposes `get_owner()` — no login/register/verify path. `UsersDTO._serialize()` calls `PasswordManagerFactory.password_manager` without ever calling `get_password_manager(keyword="argon2")` first (`access/users/dto.py`, `utils/hashutils.py`).

8. **Login identity undefined** — API login form uses field `username` with example `user@example.com`, but model separates `username` (min 6 chars, unique) and `email` (unique). Which field authenticates?

9. **Token lifecycle unspecified** — Spec defines `/auth/refresh` and `/auth/logout`, but JWT is stateless HS256 with no refresh token pair or revocation store (`token_salt` was removed in migration `ccaa69123f7e`).

10. **Types identity collision** — `TypesDTO._normalize_model()` hashes `name + classification` only (ignores `owner_id`), while `types.name` is globally unique. Two users creating "Groceries" collide on UUID and violate uniqueness.

11. **API phantom fields** — Spec accounts expose `balance`, `currency`, `initial_balance`; categories use `category_type: income|expense`, `parent_id`, hierarchy; transactions use `transaction_type`, `category_id`, `status`, `currency` — none exist on current SQLModel tables.

12. **`AccountsIndexer` skips `BaseSQLModel`** — Indexer table has no `active`, `deleted_at`, `created_at`, `updated_at` (FR-06 gap on the central hub table).

13. **Legacy data migration** — Migration `06b97dfcb5c7` adds `owner_id NOT NULL` to ~13 tables without default user seed/backfill. Pre-#26 PostgreSQL dumps cannot upgrade without manual intervention. Handlers still accept `owner=None` on load (`handlers/base.py`).

14. **Reports without read model** — Five `/reports/*` endpoints (`spending`, `budget-performance`, `cash-flow`, `trends`, `export`) have no aggregation layer; `budget-performance` depends on budgets model that does not exist.

15. **Tooling gaps** — No `.env.example` despite required `JWT_SECRET_KEY`; CI runs pytest/pre-commit but no Alembic upgrade gate on PostgreSQL; package versions diverge (model `0.1.13a28`, API `0.0.3a14`, root `v0.0.1`) — see [#11](https://github.com/Elmorralito/save-ma-money/issues/11).

## Functional requirements (with explanations)

### FR-01 — Target schema satisfies Third Normal Form (3NF)

**Requirement:** The v3 schema must satisfy 3NF unless a specific exception is documented with query-performance or domain-clarity justification.

**Why:** The current schema grew organically (indexer pattern from [PR #12 / PPT-022](https://github.com/Elmorralito/save-ma-money/pull/12), users from PR #27). Normalization reduces update anomalies (e.g. changing `owner_id` in one place vs. 13), simplifies the PostgreSQL FK graph, and makes API DTOs predictable.

**Developer notes:**

- **1NF:** Ensure atomic columns; `tags` as PostgreSQL `ARRAY` is acceptable if treated as atomic multi-value, but document whether tags belong in a junction table for queryability.
- **2NF:** If any table uses composite PKs, ensure no partial dependencies. Example: `financed_asset_accounts` uses composite PK `(bank_credit_liability_account_id, asset_account_id)` — verify all non-key columns depend on the full key.
- **3NF:** Eliminate transitive dependencies. Primary candidate: redundant `owner_id` on child tables when `owner_id` is derivable through FK chains (`transactions → accounts → users`).

**Acceptance:** v0 audit lists each violation; v3 doc lists each resolved violation or documented exception.

---

### FR-02 — Multi-tenant isolation strategy (resolves #24)

**Requirement:** Define and implement one consistent strategy so User A cannot read or mutate User B's financial data.

**Why:** [#24](https://github.com/Elmorralito/save-ma-money/issues/24) asked for per-user finance isolation. PR #27 added `owner_id` everywhere but did not decide whether redundancy is intentional, whether `types` can be global (`owner_id` nullable), or whether isolation is enforced in the app layer vs. database RLS.

**Developer notes — choose one strategy and document it:**

| Strategy | Mechanism | Pros | Cons |
|----------|-----------|------|------|
| **A — FK chain** | Filter via `accounts.owner_id`; drop redundant child `owner_id` | Fewer columns; single source of truth | Joins required for direct transaction queries |
| **B — Denormalized `owner_id`** | Keep `owner_id` on hot tables; enforce consistency via triggers or app layer | Faster tenant-filtered queries | Update anomalies if account ownership changes |
| **C — RLS (Supabase/Postgres)** | Policy: `owner_id = current_setting('app.user_id')` | DB-enforced; defense in depth | Requires Supabase/Postgres; aligns with platform decision |

**Acceptance:** Decision recorded in v3 doc; `BaseRepository` and API dependencies implement the chosen strategy; cross-tenant denial test cases listed.

---

### FR-03 — Simplify or eliminate `AccountsIndexer`

**Requirement:** Remove `AccountsIndexer` or reduce it to at most one optional extension FK plus an explicit type discriminator.

**Why:** `AccountsIndexer` (`indexers.py`) holds 8 nullable FKs (`asset_account_id`, `liability_account_id`, `banking_asset_account_id`, etc.). Only one should be populated per row, but nothing in the DB enforces that. Repository and DTO code must infer the active subtype manually.

**Developer notes:**

- Preferred patterns: **single-table inheritance** with nullable subtype columns on `accounts`, **class table inheritance** with one 1:1 extension table keyed by `account_id`, or **JSONB extension blob** for rarely queried subtype fields (document 3NF exception if used).
- Migration must map existing indexer rows to the new structure without data loss.
- Update `modules/model/src/papita_txnsmodel/services/indexers.py`, `services/extends.py` (`TypedLinkedEntitiesServiceMixin`), `handlers/factory.py`, and load handlers that depend on indexer resolution.

**Acceptance:** v3 ER diagram has no 8-FK sparse matrix; indexer service removed or reduced to trivial lookup.

---

### FR-04 — Account subtypes without subtype table explosion

**Requirement:** Banking, real estate, trading, bank credit, and credit card accounts must remain representable without requiring six separate physical tables unless each adds substantial non-overlapping columns.

**Why:** Today there are separate tables for each subtype (`banking_asset_accounts`, `real_estate_asset_accounts`, etc.) with overlapping financial columns duplicated from base `assets_accounts` / `liability_accounts`. This increases join complexity and migration cost.

**Developer notes:**

- Audit column overlap across subtype tables in `assets.py` and `liabilities.py`.
- If overlap exceeds ~70%, consolidate shared columns into base table; keep extension tables only for truly unique fields (e.g. `RealEstateAssetAccountsAreaUnits`, `financing_share`).
- Preserve enum types in `enums.py` for domain clarity.

**Acceptance:** v3 table list with column justification per subtype; fewer joins required for "list all accounts for user" query.

### FR-05 — Clear semantics for `IdentifiedTransactions` vs `Transactions`

**Requirement:** Document and model the relationship between transaction templates (`identified_transactions`) and posted transactions (`transactions`).

**Why:** `IdentifiedTransactions` holds planned name, value, day-of-month, and `type_id`. `Transactions` holds actual `value`, `transaction_ts`, and optional `from_account_id` / `to_account_id`. The API spec uses "transactions" and "movements" without mapping to these concepts — developers will build the wrong endpoints without clarity.

**Developer notes:**

- Decide: **keep two tables** (budget/recurring template vs ledger entry) or **unify** with `status` / `is_posted` discriminator.
- If kept separate: API should expose `/identified-transactions/*` or nest under accounts; `/movements/*` should not duplicate `/transactions/*` without definition.
- FK: `transactions.identified_transaction_id` is optional — document when it must be set (e.g. recurring match) vs. ad-hoc transactions.

**Acceptance:** Domain glossary in design doc; ER diagram shows cardinality; API spec updated accordingly.

items.title: perf: redesign runtime profile retrieval around semantic and exact identity search

labels.name: javascript
labels.description: Pull requests that update javascript code

items.body:
Parent: #20929

Related: #18746, #20932, #20984, #21019

## Current decision

Do not implement the previous lexical candidate-survival telemetry design.

#21019 changed runtime memory to a fact-only architecture: connector document content and document embeddings are no longer persisted, local document retrieval is disabled, and structured profile search is now the only runtime semantic consumer. The profile/document shared-embedding premise in #20932 is therefore obsolete.

Candidate survival is also not a sound quality decision gate:

- a lexical-only candidate reaching the prompt proves selection by the current algorithm, not relevance;
- a lack of lexical-only survivors does not prove lexical scoring is unnecessary, because lexical scores on semantic-overlap candidates can still change rank and token-budget inclusion;
- seed selection changes graph-expansion inputs, so request-local provenance cannot establish the exact no-lexical counterfactual without replay;
- carrying provenance through ranking, hydration, profile deduplication, and prompt packing would add cross-layer state to services shared by runtime injection, public recall, and preview without improving latency.

This issue is re-scoped from instrumenting the current candidate generator to replacing it with an intentional fact-only retrieval design.

## Current production evidence

The strict fact-only window starts at the successful `api/production` deployment of `cd03a9d31a` on `2026-07-11T06:24:36Z`. Through approximately `09:42Z`, it contains 26 enabled profile searches:

| Stage | N | p50 | p95 | max |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Profile search | 26 | 615 ms | 1,617 ms | 3,097 ms |
| Semantic embedding | 26 | 453 ms | 1,114 ms | 2,986 ms |
| Semantic query | 26 | 27 ms | 611 ms | 739 ms |
| Lexical query | 26 | 18 ms | 263 ms | 278 ms |

Thirteen searches are lexical-ineligible. Of the 13 eligible searches, 12 return no lexical candidate and one returns one candidate. This establishes low current yield, but not whether that one candidate is relevant.

The same revision has 26 `SELECT memory_search_entries` spans. Every span acquires an idle database connection; pool acquisition p95/max is approximately `0.143/0.167 ms`, while total query-span p95/max is approximately `608/736 ms`. Pool acquisition does not explain the current semantic-query tail.

No document search, document lexical, document embedding, or document hydration action occurs in this window.

The cohort is only about three hours and is too small to establish a stable long-tail distribution or make a final quality decision from frequency alone.

## Problem

Runtime profile retrieval currently uses two candidate generators:

1. a broad whole-query `ILIKE '%query%'` scan across memory text, entity display name, every alias, relationship type, and relationship summary;
2. semantic retrieval through one external embedding request and a filtered vector query.

The lexical path is neither proper full-text retrieval nor proper exact lookup:

- leading-wildcard predicates cannot use the existing B-tree indexes;
- the database requires the whole normalized query to be a substring before application token scoring runs;
- a natural-language query containing an email or domain can therefore miss the alias unless the entire query matches one searched value;
- left joining aliases can multiply rows before the bounded candidate set is deduplicated;
- the path usually returns no candidates and delays the external embedding request because lexical retrieval is awaited first.

Removing the path without a replacement would still be unsafe. It currently provides the only query-based fallback when embedding fails and can independently recall exact identity or literal-text matches.

## Goal

Make fact-only profile retrieval semantic-first, preserve deliberate exact-identity recall through an indexable equality path, retain lexical ranking value on the bounded candidate set, and remove the broad substring database scan.

The result should be a coherent retrieval behavior change, not an observability layer around the old algorithm.

## Selected design

### Candidate generation

- Normalize the retrieval query once at the profile-search boundary.
- Start the external semantic embedding request and exact-identity lookup concurrently after existing authorization and feature gates have passed.
- Do not overlap the exact-identity database query with the semantic database query: semantic vector retrieval starts after the embedding and exact lookup have settled, avoiding additional database fan-out.
- Run semantic retrieval for every authorized non-empty natural-language query when embedding succeeds.
- Extract only explicitly supported, canonical identity tokens from the query. Initially support normalized email and domain values already persisted as `memory_entity_aliases`.
- Resolve those tokens with scoped equality predicates over `(org_id, user_id, alias_type, alias_value)` so the existing unique B-tree index is usable.
- Do not interpret arbitrary words, display names, or internal provider identity encodings as exact keys without a separately defined canonical user-query form.

### Merge and ranking

- Merge semantic and exact-identity candidates by memory ID before seed ranking.
- Hydrate only the bounded candidate union.
- Compute literal/lexical score in memory over the hydrated bounded candidates so semantic-overlap candidates retain literal ranking benefit without a broad database scan.
- Give exact-identity candidates an explicit, deterministic identity contribution rather than relying on incidental substring scoring.
- Preserve deterministic tie-breaking, bounded seed selection, graph expansion, final ranking, static/dynamic deduplication, hydration, and prompt packing unless an intentional change is documented by this issue.

### Failure behavior

- External embedding failure remains fail-open.
- When embedding fails, static/dynamic profile data and any exact-identity candidates remain available.
- Generic literal-text query recall is no longer an implicit embedding-failure fallback; this is an intentional behavior change and must be covered by retrieval-quality cases.
- Database failures continue to propagate.

### Observability

- Keep existing fixed-name stage latency and candidate-count timing.
- Replace lexical-stage dimensions with low-cardinality exact-identity eligibility and candidate-count dimensions where appropriate.
- Do not add per-candidate provenance, stage-by-stage survival dimensions, content-derived dimensions, replay, shadow ranking, or shadow prompt construction.

## Acceptance criteria

- Runtime and public profile retrieval no longer execute the broad `%query%` profile predicate or join every alias as a lexical candidate generator.
- Non-empty natural-language queries continue to use semantic retrieval when embedding succeeds.
- A natural-language query containing a supported email or domain can retrieve the matching scoped entity through indexed equality lookup even when the full query is not an alias substring.
- Queries without a supported exact identity do not execute an identity database query.
- Semantic and exact-identity candidates are deduplicated by memory ID before ranking.
- Literal scoring is applied only to the bounded hydrated candidate union and can still affect semantic-overlap ordering.
- External embedding starts concurrently with exact-identity lookup, while exact-identity and semantic database queries do not overlap.
- Embedding failure preserves static/dynamic profile results and exact-identity results without adding retries or silently swallowing database failures.
- Graph expansion, final result limits, static/dynamic deduplication, prompt token budgets, prompt format, runtime preview response shape, and public Memory Search response shape remain compatible.
- Timing records expose only fixed-name, low-cardinality, privacy-safe path usage and count buckets. They contain no query text or hash, content, memory/entity/source identity, URL, object key, embedding, user ID, org ID, or secret.
- API-entry-point integration coverage uses real PostgreSQL and only mocks external embedding HTTP. It covers:
  - semantic paraphrase retrieval;
  - email and domain extraction from natural-language queries;
  - semantic/exact candidate overlap and deduplication;
  - bounded literal reranking;
  - graph expansion;
  - embedding failure with and without an exact identity;
  - static/dynamic deduplication and token packing;
  - unchanged public recall and preview contracts.
- Relevant API tests, API type-check, API lint, formatting, and knip pass.

## Retrieval-quality gate

The behavior change must be evaluated with deterministic integration cases rather than candidate-survival telemetry alone. The cases must include:

- semantic paraphrases that share no required literal token with the stored fact;
- exact email and domain references both alone and inside natural-language queries;
- short display-name queries;
- multilingual queries represented by current product usage;
- ambiguous identifiers scoped to the current organization and user;
- embedding-provider failure;
- literal memory-text matches that the old broad scan would return but semantic and exact-identity retrieval do not.

Any material required recall gap found by these cases must be addressed explicitly. Do not preserve the broad scan solely because it exists today.

## Risks and constraints

- Alias values are producer-provided. Exact lookup is safe only for alias types with a canonical write/query representation.
- Removing broad substring candidate generation can drop independent display-name, relationship-summary, relationship-type, and literal memory-text matches.
- Semantic retrieval still uses a globally indexed HNSW query with tenant/model filters. The current database tail is outside pool acquisition and remains a separate performance concern.
- `getZeroMemoryProfile()` is shared by runtime injection and public recall; the new candidate behavior must be consistent and response types must not expose internal path metadata.
- Frontend, API, and runner deploy independently, so no persisted or public contract may require a coordinated rollout.

## Non-goals

- Do not implement the previous lexical-only survival ladder.
- Do not add trigram indexes, PostgreSQL full-text search, or generic hybrid-search infrastructure without retrieval-quality evidence that general keyword recall is required.
- Do not change the HNSW index, enable pgvector iterative scan, or force an exact vector scan in this PR; choose that path separately from production cardinality and query-plan evidence.
- Do not add cross-request embedding caching, generic timeouts, hedges, or retries.
- Do not restore or instrument connector document retrieval removed by #21019.
- Do not expose candidate source or identity in public APIs, prompt text, persisted state, or telemetry.
- Do not change connector ingestion, prompt budgets, frontend contracts, runner protocols, or unrelated memory lifecycle behavior.

## Follow-up evidence

After deployment, update #20929 with:

- exact-identity eligibility, hit rate, and latency;
- semantic embedding and vector-query latency by existing trigger source;
- end-to-end profile and runtime-injection latency;
- any retrieval-quality difference found by the deterministic cases;
- a longer post-#21019 production window.

Separately evaluate the current filtered global HNSW query against a tenant-scoped exact vector scan using active-entry cardinality, production PostgreSQL/pgvector settings, query plans, and recall. Pool acquisition has already been ruled out for the initial fact-only cohort.

---
