items.title: [EPIC] Knowledge lifecycle correctness and reproducible agent retrieval
items.body:
## Objective

Bring the Vera Knowledge Fabric to **knowledge-lifecycle correctness and reproducible, agent-consumable retrieval**: exact chunk-level provenance, deterministic same-source update semantics, an authoritative-first write path, stale-projection deletion, genuinely hybrid retrieval, bitemporal reproducible snapshots, a complete MCP contract for coding agents, Confluence resilience, ontology governance, and governed Graphiti community lineage.

Scoped to verified gaps at commit `1bb70a6b38184cc766069e189440ee5e7616819b` (branch `main`, `KKloudTarus/vera`).

**Renamed from "production readiness".** Full production readiness (load/SLO, tenant-isolation security tests, MCP authorization, data-poisoning/prompt-injection defenses, backup/restore, retention/deletion, observability/incident recovery) is explicitly **out of scope here** and belongs to a separate dependent EPIC (see Non-goals). This EPIC is a prerequisite for that one.

## Current verified capabilities

Verified against HEAD `1bb70a6`. Local gates green (evidence block at the end).

- Fact / Assertion / Evidence / Entity / KnowledgeEvent model with content-derived `fact_key` / `slot_key` (`src/vera/domain/knowledge/fabric.py`).
- Reconciliation with authority-based single-valued supersession, withdraw-on-drop for a new version of the same artifact, and refute handling (`src/vera/application/curation/reconciliation.py`).
- Ontology governance persisted per version (cardinality, absence semantics, conflict strategy) with a startup code-vs-DB drift guard (`src/vera/domain/ontology/policy.py`, `descriptor.py`, `src/vera/bootstrap.py:verify_ontology`).
- Transactional outbox on `ingestion_jobs`; outbox-driven fabric fact-to-graph projection behind `memory.fabric_enabled` (`src/vera/entrypoints/worker/lane_pool.py`, `src/vera/application/projection/service.py`).
- Rebuildable RELATES_TO fact projection with drift verification (`src/vera/adapters/graph/fact_projection.py`, `application/projection/service.py:verify_group`).
- Community construction on Neo4j (native) and FalkorDB (bounded label-propagation + Graphiti LLM summarizer) (`src/vera/adapters/graph/graphiti_adapter.py`, `entrypoints/build_communities.py`).
- Gated pgvector passage/code retrieval behind the FTS ports (`src/vera/adapters/persistence/repositories/pgvector_index.py`, migration `e2b3c4d5f6a7`, `backfill_chunk_embeddings.py`).
- Snapshots freeze active fact membership, `as_of` valid-time, ontology version, source boundaries; context packs restrict passages to the snapshot freeze time (`src/vera/adapters/persistence/repositories/snapshot.py`, `application/snapshot/service.py`).
- Cross-scope DB role split behind `db.role_enforcement` (`src/vera/adapters/persistence/base.py`).
- Confluence connector drains pagination in one run and preserves headings as Markdown (`src/vera/adapters/connectors/confluence.py`).
- Retrieval quality gate: golden set + hit@k / MRR / nDCG@k / citation-rate (`datasets/retrieval/golden.json`, `application/queries/retrieval_eval.py`, `tests/integration/test_retrieval_golden.py`).
- MCP tools: `knowledge_get_context`, `knowledge_search`, `knowledge_explain_fact`, `knowledge_get_evidence`, `knowledge_feedback`, `knowledge_get_changes`, `knowledge_get_conflicts`, `knowledge_create_snapshot`, `knowledge_get_snapshot`, `knowledge_propose` (`src/vera/entrypoints/mcp/main.py`).

## Why this EPIC exists

The write, projection, and retrieval paths run and are gated, but several correctness and reproducibility properties required for an authoritative knowledge source are missing or partial: evidence without exact chunk-level provenance, incremental graph projection that never deletes stale facts, non-deterministic same-source updates, retrieval that is not genuinely hybrid, an incomplete MCP contract, and a Confluence connector without retry/tombstone/checkpoint semantics.

## P0 — Knowledge lifecycle correctness

### Exact chunk-level provenance (normalized)

Do not copy `heading_path` / full excerpt / coordinates onto every Evidence row (denormalized duplication). Reference an immutable Chunk and an ExtractionRun; the API joins to return the verbatim quote.

```text
Evidence
- chunk_id            # FK to the immutable chunk
- quote_start         # offset into chunk.content
- quote_end
- quote_hash          # hash of the exact quoted span
- citation_override   # optional, else derived from chunk/source
- extraction_run_id   # FK to ExtractionRun
Chunk
- artifact_version_id
- heading_path
- content
- content_hash
- source_coordinates
ExtractionRun
- model
- provider
- prompt_version
- pipeline_version
- started_at
```

The extractor must return the exact quote and its offsets; the worker cannot infer a span if the LLM paraphrases. Extend the extraction contract:

```json
{
  "subject": "Vera",
  "predicate": "RUNS_ON",
  "object": "PostgreSQL",
  "source_quote": "Vera stores authoritative facts in PostgreSQL.",
  "quote_start": 124,
  "quote_end": 173
}
```

- [ ] Extend the extraction contract (`domain/ports/curation.py:ExtractedClaim` and the extractor adapters) to return `source_quote`, `quote_start`, `quote_end`. Acceptance: `source_quote` is an exact substring of the immutable chunk; `hash(chunk.content[quote_start:quote_end]) == quote_hash`; offsets are computed on a fixed normalized-Unicode convention; if the span cannot be aligned the assertion goes to `needs_review` and no synthetic evidence is created. Tested.
- [ ] Persist Evidence with `chunk_id`, `quote_start/quote_end`, `quote_hash`, and `extraction_run_id` from the live triple-ingest path. Verified gap: `src/vera/entrypoints/worker/lane_pool.py:266` sets `excerpt=f"{subject} {predicate} {obj}"` with no `chunk_id`, even though `Evidence` supports it (`src/vera/domain/knowledge/fabric.py:230-234`) and `reconciliation.py:365-367` reads `prop.chunk_id`. Acceptance: `knowledge_get_evidence(fact_key)` returns the verbatim quote by joining Evidence → Chunk (not the synthetic `"subject predicate object"` string); integration test.
- [ ] Add an `ExtractionRun` record (model, provider, prompt_version, pipeline_version, started_at) sourced from `CURRENT_PIPELINE_VERSIONS`, referenced by each Assertion/Evidence produced by the live path. Acceptance: a test asserts non-null extraction lineage resolvable from any live-path assertion.

### Deterministic same-source update semantics

Verified partial and **not deterministic today**: reconciliation of the new value may occur before withdrawal of the previous version's assertion, so ECS can be marked `disputed` and is not guaranteed to be promoted back to `active`. Evidence: `reconciliation.py:_resolve_single_valued` (209-235) marks equal-authority as `disputed`; `_withdraw_dropped` (296-320) runs earlier but only when the new version drops the proposition.

**Version precedence must be defined explicitly.** `artifact_version_id` is a UUID and cannot order versions. Add ordering columns and compare on them:

```text
ArtifactVersion
- source_revision          # native revision number when the source provides one
- source_updated_at        # source-reported last-modified
- observed_at              # when Vera fetched it
- predecessor_version_id
```

Precedence policy: for the same artifact, if `incoming source_revision <= current source_revision` it is a **stale replay** and must not change the active fact. When the source has no revision number (e.g. Confluence), order by the stable tuple `(source_updated_at, source_version_id)`.

- [ ] Add `source_revision` / `source_updated_at` / `observed_at` / `predecessor_version_id` to ArtifactVersion and drive same-source precedence from them (not from the UUID). Acceptance: a stale replay (lower/older precedence) is a no-op on the active fact; tested.
- [ ] Make a newer version of the same artifact deterministically supersede the prior value regardless of reconcile/withdraw ordering: withdraw the prior version's assertion for the slot before (or atomically with) evaluating the new value, so the old value never leaves a `disputed` residue. Acceptance criteria — the final state is always ECS `active`, EKS `retracted/superseded`, for all three tests:
  - [ ] `v1 EKS → v2 ECS` (in order).
  - [ ] `v2 ECS processed before v1 EKS` (out-of-order delivery).
  - [ ] replay `v1 EKS` after `v2 ECS` is already active (a stale older version must not cause knowledge regression).
- [ ] Keep independent equal-authority sources as `disputed` (genuine conflict), distinct from same-artifact version replacement. Acceptance: a test with two different sources asserting EKS vs ECS at equal authority yields `disputed`.

### Authoritative-first write path

Verified gap: `lane_pool.py:181-185` calls `memory.ingest_episode` (graph) before `_reconcile_to_fabric` (facts) in the same transaction; only a boolean `memory.fabric_enabled` exists (`config/settings.py:235`), not distinct `legacy` / `dual` / `fabric` modes.

- [ ] Introduce explicit `legacy` / `dual` / `fabric` modes. In `fabric` mode, graph/vector/search projections originate only from committed fact/outbox events; no projection precedes the authoritative fact commit. Acceptance: an integration test proves that in `fabric` mode the episode graph write does not precede the fact commit, and projections are driven solely by the outbox.

### Stale projection deletion + idempotent replay

Verified gap: `application/projection/service.py:project_group` (31-38) projects only active facts and upserts them; it never removes edges for facts that became `superseded` / `withdrawn` / `retracted` / `expired`. Only `rebuild_group` (clear + reproject) removes them.

- [ ] Delete stale graph facts during incremental projection (not only on full rebuild). Acceptance: `EKS active → project → ECS supersedes EKS → project` ends with the graph containing ECS and not EKS, without a full rebuild.
- [ ] Make projection deletion idempotent under retry, duplicate delivery, and rebuild. Acceptance: two consecutive projections and a simulated duplicate outbox delivery yield identical `projected_fact_keys` and pass `verify_group(...).in_sync`.

## P1 — Reproducible retrieval and agent consumption

### Genuinely hybrid retrieval + live embeddings

Verified gap: `entrypoints/knowledge/service.py` selects `PgVectorPassageIndex` OR `SqlAlchemyPassageIndex` by flag (either/or); `application/retrieval/context_assembler.py` blends by weighted signals, no RRF; embeddings only on chunks; dimension frozen at 1024 (migration `e2b3c4d5f6a7`, `MemorySettings.vector_dim`).

- [ ] Fuse FTS and vector candidates with RRF (or a documented alternative) instead of replacing one with the other. Acceptance: an FTS-only chunk (no embedding) and a vector-only hit both appear in one fused ranked list; integration test.
- [ ] Store embeddings in a dedicated table, not a single vector column on `chunks` (a column pins each chunk to one model, but Vera switches between OpenAI / Voyage / self-hosted). Model:

```text
chunk_embeddings
- chunk_id
- provider
- model
- model_version
- dimension
- embedding
- content_hash
- created_at
- active
unique (chunk_id, provider, model, model_version)
```

  Acceptance: a chunk can hold embeddings from multiple models concurrently; re-embedding with a new model does not overwrite the old vector; a snapshot can pin an embedding/index version; a model rollback flips `active` without data loss. Tested.
- [ ] Reject a dimension mismatch (embedding length vs the model's declared dimension) with a clear error. Acceptance: test covers stored provenance and a rejected mismatch.
- [ ] Embed newly ingested chunks automatically on the live path when vector search is enabled (not only via `backfill_chunk_embeddings`). Acceptance: after ingest with vector on, chunks are ANN-queryable without a manual backfill; integration test.
- [ ] Run pgvector integration tests in CI. Verified gap: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:43` uses `postgres:18`, so the conditional pgvector migration is a no-op and `tests/integration/test_pgvector_retrieval.py` skips silently. Acceptance: the CI integration job uses a pgvector-capable Postgres image and the pgvector test executes (asserted by a non-zero pgvector test count in the run).

### Bitemporal reproducible snapshots

Do not conflate valid time and system time. A snapshot must record both:

```text
as_of_valid_time        # knowledge validity boundary
frozen_at_system_time   # ingestion/freeze boundary
```

Verified partial: snapshots freeze fact membership + `as_of` + ontology version + source boundaries and gap-12 restricts passages by freeze time, but do not record embedding/index version or a graph projection checkpoint.

- [ ] Record `as_of_valid_time`, `frozen_at_system_time`, embedding/index version, and a graph projection checkpoint on each snapshot. Acceptance (both must hold):
  - [ ] a fact not yet valid at `as_of_valid_time` does not appear;
  - [ ] an artifact/chunk ingested after `frozen_at_system_time` does not appear, even if it declares an older valid time.

### Complete MCP contract for coding agents

Define the contract before implementing; do not add a redundant alias of `knowledge_get_context`.

| Tool | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `knowledge_get_context` | High-level query that assembles a context pack |
| `knowledge_get_context_pack` | Retrieve an already-created pack by pack id / snapshot (retrieval only, never creates) |
| `knowledge_search` | Raw search, no assembly |
| `knowledge_explore` | Graph neighborhood / traversal |
| `knowledge_get_fact` | A single authoritative fact |
| `knowledge_get_entity` | An entity and its related facts |
| `knowledge_get_source` | A source, its artifact versions, and freshness |

`knowledge_get_context_pack` needs explicit persistence semantics: a pack must be stored and immutable so it can be re-read. Model:

```text
ContextPack
- pack_id
- scope_id
- snapshot_id
- request_hash
- result_references
- created_at
- expires_at
- assembler_version
```

- [ ] Add `knowledge_get_fact`, `knowledge_get_entity`, `knowledge_get_source`, `knowledge_explore`, and `knowledge_get_context_pack` (retrieval-only) per the table; none exist today in `entrypoints/mcp/main.py`. Acceptance: each tool resolves scope server-side and has an MCP contract test; `knowledge_get_context_pack` retrieves a stored pack, never creates one.
- [ ] Persist ContextPack (per the model above) so `knowledge_get_context_pack(pack_id)` returns a frozen result. Acceptance: the same `pack_id` always returns the same frozen result; a pack from another scope is not readable; an expired pack returns a clear error. If retrieval only recomputes from a snapshot rather than returning a stored pack, it must not be described as retrieving an already-created pack. Tested.
- [ ] Extend context parameters: `as_of` (valid time), snapshot id, repository, branch, code path, PRD/ADR/source-type filters, include/exclude predicates, authority/trust threshold, citation mode, conflict handling, and project alias/slug (not only internal group ids). Token budget already exists. Acceptance: each parameter changes the returned pack in a documented way, covered by tests.

## P2 — Production hardening (within this EPIC's scope)

- [ ] Confluence connector resilience. Verified gap: `adapters/connectors/confluence.py` has no `429`/`Retry-After`, no exponential backoff with jitter, no deleted/archived tombstones, no crash-safe per-page checkpoint, no bounded concurrency. Acceptance: honors `Retry-After`, backs off with jitter, emits tombstones for deleted/archived pages (which retract the corresponding facts), checkpoints each page so a crash resumes without loss or duplication, and bounds concurrency; tested with a mocked API across 28-, 100-, and 500-page spaces.
- [ ] Ontology governance completeness. Verified partial: `policy.py` persists cardinality/absence/conflict + drift guard; missing subject/object type-constraint enforcement, qualifier schemas, source-authority requirements, TTL/freshness, deprecation/replacement, and ontology version diff. Acceptance: reconciliation rejects/reviews assertions violating type constraints or required qualifiers; TTL expiry transitions facts to `expired`; an ontology version diff report exists; tested.
- [ ] Governed Graphiti community lineage (normalized, not a giant array on the node). Verified gap: community nodes carry `source_description="vera"` only (`graphiti_adapter.py:232`), no lineage, not consumed by retrieval, summaries not marked derived. **Source of truth for lineage is PostgreSQL** (consistent with ADR-0003: Postgres/S3 authoritative, the graph is a rebuildable projection); `community_fact_lineage` is a Postgres table, and the graph community node carries only the pointers needed to reference it. Model:

```text
community_fact_lineage        # PostgreSQL (authoritative)
- community_id
- fact_id
- derivation_run_id
Community node (graph projection, rebuildable)
- derivation_run_id
- source_fact_set_hash
- projection_checkpoint
- derived=true
```

  - [ ] Store per-fact lineage in the Postgres `community_fact_lineage` table, and put `derivation_run_id` / `source_fact_set_hash` / `projection_checkpoint` / `derived=true` on the graph community node as pointers to it. Acceptance: lineage is queryable and paginable from Postgres; the graph communities rebuild from Postgres lineage and recompute `source_fact_set_hash` deterministically.
  - [ ] When retrieval includes a community summary, label it `derived` and never present it as authoritative evidence. Acceptance: an integration test asserts the derived label and that community summaries are excluded from authoritative-fact results.
- [ ] Dedicated FalkorDB community integration test. Verified gap: `tests/integration/test_falkordb.py` exists but no committed test exercises `build_communities` on FalkorDB end to end. Acceptance: a test builds communities on FalkorDB and asserts a non-empty, lineage-tagged result.

## Mandatory end-to-end acceptance suite

- [ ] E2E: connector → chunk → extract → reconcile → outbox → projection → retrieval → MCP in `fabric` mode, asserting verbatim chunk-level citations (joined Evidence → Chunk) in the returned pack.
- [ ] E2E: same-source `EKS→ECS` across two versions leaves ECS active, EKS retracted, and the incremental graph projection contains ECS and not EKS; also holds under out-of-order and replay.
- [ ] E2E: hybrid retrieval returns an FTS-only chunk and a vector-only chunk fused in one ranked list.
- [ ] E2E: a snapshot excludes a fact not valid at `as_of_valid_time` and an artifact ingested after `frozen_at_system_time`.
- [ ] E2E: Confluence resume after a simulated mid-space crash yields no duplicate or missing facts; a deleted page retracts its facts.
- [ ] E2E: community summaries are returned labeled `derived` with queryable lineage, never as authoritative evidence.

## Definition of Done

- [ ] All P0, P1, and P2 tasks in this EPIC complete with passing tests.
- [ ] The mandatory E2E acceptance suite passes in CI, with pgvector, Neo4j, and FalkorDB coverage actually executing (not skipped), proven by non-zero test counts per backend in the CI run.
- [ ] `make check` (ruff, `ruff format --check`, pyright strict, import-linter, unit) and the integration suite are green.
- [ ] `docs/remaining-risks.md` updated; no closed item remains listed as open.
- [ ] The separate production-operations EPIC (see Non-goals) is filed and linked as the follow-on; this EPIC does not claim full production readiness on its own.

## Recommended implementation order

Provenance → Deterministic reconciliation → Authoritative write mode → Projection cleanup/replay → Hybrid retrieval + live embeddings → Bitemporal snapshots + MCP contract → Confluence/ontology/community hardening → Full E2E.

## Child issues (to be split from this EPIC)

Dependency order: Provenance → Reconciliation → Authoritative write → Projection cleanup → Hybrid retrieval → Snapshot + MCP → Full E2E.

- [ ] Exact provenance and extraction lineage (P0)
- [ ] Deterministic source-version reconciliation (P0)
- [ ] Authoritative fabric write mode (P0)
- [ ] Incremental projection deletion and replay (P0)
- [ ] Hybrid retrieval and live embeddings (P1)
- [ ] Bitemporal reproducible snapshots (P1)
- [ ] MCP contract for coding agents (P1)
- [ ] Confluence resilience and tombstones (P2)
- [ ] Ontology governance (P2)
- [ ] Community derivation lineage (P2)
- [ ] Mandatory E2E acceptance suite

## Non-goals

- Saga construction and governance.
- Replacing Graphiti or the graph backend.
- Multi-cloud managed services.
- **Full production operations, tracked in a separate dependent EPIC**: load/SLO tests, tenant-isolation security tests, MCP authorization, data-poisoning/prompt-injection defenses, backup/restore, retention/deletion, observability and incident recovery, and a production-scale performance benchmark.

## Evidence from current HEAD

Reviewed commit: `1bb70a6b38184cc766069e189440ee5e7616819b` (branch `main`, `KKloudTarus/vera`).

**Quality gates — run locally (not a CI run), read-only, at HEAD `1bb70a6`:**

```text
Commit:   1bb70a6b38184cc766069e189440ee5e7616819b
Env:      conda env `vera` (repo uses conda + Makefile, not uv)
ruff check src tests            -> passed
ruff format --check src tests   -> 273 files already formatted
pyright                         -> 0 errors, 0 warnings
lint-imports                    -> Contracts: 2 kept, 0 broken
pytest -m "not integration and not llm"  -> 191 passed, 116 deselected (2.61s)
pytest -m "integration and not llm"      -> 113 passed, 194 deselected, 0 skipped (37.96s)
Local integration services: pgvector/pgvector:pg18, neo4j:5.26, falkordb:latest
```

Caveat: these are LOCAL runs, so there is no CI workflow-run URL. Locally pgvector, Neo4j, and FalkorDB tests executed (0 skipped) because the local Postgres is the pgvector image. **In CI they do not: `.github/workflows/ci.yml:43` uses `postgres:18`, so `tests/integration/test_pgvector_retrieval.py` skips silently.** Making CI prove pgvector/Neo4j/FalkorDB execution is a P1 task above.

**Source evidence:**

- Provenance excerpt: `src/vera/entrypoints/worker/lane_pool.py:266`; Evidence model `src/vera/domain/knowledge/fabric.py:230-234`; reconcile `src/vera/application/curation/reconciliation.py:360-367`.
- Same-source supersession ordering: `src/vera/application/curation/reconciliation.py:209-235` and `:296-320`.
- Write order / fabric flag: `src/vera/entrypoints/worker/lane_pool.py:181-185`; `src/vera/config/settings.py:235`.
- Stale deletion: `src/vera/application/projection/service.py:23-47`; `src/vera/adapters/graph/fact_projection.py:38-108`.

items.title: Trinity: Canonical Evidence Model with content hash deduplication
items.body:
## Objective
Implement the `EvidenceUnit` canonical input contract as defined in the Trinity formal production definition §7.

## Unified Context
The current system ingests raw evidence with no canonicalization, no exact-hash deduplication, and no structured provenance. This causes duplicate evidence units to enter the pipeline independently, generating redundant candidates that pollute the candidate pool and waste AI compute.

## Problem
Without a canonical evidence model:
- The same web article can be ingested multiple times as separate sources, generating duplicate knowledge candidates
- There is no content hash to detect exact duplicates before they enter the Generator
- Evidence cannot carry structured `topicHints`, `freshnessWindow`, or `provenance` — so the Generator has no policy context for recall optimization
- Evidence deduplication cannot happen at the boundary, forcing maintenance to clean up downstream artifacts

## Goal
Make the evidence layer the authoritative, deduplicated, tenant-bound entry point for all generation. Every evidence unit that enters the Generator must be canonical, unique by content hash, and traceable to origin.

## In Scope
- `EvidenceUnit` schema: `evidenceId`, `companyId`, `sourceType`, `sourceRef`, `contentRaw`, `contentCanonical`, `contentHash`, `metadata`, `topicHints[]`, `createdAt`, `updatedAt`, `freshnessWindow`, `provenance`
- Exact-hash deduplication at ingress (reject if `contentHash` already exists for the same `companyId`)
- Canonicalization function: lowercase, normalize whitespace, strip decorative markup
- Support for both single and grouped evidence processing

## Out of Scope
- Semantic deduplication of evidence (handled in Refiner)
- Embedding or vector indexing of evidence
- Source ranking or scoring

## Execution Prompt
The evidence layer is the contract boundary. If it is sloppy, every downstream stage inherits that sloppiness. Canonicalization and hash deduplication are not optional polish — they are correctness requirements.

## Constraints
- Every evidence unit MUST be tenant-bound (`companyId` required)
- Exact duplicate evidence (same `contentHash`, same `companyId`) MUST be rejected silently, not errored
- Provenance MUST be preserved from ingestion through to candidate output

## Acceptance Checks
- [ ] `EvidenceUnit` schema is implemented with all required fields
- [ ] Ingesting the same content twice results in exactly one stored evidence unit
- [ ] `contentCanonical` field is populated by a deterministic normalization function
- [ ] Evidence units carry `topicHints[]` consumable by the Generator
- [ ] Grouped evidence processing (multiple units in one batch) is supported

## Dependencies
- None (this is a foundation milestone)

## Risks
- Without this, all downstream stages operate on non-canonical input, making cache hits, deduplication, and reliable provenance impossible.

## Delivery Artifact
`EvidenceUnit` schema, ingestion endpoint with hash dedup, and canonicalization utility.

items.title: [E/C] Migrate capacity and dispatch to dstack and Hatchet with Grafana Cloud
items.body:
## Outcome
Replace new-path capacity provisioning with dstack and dispatch with Hatchet while retaining the existing business job/attempt/asset/budget authority and the approved creator API. Use the existing Grafana Cloud stack for telemetry storage.

User authorization: implement the reviewed migration plan, configure existing Grafana Cloud, make routine decisions autonomously and record blockers. This is not a reset of accepted work or historical costs. Original no-paid wording is historical. The latest user-authorized bounded batch covers one normal cold Vast REF run and one original Agent REF job, with max_price and existing capped budgets, plus the explicitly approved small compatibility PR/release. It does not authorize extra rentals/generations, budget resets/increases, stopping unrelated user machines or destructive migration.

## Acceptance and sequence
- [ ] P0: pinned reusable runtime and Cloud telemetry; stage start/end and bounded safe exports, versioned dashboard; no self-hosted long-term telemetry database.
  - [x] Native runtime pinned and locally built; dependency, FFmpeg and decoder CPU checks.
  - [x] Existing Cloud configured; actual Loki, Mimir and Tempo readback; safe bounded SDK exports and versioned dashboard.
  - [x] Publish the immutable native image; exact pinned digest was independently read back and used for real owned FL/REF runs.
  - [ ] Complete actual image/weights/model/mode-switch stage telemetry and labels. Cold REF download/setup and real output are observed, but the full stage/Cloud criterion remains partial.
- [x] P1: Hatchet outbox bridge with immutable route, atomic exact-job claim, duplicate dispatch protection and unknown-submission reconciliation; offline failure proof including concurrency and collection recovery.
  - [x] Original-ledger route, exact claim/fences, worker affinity, owner fairness/FIFO aging and identity-only wakeups; historical legacy identities/scalar recovery preserved.
  - [x] Offline and isolated PostgreSQL concurrency, cancellation, unknown response and collection recovery; final complete CI passed.
  - [x] Authenticated short CPU broker proof: one original attempt, one submit and one fetch despite response loss and recovery; matching successful Cloud records.
  - [x] Final-runtime >10-minute original business lifecycle/recovery proof passed: 635.189 seconds, 21 recovery events, one original attempt/submit/fetch, validated video and independent audio, older planned work retained. Short yielding callbacks use the actual 30-second cadence; this is CPU simulation, not a continuously running ten-minute callback or GPU inference. Exact tested source 24270819 has the merged main tree; matching actual Loki/Tempo/Mimir completion was independently read back.
- [ ] P2: dstack Vast/RunPod capacity adapter and warm single-GPU runs; distinguish machine running from model ready; owned cleanup and bounded idle/hold policy.
  - [x] Pinned schema and API adapter, original intent/reservation journals, no repeat on unknown results, independent native/broker/admission gates and bounded lifecycle tests.
  - [x] Correct explicitly selected central Vast/RunPod endpoint profiles; authenticated read-only stock/account checks passed before rental. [Verified provider checkpoint](https://github.com/inkseq/h3-studio/issues/132#issuecomment-6104731514). RunPod remains read-only.
  - [ ] Actual owned single-GPU FL/REF warm successive generation, cache/model observations and keep-on qualification remain partial.
  - [x] One normal cold Vast REF startup and one original Agent REF job passed on the released lifecycle-v2 route; original job/attempt preserved.
  - [x] Automatic idle600 shutdown passed: exact dstack run terminated, node stopped, and all four complete authenticated provider account lists empty at13:55UTC. Historical intent/billing retained without a new reconciler. Infinite keep-on remains unverified live.
- [ ] P3: reviewed CPU deployment and creator API proof returning validated video and independent audio, with original job/attempt/receipt identity preserved.
  - [x] Independently reviewed private CPU overlay, supervisor/bootstrap journals and authenticated real local dstack startup; [CPU proof](https://github.com/inkseq/h3-studio/issues/132#issuecomment-6099645148).
  - [x] Exact immutable image publication and protected integrated CPU rollout; backend5b822 and frontend5e78 actual release receipts passed.
  - [ ] Measured host memory/OOM envelope. Configured aggregate memory caps and healthy service readback are not an RSS measurement.
  - [x] Real Quick Chat FL job2587f7d1 and original Agent REF job1a447d6c delivered validated video and independent audio on the new path, preserving original ownership/history/accounting. Native frame counts, artifact hashes and full decoding passed; artistic/reference fidelity and subjective audio quality are unverified.
- [ ] P4: simple operator groups/lists/start/stop/hold with truthful readiness, estimated vs actual cost and compatible generation availability.
  - [x] User-approved P4 redesign and all eight final refinements implemented, locally accepted, released at `965a9883e7f234d53cd102c6d60426acbedb425d`, and authenticated live readback verified. Actionable groups, independent multi-start commands, queue/last-machine warning, lifecycle/retained costs, Ungrouped, responsive keep-on, history/today metrics and explicit all-account admin workspace; actual Grafana historical sample160.3293335s. [Per-criterion release handoff](https://github.com/inkseq/h3-studio/issues/132#issuecomment-6117843259). No new paid GPU matrix.
  - [x] Original-ledger cookie/CSRF-authorized APIs and unknown-result/idempotency checks; canonical lists/details UI merged and source snapshot verified.
  - [ ] Full provider lifecycle/browser acceptance remains partial; normal Vast cold start, one original REF generation and automatic idle-stop passed. Broader providers and keep-on qualification remain open.  - [ ] Provisioned RunPod cache proof; no RunPod rental authorized in this bounded batch.
  - [ ] Actual paid lease-extension contract/provider proof remains #125. Released opt-in v2 uses idle/finite/until-manual-stop policies without a fixed hard deadline, funding continuing runway from original capped accounts. Original v1 finite deadlines remain unchanged; the approved P4 console UX is released and read back; broader real lifecycle qualification and legacy physical extension acceptance remain open.
- [ ] P5: retire replaced legacy responsibilities only after >=14 stable days, all legacy tasks recovered and billing obligations resolved; record this deferred gate rather than declaring it complete now.

## Source, evidence and release
- [Final verified source / long CPU / Cloud handoff and next scope](https://github.com/inkseq/h3-studio/issues/132#issuecomment-6100207583). P1 is accepted at its defined offline/CPU scope; composite P0/P2/P3/P4 and deferred P5 remain open.
- Backend [PR #133](https://github.com/inkseq/h3-studio/pull/133), merged `f93b67c0edc616360e19561c65871c8e3b6e49d2`; exact PR head `24270819a957795aeb545a28137cb5a425c10f5c` has the same tree. Complete [PR CI](https://github.com/inkseq/h3-studio/actions/runs/38069916324) and automatic [main CI](https://github.com/inkseq/h3-studio/actions/runs/38070294372) passed. Canonical frontend [PR #18](https://github.com/inkseq/sixnine-design/pull/18), merge `4ae57d083e51cb54cb9f4c8f74a4ef40fa4c3b7a`, passed its source CI.

Root additionally read Tempo trace `43fba578d6f6757c24a151436128a7a3` (32.87 seconds) and Mimir end-to-end count 1 with exact fixture `service_version=2efeeb2184e5eff64f84080d339968f10d54b829`. A single CPU simulation does not establish GPU performance statistics.
- Final long job `f9f450a1-d9a4-4fe7-a2e0-3d908d314e8e`, attempt `73b28232-6d33-43dc-bd49-94f1d1f3874a`, terminal broker run `b16360a1-a7bd-444e-a8c7-f662fc7368f6` completed. Root read actual Tempo trace `095e23a9e4ed365cc6b2ec9e6d7c0edf` (638.414689-second durable create-to-commit interval) and Mimir count 1 with exact final `service_version=24270819a957795aeb545a28137cb5a425c10f5c`, matching successful original-job Loki events. Different caller/Cloud start boundaries are documented, not treated as a timing contradiction.
- Release: **Released at 5b822ffb526a94aac6ca1aefa96959b7050499e8** through PR #141; required main CI38139755064 and exact approved host release passed. [Current release, manual marks and bounded cold-REF scope](https://github.com/inkseq/h3-studio/issues/132#issuecomment-6109284556). Both legacy ghosts are manually reviewed and cleared from current/pending; historic identities and money remain. Website FL real video/independent audio delivery retains its prior pass. Normal cold REF and original Agent video/independent audio delivery passed; static frontend #142 is actually released at5e78db55d794f326b23a24c5e6f338b46b3f27b9, while backend/controller remain5b822. Composite P0/P2/P3/P4 and deferred P5 stay open. See the latest bounded acceptance handoff for exact IDs, validation, shutdown and cost evidence.

## Safety and compatibility
Existing queue/control recovery responsibilities remain until P5. Hatchet is at-least-once and never authorizes blindly retrying GPU inference. Resource recommendations use actual model support and resource floors; historical joint_cases and #130 timings are not parameter whitelists. Initially one GPU per run; larger allocations need independently registered physical slots and qualification. Old accepted jobs retain their original route. Original billing obligations, budgets and deadlines remain untouched.

## Scope ownership
[agent:Codex] Unclaimed after verified bounded handoff. PR #141/#142 are released, both legacy marks verified, and exactly one normal cold Vast REF plus original Agent REF video/audio delivery and automatic idle-stop passed. All four supplier account lists contain zero GPUs at13:55UTC. No new subtasks or P4 coding. Next implementation awaits user review of the P4 sketch; read the latest comment and Project before claiming another scope. The user stopped the standalone physical-removal-reconciler approach; no such prerequisite remains. Prior released implementation claims are history, not current ownership. Original migration worktree/branch remain preserved as history; latest bounded source worktrees are linked in the final handoff. Shared feature checkouts and unrelated PRs #118/#64/#23 remain preserved. Only this batch's CPU test helpers/engines are stopped; original evidence volumes remain.

Completed prerequisites: immutable native publication, explicit central Vast/RunPod read-only validation and protected host/static releases. Next implementation gate: user review of the P4 sketch; wider telemetry, warm/keep-on qualification and >=14-day stability remain separately open. Do not start extra paid work from old authorization or the Project status. Do not infer paid authorization from a board status. Evidence/obligations: #129 ffmpeg, #130 hardware qualification, #120 eligibility, #125 console/extension and #28 historical billing. English plan `DSTACK-MIGRATION.md`, DEC-013 and the generation contract are the next-session entry points.
